3	Established 2026-06-29 (kickoff), first-session build 2026-07-01. Lives on the non-sync drive at `C:\Claude (not on Gdrive, nor OneDrive)\ppqviewer\`. Owned by no subject; tracked as an estate shared asset in `EdTech Overview\SHARED_ASSETS.md` ("ppqviewer" / "Question Tools engine").

5	## What it is
6	
7	One shared engine that displays authentic past-paper-question images, lets a pupil self-mark on a 1-to-6 scale, and shows a per-skill dashboard (a last-N tick/cross ribbon plus a 1-to-6 rating heat map, shared colour ramp and intensity formula), with a drawing overlay and an image modal. Every subject runs the SAME engine and supplies only its own config and question data. A universal improvement is made once here and is live for every subject the next time their page opens.
8	
9	## Why it exists
10	
11	Chemistry and ESAT each grew their own copy of the same viewer, and the copies drifted. The concrete proof is the prefetch drift: a "longer pre-fetch" improvement (`PREFETCH_AHEAD = 3` with sibling-part warming) landed in the live chemistry copy alone and reached neither the ESAT sibling (one-step preload only) nor the stale G: chemistry mirror. The single-shared-engine model exists to stop exactly this: propagate universal gains automatically, and make each subject aware of the optional capabilities it is not using.
12	
13	## The model (three layers plus data)
14	
15	- **Engine (shared, here):** all logic. Filter / order / shuffle / start-number, navigation, the 1-to-6 self-mark, the dashboard, parametrised prefetch, the drawing overlay, the modal, the keyboard map, question loading.
16	- **Config (per subject):** a required and UNIQUE namespaced storage key, field and label names, the grouping function, prefetch depth, and which optional modules are switched on.
17	- **Optional modules (opt-in, built here):** reference-booklet deep-link, structured multi-part navigator, question-type plugins (auto-marked MCQ, image self-mark, reveal-markscheme flashcard, examiner-report panel), KaTeX math rendering, post-question "where did you go wrong" interrogation.
18	- **Data (per subject):** the question catalogue and the asset folders only.
19	
20	Subjects never edit the engine. A new need is either a new shared capability (made here) or a new opt-in module (made here, switched on in that subject's config). Never a fork.
21	
22	## Consumers
23	
24	See `REGISTRY.md` for the live table. In brief: Chemistry (live) and ESAT (live) are the two real copies to fold in; Special Relativity is a possible future migration target (it currently runs a different engine family, not this one); Economics and Maths are possible future consumers with no copy yet.
25	
26	## Change and notification
27	
28	Universal changes are made once here and notified into each consumer's inbox, with `CHANGELOG.md` as the record. Subject-specific modules are logged in `REGISTRY.md` so every other subject can see the capability exists and is simply switched off for them. Change-requests arrive in `inbox\`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_from-<subject>_<topic>.md`, tagged UNIVERSAL or SUBJECT-SPECIFIC on the first line.

1	# DECISIONS: ppqviewer
2	
3	Numbered, newest reasoning appended. Cite as "d001 (ESAT-spine seed)", never bare "d001".

6	
7	## d001 (ESAT-spine seed): seed the shared engine's spine from ESAT, port chemistry's richer features on as opt-in modules
8	
9	**Decision.** Agree with the seat recommendation. The canonical engine's SPINE (storage model, config indirection, filtering/navigation skeleton) is seeded from ESAT's `engine.js`. Chemistry's richer FEATURES (multi-part navigator, data-booklet deep-link, dual MCQ/flashcard/examiner-report modes, KaTeX, the longer prefetch with sibling-part warming) are ported on as opt-in modules. Hard rule: the combined engine must do everything chemistry's does and everything ESAT's does.
10	
11	**Reasons, from reading both engines in full (not taken on trust):**
12	
13	1. **Storage model is the deciding factor.** ESAT stores a flat attempts log (`recordAttempt`: one row per answer with chosen option, correctness, `time_ms`, `timing_mode`, `self_report` reserved, `ts`, `app_version`, `context`) and derives the dashboard from it. Chemistry stores only the final state: a `scores` map (id to 1-6) and an `mcqResults` map (id to boolean), no attempt history and no timing. An attempts log is a superset: the score-only view can be derived from it, but not the reverse. Retrofitting an attempts log into chemistry's `saveState` is more invasive than porting chemistry's view features onto ESAT's spine.
14	
15	2. **ESAT is already config-driven** (`window.ESAT_CONFIG`: title, versionLabel, appVersion, storageKey, learnerId, timingMode, subjectLabels, specLabels). Chemistry hard-codes its equivalents in the engine and in `ppqs.js`. The config-driven shape is exactly what the shared model needs, so ESAT is closer to the target.
16	
17	3. **Silent timing capture** (`time_ms`, `timing_mode`) already exists in ESAT with the UI gated for later. This is a real analytics gain chemistry lacks, and it is on the spine.
18	
19	**Census correction (material, found this session).** The 2026-06-29 divergence census argued for the ESAT spine partly on the grounds that chemistry still used a bare `ppq_scores` / `ppq_mcq` storage key while ESAT alone namespaced. That is now out of date: the live `C:\Claude...\chemistrydriller\ppq.js` (dated 29 Jun 03:42) has ALREADY adopted namespaced keys (`chemistrydriller_ppq_v1_scores` / `_mcq`, its own d005 fix). So both copies now namespace, and that particular argument no longer separates them. The conclusion is unchanged because reason 1 (attempts-log vs score-map) is the deeper structural difference and stands on its own. Recorded so the reasoning is honest rather than inherited.
20	
21	**Cost this decision accepts (tracked in ROADMAP).** Chemistry's features are non-trivial to port: the multi-part block detection and whole-question navigator (`getQuestionBlockKey` / `getQuestionBlockParts` / `goToQuestionId` / part-chips / `wq-part` stack), the 24-entry data-booklet deep-link with the in-text "Section N" / "periodic table" scanner, the dual MCQ-vs-flashcard rendering with examiner reports, and KaTeX + mhchem. None may be lost.
22	
23	**Fork-vs-stale verification (2026-07-01, Smith asked).** Read the full G: chemistry `ppq.js` (736 lines) against the live copy (826 lines), not just the head. The G: copy is stale, not a fork: every capability it has is present in the live copy, mostly enhanced (namespaced storage, part-navigator, `goToQuestionId`, deeper prefetch, KaTeX cold-cache safety net). No divergent development. ONE micro-heuristic in G: was NOT carried into the live copy and must be folded into the shared structuredPaper module rather than lost: in its "Show Full Question Pages" view, G: peeks at the previous question in the catalogue and, if it shares the same paper code, prepends that previous page image (a workaround for a stem that began at the foot of the earlier printed page). Tracked as a structuredPaper requirement (DESIGN §4).

27	## d002 (namespaced storage mandatory): all storage keys off a required config namespace
28	
29	The engine keys every localStorage read/write off `CONFIG.storageKey`, which is required and must be unique per consumer. No bare `ppq_scores`. This is the fix for the original collision (chemistry's bare key clashing with the Pre-IB Topic 7 key). Both live copies already comply; the shared engine enforces it (fail loud if `storageKey` is absent).
30	
31	---
32	
33	## d003 (canonical DOM contract): the engine renders its own question DOM into one mount point
34	
35	Reading both HTML shells showed they use DIFFERENT element IDs and structures for the same parts (chemistry: `mcq-options`, `comp-widget`, `answer-panel`, `ms-text`, `q-text`, a three-column syllabus layout with `lhs-content` / `rhs-content`; ESAT: `options-grid`, `competence`, `answer-line`, `crop-stack`, `dash-content`, a single dashboard). If the shared engine simply "expects IDs", every consumer's HTML has to converge on one hidden contract, which is a fresh source of drift.
36	
37	**Decision.** The shared engine owns its DOM: each consumer page supplies one mount element (plus the standard `<head>` assets and the GA/Clarity blocks), and the engine builds the card, controls, competence widget, dashboard and modal inside it. Config chooses dashboard shape (single-column grouped, or a two-column split like chemistry's 1B / S+R). This keeps "subjects supply only config + data" true at the HTML level too, not just the JS level. It is a larger up-front rewrite than an ID-matching approach, recorded as an open trade in `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` (q02) in case Smith prefers the lighter ID-contract route.
38	
39	**CONFIRMED 2026-07-01: Smith chose Option A (engine builds the furniture).** q02 resolved. The engine draws all furniture into one `#ppq-root` mount; consumers ship only config + data. This is the Phase 2 build shape.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## d004 (dashboard is one configurable component): group function from config, untagged bucket last
44	
45	One `renderDashboard`, shared. The last-N ribbon, the 1-to-6 heat map, the colour ramp `{1:'229,62,62',2:'221,107,32',3:'214,158,46',4:'72,187,120',5:'56,161,105',6:'47,133,90'}` and the intensity formula `0.2 + 0.8 * count / max` are already verbatim-identical across both copies, so they become the shared default. Grouping (`groupKey` / `groupLabel`) and the "untagged last" sort come from config. Chemistry's syllabus-specific two-column split (driven by `category_code` prefixes and paper `1B`) is expressed as a dashboard-layout config option, not baked into the core.
46	
47	---
48	
49	## d005 (prefetch is one parametrised function): depth from config
50	
51	The prefetch becomes a single shared function with the lookahead count exposed as `CONFIG.prefetchAhead` (default 3), warming the visible crop, the full-page stem, the markscheme page, and, when the structured-paper module is on, the sibling-part crops. Retained-image cap stays bounded (80). Today's prefetch change would then be a one-line default edit inherited by everyone, which is the whole point.
52	
53	**Smith confirmation (2026-07-01):** yes, prefetch several questions ahead, and warm the ANSWER / markscheme image as its own separate fetch (not only the question crop), so revealing the answer is instant too. This is already how the live chemistry prefetch behaves (`answer_url` warmed alongside the stem); keep it, and keep the depth in config.
54	
55	---
56	
57	## d006 (self-report is pluggable, not a hardcoded 1-to-6): the rating scheme is defined in config, not baked into the core
58	
59	**Decision.** The 1-to-6 self-mark is the shared DEFAULT, but the core must not assume it is universal or permanent. Smith (2026-07-01): all consumers use 1-to-6 today, but "the self-report might develop in different ways with different things." So the self-report scheme (number of levels, labels, colour ramp, and whether it is a rating at all versus, say, a confidence tag or a free response) is defined in `CONFIG.selfReport` and the storage + dashboard read the scheme from there. The heat-map colour ramp and the attempt row's `self_report` field are driven by the scheme definition, not by a fixed 1..6 literal. Nothing changes for the current consumers; the core just stops hard-coding the scale.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## d007 (help / assistance layer with visibility scopes): a pupil can ask for help on a question, a teacher records an answer, and the answer has a visibility scope
64	
65	**Decision (new capability, future phase).** Smith wants, on a question, the pupil to be able to ask for assistance and write a free response, and for the teacher to record an answer against it. The recorded answer carries a VISIBILITY SCOPE, one of: direct to that pupil, visible to that pupil's class, or visible to all users. This is an opt-in shared module (`assistance`), built once here, not per subject. It writes to a store that is separate from the local attempts log because it crosses users (a teacher answer seen by a class is not local-only state). It implies the identity/classes layer in d008. Recorded now so the spine is not designed in a way that blocks it; built in a later phase (ROADMAP). See OPEN_QUESTIONS q06 for the cross-consumer analytics-visibility question that rides alongside it.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## d008 (identity and classes, for all logins): real logins with class membership, needed by the assistance layer and beyond
70	
71	**Decision (future, dependency of d007).** Smith: logins are "something we should do for all logins", and on login the teacher can assign users to classes. So the shared model gains an identity layer: a real login (not the current `learnerId: "local"` placeholder) and a class membership per user, so a teacher answer can be scoped to a class. This is the FastAPI + Google-OAuth backend tier the estate web kit already points at (the Memoriser pattern). `learnerId` stays out of the question/analysis stores as raw identity; the login maps to it. Big, later, but recorded as the substrate the assistance layer needs. Do not bake a two-value-only or syllabus-only assumption anywhere that would block it (Smith's "don't block innovation").
72	
73	---
74	
75	## d010 (chemistry migration details): unified v2 store with seed-from-v1, and the split preserved as two labelled columns
76	
77	**Storage.** Chemistry moves to a single unified key `chemistrydriller_ppq_v2` holding `{attempts, scores}` (the shared shape). A `migrate` config hook seeds it once from the old `chemistrydriller_ppq_v1_scores` / `_mcq` keys, so pupils keep their self-ratings and their MCQ history (old booleans become minimal attempt rows). Confirmed by test.
78	
79	**Question types.** Paper 1A renders as auto-marked `mcq` (synthetic A-D option text from `choices`, marked against `answer_key`, examiner-report panel); papers 1B and 2 render as reveal-markscheme `flashcard` (formatted markscheme text, optional full-page markscheme spoiler, examiner-report). Graded types (mcq, imageSelfMark) write attempt rows; flashcard records only the self-rating, matching the donor.
80	
81	**Split dashboard (q05 preserved).** Chemistry's two-column syllabus split is expressed as `dashboardColumns` and rendered as two labelled columns ("Paper 1B Mastery" with rating boxes, "Syllabus Overview" with tick/cross ribbon + rating heat map) inside the dashboard panel. The split CONTENT is preserved faithfully; its exact left-and-right-of-centre placement from the old three-column page is a later cosmetic option (this is the "or move the join point back" half of Smith's q05 note, deferred as non-essential).
82	
83	---
84	
85	## d009 (embeddable as a bolt-on component, not only a standalone page): the viewer must run inside a larger app
86	
87	**Decision.** Smith (2026-07-01) on Special Relativity: it IS a consumer and wants to use this soon, but "it's only a part" of the app, "a thing to be bolted onto". So the viewer is not always the whole page; it must run as a component mounted inside a larger host app (the circuit-builder-embed pattern from ECM). This fits d003 (engine-owns-DOM into one `#ppq-root` mount): the same mount-point design serves both a standalone page and an embed. Requirement: no reliance on owning `<body>`, the header, or global singletons that would clash with a host; everything scoped to the mount and namespaced. SR is the first embed consumer, near-term.
88	
```

4	For: the ppqviewer chat (the chat that builds and owns the shared engine in this folder)
5	Date: 2026-06-29
6	Canonical copy also at `EdTech Overview\dispatch_packets\ppqviewer_kickoff_packet.md`.
7	
8	You own `ppqviewer`, the estate's shared past-paper-question viewer engine, living here at `C:\Claude (not on Gdrive, nor OneDrive)\ppqviewer\`. It is owned by no subject. Chemistry and ESAT already run their own copies; your job is to make one engine they all share. This is a brief, not a rulebook: where you have good reason to depart, do, and record the reason in DECISIONS.
9	
10	## The decision Smith has made: a single shared engine
11	
12	All subjects run the SAME engine, not copies. The engine lives here; each subject supplies only its own config and its own question data and loads the one engine. A universal improvement is therefore made once, here, and is live for every subject the next time their page opens. This is deliberate: the divergence census found a "longer pre-fetch" improvement trapped in the chemistry copy alone, and the single-shared-engine model exists to stop exactly that.
13	
14	- **Engine (shared, yours):** all the logic. Filter / order / shuffle, the 1-to-6 self-mark, the dashboard (last-rating ribbon plus rating-distribution heat map, shared colour ramp and intensity formula), parametrised pre-fetch, the drawing overlay, the modal, the keyboard map, the question-loading and multi-part handling.
15	- **Config (per subject):** a required and UNIQUE storage key (namespaced, e.g. `chem_ppq_v1`, `esat_ppq_v1`; chemistry's current bare `ppq_scores` is a collision bug to fix), field and label names, grouping function, `PREFETCH_AHEAD`, and which optional modules are switched on.
16	- **Data (per subject):** the question catalogue and the asset folders only.
17	- **Subjects never edit the engine.** If a subject needs new behaviour, it is either a new shared capability (made here) or a new optional module (made here, switched on in that subject's config). Never a fork.
18	
19	## Your first job: consolidate the two real copies, with a longer think
20	
21	The divergence census (`ppqviewer_divergence_census.md`, in this folder) is your evidence base. It found only two genuine copies: the live chemistry engine (`C:\Claude (not on Gdrive, nor OneDrive)\chemistrydriller\ppq.js` + `ppq.html`; the `G:` chemistry copy is a stale mirror to retire) and ESAT (`C:\Claude (not on Gdrive, nor OneDrive)\ESAT Prep App\app\engine.js`).
22	
23	The seat's recommendation, passed on as INPUT you are free to disagree with: seed the SPINE from ESAT (it is the cleaner rewrite, with mandatory namespaced storage and a flat attempts-log from which the dashboard is derived), and port chemistry's richer FEATURES onto it as opt-in modules (data-booklet deep-link, multi-part whole-question navigator, the MCQ / flashcard / examiner-report question types, KaTeX). Smith's explicit instruction is that YOU decide this with a proper, longer look at both live copies rather than taking the recommendation on trust. Read both engines in full, weigh them yourself, and record your seed decision and reasons in DECISIONS. The one hard rule: lose no capability that either copy already has. The combined engine must do everything chemistry's does and everything ESAT's does.
24	
25	## Optional modules to carry
26	
27	- **Chemistry's data-booklet deep-link** (jump to the relevant page of the data booklet from a question).
28	- **Post-question "where did you go wrong" interrogation.** ESAT wants this heavily; Smith expects economics, maths and others to want it too, so build it ONCE as a shared optional mode, not an ESAT-only feature. It is the estate's lost-marks idea (record what was got wrong) applied at the viewing layer, so bind its categories to `misconceptions_core.yaml` (the ratified spine at the IB Physics Overview root) rather than inventing a private vocabulary.
29	- Any other per-copy feature the census surfaces. When in doubt, make it a module rather than baking it into the shared core.
30	
31	## Change, notification and "what you are not getting" (Smith's requirement)
32	
33	All consumers are on the same engine AND must be kept aware of changes:
34	
35	- **Universal changes:** made once here, and you NOTIFY every consumer. Keep a `CHANGELOG.md` in this folder, and on a universal change drop a short note into each consumer's inbox so a subject author is never surprised by behaviour they did not ask for.
36	- **Subject-specific modules:** when a module is added for one subject, record it in the REGISTRY so every OTHER subject can SEE the capability exists and is simply switched off for them, and can opt in if they want it. Smith's words: subjects "should be aware of what they're not getting." The registry is that awareness surface.
37	- **REGISTRY.md** (create it): one row per consumer with engine version, copy/location, storage key, and which optional modules are enabled. This is both the drift detector and the what-each-subject-has map.
38	
39	## Routing: how a subject asks for a change
40	
41	A subject that wants a change has its own chat drop a note into `ppqviewer\inbox\`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_from-<subject>_<topic>.md`, tagged UNIVERSAL or SUBJECT-SPECIFIC on the first line. You read the inbox, make universal changes in the shared engine, and treat subject-specific ones as config or a new opt-in module. The EdTech Overview seat will tell each current consumer chat that this inbox is the channel, so requests actually arrive here rather than landing in whichever subject Smith happens to be in (which is how the pre-fetch drift happened).

It currently runs a different engine family, so treat it as a migration target, not a current copy. Coordinate the migration via the IB Physics Overview seat when it is ready.

383	## Review Workflow
384	
385	Open the generated review page in a browser:
386	
387	```text
388	outputs/review/trilogy_2024_p1h/index.html
389	```
390	
391	It shows each question part with its shared stem, extracted question text, aligned mark scheme answer, examiner-report comments, AO/spec references, extracted figures, visual crops, and links to the rendered question-paper, mark-scheme, and examiner-report pages. This is the main human-review surface for checking extraction quality before database import.
392	
393	The examiner-report preview splits comments by printed part labels such as `04.3` and keeps continuation paragraphs and example-response notes with the current part until the next printed label. It also crops the original report region for review, because examiner reports often include example responses, diagrams, or layout-sensitive comments.
394	
395	The mark-scheme preview now also keeps a row-level `mark_points` layer. This is meant to preserve which answer line earns which mark, whether the credit is printed in the right-hand mark column or shown as an inline bracket such as `(1)` in an alternative route. Extra information is aligned to those marking points where the PDF table layout makes that recoverable.
396	
397	The mark-scheme layer also records emphasis in the printed scheme. Bold spans are saved as `bold` emphasis, and detected underlined spans are saved as `underline` emphasis with `required_exact: true`, because underlined mark-scheme wording normally has to be used exactly.
398	
399	The visual crops are important: PDF text extraction can lose mathematical layout such as fraction bars, stacked formulae, and equation spacing. The searchable text is still useful, but the original crop is kept beside it so the reviewed database can preserve the actual printed maths and diagrams.
400	
401	The preview also saves detected maths in structured form where the PDF layout makes this possible. Examples include superscripts such as `P = I^{2} R` and simple stacked fractions such as `P = \frac{W}{t}`. These detected items are a helper layer, not a replacement for the original crop.
402	
403	Question answer spaces are also preserved where they are drawn as horizontal lines in the PDF. The review text inserts markers such as `[answer space: ______]` for inline blanks and labelled fill-in spaces, while long open-response ruled areas remain in the structured answer-space data and visual crops without cluttering the plain question text.
404	
405	Some equations are embedded as images rather than text in the source PDF. For those cases the review workflow can use notation overrides under `data/notation_overrides/`; the first example is the `05.2` nuclear equation in Trilogy 2024 P1H.
406	
407	Greek symbols in the PDF text layer are normalised into LaTeX-style commands inside detected maths, for example `\alpha`, `\beta`, `\theta`, `\lambda`, `\mu`, `\Delta`, and `\Omega`. If a Greek symbol is only present in an image, the visual crop preserves it for review.
408

1	# ESAT Prep App
2	
3	**Vision (one paragraph).** A preparation app for the Cambridge **ESAT** (and its ENGAA/NSAA predecessors and the Oxford **PAT**, used as proxies because no genuine ESAT past papers exist yet). It starts as a past-paper question **viewer** in the shape of the Chemistry Driller's PPQ viewer, drawing from the ~1,000+ already-classified questions in `PaperDatabases\Esat Categorisation`, shown as authentic image crops because the OCR text is not yet reliable. Its distinctive purpose is not syllabus coverage (a revealing strand, but not the main one): it is to **understand multiple-choice performance deeply**. Every question gets exhaustive per-distractor analysis (what specific reasoning leads to each wrong option), all available correct **methods** plus any elimination tricks and speed techniques (ESAT rewards seeing fast, not just solving), a structured **self-report** layer where a learner records exactly what they saw, used, discarded or got stuck on, and **timing** in several modes (none / end-only / per-question / sweep clock / a positive-negative time bank). The app then feeds back on what the learner could have seen or done faster. Authoring new questions comes much later; the near-term work is the viewer plus the analysis layer that hangs off it.

#### Thinking

Now I can see the picture clearly:

1. **Trilogy Physics** has a `reportToShell()` mechanism: the engine calls `M.report(payload)` on every attempt event, and the shell (index.html) adds project/identity/session/topic and POSTs to `REPORT_URL` (the Google Apps Script endpoint). The payload matches the ECM schema: item_id, topic, qtype, mode, level, status, picked_id, misconception_id, extra_json.

2. **ppqviewer** has NO logging/reporting mechanism at all. It stores attempts in localStorage (the flat attempts log), but it doesn't POST anywhere. There's no `report` callback, no `REPORT_URL`, no GA4 event firing on attempts. The self-report ratings (1-6) are written to localStorage only.

3. The **GA4 + Clarity** blocks in the live Chemistry ppq.html are page-level analytics (page views, clicks), not attempt-level logging. They don't record which question was answered or what rating was given.

So Smith is asking: can I wire the ppqviewer comparison pages to POST attempt data (including the 1-6 ratings) to the shared Google Sheet, the same way Trilogy does?

The answer is: the ppqviewer engine doesn't have a report hook yet. I'd need to add one. The cleanest approach would be:
1. Add a `report` callback to the ppqviewer config (like Trilogy's `M.report`)
2. Fire it on every attempt (MCQ answer, self-mark rating)
3. In the comparison HTML pages, wire that callback to POST to the REPORT_URL

But wait - Smith said "I don't know if you can see it. Probably not." He's asking whether I can see the logging infrastructure. I can - I've found the teacher-tracking.gs and the Trilogy report mechanism. He's also noting that the ppqviewer doesn't have this yet ("I see we haven't got that").

#### Thinking

Let me give Smith a clear summary of what I've done.

Done. Here's what's now wired in:

**Engine change (ppqviewer.js, v0.2.1):** The mount now accepts an optional `report` callback. The engine fires it on three events: `session_start` (page load), `answered` (MCQ or image-self-mark, carrying correct/incorrect + time taken), and `rated` (every 1-to-6 self-mark, carrying the rating value). The payload shape matches the estate's `teacher-tracking.gs` schema exactly, so rows land in the same Google Sheet with the same columns Trilogy uses. The engine itself stays transport-agnostic; it just calls the callback.

**Comparison pages (both now have logging):**

When you open either page, you'll see a sign-in gate first (name + class, honour-system, same as Trilogy). Once you're in, every MCQ answer and every 1-to-6 rating POSTs a row to the shared Apps Script endpoint. The rows land in the "Smithics driller responses" Sheet under tabs named `ppqviewer_chemistry` and `ppqviewer_esat` respectively. You'll see a small "sent" flash in the bottom-right corner confirming each POST.

Both pages also carry the GA4 + Clarity blocks (the estate WEB_KIT standard), so page-level analytics are recorded too.

**What you'll see in the Sheet:** For each rating, a row with timestamp, pupil name, cohort, session_id, item_id (the question code like "25N.1A.SL.TZ1.1"), topic (the syllabus code like "S1.1"), qtype ("self_report"), status ("rated"), and extra_json carrying `{"rating": 4}`. For MCQ answers, status is "answered" with picked_id and correct/incorrect in extra_json.

**Edits declared (QoderWork 2026-07-22):**
- `ppqviewer/engine/ppqviewer.js`: added report callback (constructor, _fireReport helper, calls in _recordAttempt + scale-btn handler + init), version bumped to 0.2.1
- `ppqviewer/example/chem-compare.html`: rewritten with GA4, Clarity, sign-in gate, REPORT_URL wiring
- `ppqviewer/example/esat-compare.html`: rewritten with GA4, Clarity, sign-in gate, REPORT_URL wiring
- `ppqviewer/CHANGELOG.md`: new entry for v0.2.1

One note: the Apps Script endpoint needs to be deployed with "Anyone" access for the POST to work from a local file:// page. If it's already deployed that way (which it should be, since Trilogy uses it), the rows will appear. **Layout (`.ppq-layout`):** `display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 300px;` — main card on left (1fr), dashboard on right (300px). `align-items: start`. So the main question card is the left column, the mastery dashboard is the right 300px column.

**Scrolling:** The dashboard `.ppq-dash` has `max-height: calc(100vh - 120px); overflow-y: auto;` — so the mastery DOES scroll independently (matches Smith: "mastery does scroll independently"). But the main card `.ppq-card` has NO max-height/overflow — so the main content just grows the page, and scrolling the page scrolls everything (the whole document scrolls). That's the "main page drags mastery" issue: when the main content is long, you scroll the whole document, and since the dashboard is `align-items: start` with its own max-height, the dashboard stays at top but the page scroll moves the viewport. Actually wait — the dashboard has its own overflow scroll and max-height 100vh-120px, so it's roughly viewport-height. But it's not position:sticky, so when you scroll the document down (to see more of the long main card), the dashboard scrolls away with the document. That's "dragging mastery."

The fix for independent scrolling: make the layout a fixed-height container where BOTH columns scroll independently. The cleanest approach: make `.ppq-layout` fill the viewport height (minus header), and give BOTH the main card and the dashboard their own `overflow-y: auto` with bounded heights. OR make the dashboard `position: sticky; top: ...` so it stays put while the main content scrolls.

That way, scrolling the main page keeps the mastery pinned in the viewport, and the mastery's internal content still scrolls independently within its max-height. This is the least invasive and matches "mastery does scroll independently" (keep that) + "main page shouldn't drag mastery" (pin mastery with sticky).

**Issue 1 — main page drags mastery (scrolling):**
`.ppq-dash` has `max-height: calc(100vh - 120px); overflow-y: auto`. So the dash internal content scrolls. But the dash itself is at the top of the right grid cell (align-items: start). When the main card (`.ppq-centre`) is long and you scroll the browser window down, the whole `.ppq-layout` grid scrolls up, taking the dash with it (it disappears off the top). So scrolling the paper "drags" the mastery out of view.

Fix: make `.ppq-dash` sticky so it stays in the viewport while the centre scrolls. `position: sticky; top: 1rem;`. This keeps mastery visible while you scroll the paper, and the mastery's own internal scroll still works independently. This precisely matches: "mastery does scroll independently" (keep) + "main page shouldn't drag mastery" (sticky pins it).

But wait — for sticky to work, the grid item must be able to stick within its grid area. The right grid area spans the full row height (which equals the tall centre column). The `.ppq-dash` with align-self:start is placed at the top, sized to its content (capped by max-height). With position:sticky + top, as the page scrolls, the dash sticks until the bottom of its grid area passes. Since the grid area is as tall as the centre column, the dash stays stuck for the whole scroll. 

However, there's a subtlety with CSS grid and sticky: a grid item with `align-self: start` has a box that's only as tall as its content. Sticky works within the containing block. For a grid item, the containing block for sticky purposes is the grid area. So sticky should work. Let me add it.

689	    try { window.renderMathInElement(elm, { delimiters: [{ left: "$$", right: "$$", display: true }, { left: "$", right: "$", display: false }, { left: "\\(", right: "\\)", display: false }, { left: "\\[", right: "\\]", display: true }] }); } catch (e) { /* KaTeX not ready */ }
690	  };
691	
692	  // --------------------------------------------------------------- modal
693	  Viewer.prototype.openModal = function (urlOrUrls) {
694	    const urls = Array.isArray(urlOrUrls) ? urlOrUrls : [urlOrUrls];
695	    this.q(".ppq-modal-body").innerHTML = urls.map((u) => (String(u).slice(-4) === ".pdf") ? '<iframe src="' + esc(u) + '" class="ppq-modal-pdf"></iframe>' : '<img src="' + esc(u) + '" class="ppq-modal-img">').join("");
696	    this.q(".ppq-modal").classList.add("show");
697	  };
698	  Viewer.prototype.closeModal = function () { this.q(".ppq-modal").classList.remove("show"); this.q(".ppq-modal-body").innerHTML = ""; };
699	
700	  // --------------------------------------------------------------- keyboard
701	  Viewer.prototype._bindGlobalKeys = function () {
702	    const self = this;
703	    this._keyHandler = function (e) {
704	      if (!self.cur || !self._shouldHandleKey(e)) return;
705	      if (self.q(".ppq-modal").classList.contains("show") && e.key === "Escape") { self.closeModal(); return; }
706	      if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") { self.prev(); return; }
707	      if (e.key === "ArrowRight") { self.next(); return; }
708	      if (e.key === "s" || e.key === "S") { if (!self.answered) self.skip(); return; }
709	      if (e.key === "r" || e.key === "R") { if (!self.answered && (self._curType === "flashcard" || self._curType === "imageSelfMark")) self.reveal(); return; }
710	      if (e.key === "Enter") { if (self.answered) self.next(); else if (self._curType === "flashcard") self.reveal(); return; }
711	      if (!self.answered) {
712	        const L = e.key.toUpperCase(), labels = self._answerLabels || [];
713	        if (labels.indexOf(L) >= 0) { self._pick(L); return; }
714	        const numMap = { "1": "A", "2": "B", "3": "C", "4": "D", "5": "E", "6": "F", "7": "G", "8": "H" };
715	        if (numMap[e.key] && labels.indexOf(numMap[e.key]) >= 0) { self._pick(numMap[e.key]); return; }
716	      } else if (e.key >= "1" && e.key <= String(self.cfg.selfReport.levels)) {
717	        const b = self.q('.ppq-scale-btn[data-val="' + e.key + '"]'); if (b) b.click();
718	      }
719	    };
```

function makeDashPanel(col, cls) {

```js
Viewer.prototype._renderSplit = function () {
  const cfg = this.cfg;
  const panels = this.qa(".ppq-dash-split-panel");
  cfg.dashboardColumns.forEach((col, i) => {
    const panel = panels[i];
    if (!panel) return;
    const content = panel.querySelector(".ppq-dash-content");
    const groups = {};
    this.questions.forEach((q) => { if (!col.includes(q)) return; const k = col.groupKey(q); if (!groups[k]) groups[k] = { label: col.groupLabel(q), total: 0, marks: [], ratings: this._zeroRatings(), seq: [] }; groups[k].total++; });
    this.store.attempts.forEach((a) => { const q = this.byId[a.id]; if (!q || !col.includes(q)) return; const g = groups[col.groupKey(q)]; if (g) g.marks.push(a.correct === true || a.is_correct === "right"); });
    Object.keys(this.store.scores).forEach((id) => { const q = this.byId[id]; if (!q || !col.includes(q)) return; const g = groups[col.groupKey(q)]; if (g) { if (g.ratings[this.store.scores[id]] != null) g.ratings[this.store.scores[id]]++; g.seq.push(this.store.scores[id]); } });
    const keys = Object.keys(groups).sort();
    content.innerHTML = keys.map((k) => this._catHtml(k, groups[k], col.style)).join("");
  });
  this._wireCats();
};
```

```js
  Viewer.prototype._renderSplit = function () {
    const cfg = this.cfg;
    /* QoderWork 2026-07-22: each column renders into its own flanking panel
       (left = column 0, right = column 1) rather than stacking in one sidebar. */
    const panels = this.qa(".ppq-dash-split-panel");
    cfg.dashboardColumns.forEach((col, i) => {
      const panel = panels[i];
      if (!panel) return;
      const content = panel.querySelector(".ppq-dash-content");
      const groups = {};
      this.questions.forEach((q) => { if (!col.includes(q)) return; const k = col.groupKey(q); if (!groups[k]) groups[k] = { label: col.groupLabel(q), total: 0, marks: [], ratings: this._zeroRatings(), seq: [] }; groups[k].total++; });
      this.store.attempts.forEach((a) => { const q = this.byId[a.id]; if (!q || !col.includes(q)) return; const g = groups[col.groupKey(q)]; if (g) g.marks.push(a.correct === true || a.is_correct === "right"); });
      Object.keys(this.store.scores).forEach((id) => { const q = this.byId[id]; if (!q || !col.includes(q)) return; const g = groups[col.groupKey(q)]; if (g) { if (g.ratings[this.store.scores[id]] != null) g.ratings[this.store.scores[id]]++; g.seq.push(this.store.scores[id]); } });
      const keys = Object.keys(groups).sort();
      content.innerHTML = keys.map((k) => this._catHtml(k, groups[k], col.style)).join("");
    });
    this._wireCats();
  };
```

```css
/* QoderWork 2026-07-22: split dashboard = three columns (left mastery, centre
   question, right mastery), matching the original Chemistry viewer. The flanking
   panels inherit position:sticky from .ppq-dash, so scrolling the paper keeps the
   mastery in view while each panel still scrolls its own content independently. */
.ppq-layout-split { grid-template-columns: 280px minmax(0, 1fr) 280px; }
.ppq-layout-split .ppq-centre { min-width: 0; }
.ppq-dash-split-panel { align-self: start; }
@media (max-width: 980px) {
  .ppq-layout-split { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
  .ppq-layout-split .ppq-dash-split-panel { position: static; max-height: none; }
}

/* QoderWork 2026-07-22: legend explaining the 1-6 self-report scale */

But there's a concern: in single mode, `.ppq-dash` sticky with the `.ppq-layout` grid `align-items: start`. The dash is the right grid item, content-sized (max-height capped), start-aligned. Sticky top:1rem makes it stick. Good — fixes single-mode dragging too.

However — one issue: sticky elements need their containing block to be taller than themselves to have scroll room. In single mode, the grid row height = max(centre height, dash height). If centre is short (shorter than dash), the row = dash height, and sticky has no room (fine, dash just sits normally). If centre is tall, row = centre height, dash sticks. Good.

#### Thinking

This is rich. The ESAT analysis viewer reveals the full shape of the existing post-question analysis. Let me understand the data model. Each record `r` has:

- `assessment`, `year`, `section`, `question_number`, `subject`, `q_type`, `option_format`, `option_count`, `correct_answer`, `cognitive_demand`, `esat_in_spec`
- `crop` (image)
- `mid_families` + `primary_mid_family` (misconception-ID families?)
- `probe`: { text, difficulty_source, trick_type, discriminating_atoms[] } — "The Probe" = what the question is really testing/probing
- `cross_member_constraint`
- `options[]`: each { label, is_correct, error_path, sub_answers[] {member_key, error_path}, misconception_slugs[], option_relations[] {relation, of, on} } — "Options & Distractors" with the ERROR PATH for each distractor + misconception slugs
- `methods[]`: each { id, kind, speed, defeats_trap, description, eliminates, when_profitable, strategy_slugs[] } — "Methods" with speed rating, what trap it defeats, when profitable
- `self_report_prompts[]`: each { method_ref, prompt } — "Self-Report Prompts" tied to a method
- `feedback[]`: each { on, when, text } — "Feedback Rules" triggered on certain conditions

This is EXACTLY the post-question feedback / metacognition layer Smith described, already analysed for 33 questions. The structure includes:
1. **The Probe** — what the question discriminates (difficulty source, trick type, discriminating atoms).
2. **Options & Distractors** — each wrong option's ERROR PATH + the misconception slug it maps to. This is the error taxonomy attached to options! When a pupil picks a distractor, you know which misconception/error path they fell into.
3. **Methods** — multiple methods, each with a speed rating, what trap it defeats, when it's profitable, strategy slugs. This is the "shortcut" analysis — the shortcut-awareness ladder Smith described maps onto methods with speed ratings.
4. **Self-Report Prompts** — prompts tied to a method ("did you use this method? did you spot this shortcut?"). This is the post-question self-report tied to methods.
5. **Feedback Rules** — conditional feedback: "on: [event] | when: [condition] → text". Triggered feedback based on what the pupil did.

So "I think we have one" — YES, the ESAT analysis already has a post-question feedback mechanism designed and analysed for 33 questions: the self_report_prompts + feedback rules + methods (with speed/shortcut analysis) + option error paths (misconception mapping). This is the "one" he's referring to. It's been analysed (the data exists) but never WIRED into a viewer (per memory: "Builder never wired analysis panel"; "ESAT feedback loop blocked").

So Smith is showing me: here's the shape of the post-question analysis that's already been done. The kinds of things that need to be brought in for ESAT. 88	
89	- **Question-level fields come from the existing taxonomy (`d026`)**, not reinvented: `q_type`, `cognitive_demand`, `math_demand`, `option_format`. Propose additions against the controlled list.
90	- **Compound answers** (`option_format` = `statement_set`/`table`): each option carries `sub_answers[]` keyed by `member_key`; the question carries a `cross_member_constraint`; `option_relations` may be scoped `on` a `member_key` (`d025`).
91	- **Strategy slugs** reference `data/misconceptions.yaml` and split `mcq_strategy` vs `fast_technique` (`d020`); content slugs likewise. New ones proposed, not invented silently (`d006`, `d010`).
92	- **Read/write via the file reader, not a shell (`d027`).**

94	## Codex hand-back (`d013`)
95	
96	The store mirrors to JSON (`data/analysis/<slug>.json`); Codex ingests it keyed by `id` so the corpus stays the source of truth and any future Question Tools engine inherits it. Architecture owns this format; the per-record shape above IS the hand-back shape (JS wrapper is just the app's load convenience).

380	
381	The current preview finds 6 question groups, 28 question parts, 28 aligned mark-scheme entries, and 28 aligned examiner-report entries for the selected paper. The aligned mark-scheme total is 70 marks, with no missing labels or mark mismatches. This is a preview, not yet a reviewed database import.
382	
383	## Review Workflow
384	
385	Open the generated review page in a browser:
386	
387	```text
388	outputs/review/trilogy_2024_p1h/index.html
389	```
390	
391	It shows each question part with its shared stem, extracted question text, aligned mark scheme answer, examiner-report comments, AO/spec references, extracted figures, visual crops, and links to the rendered question-paper, mark-scheme, and examiner-report pages. This is the main human-review surface for checking extraction quality before database import.
392	
393	The examiner-report preview splits comments by printed part labels such as `04.3` and keeps continuation paragraphs and example-response notes with the current part until the next printed label. It also crops the original report region for review, because examiner reports often include example responses, diagrams, or layout-sensitive comments.
394	
395	The mark-scheme preview now also keeps a row-level `mark_points` layer. This is meant to preserve which answer line earns which mark, whether the credit is printed in the right-hand mark column or shown as an inline bracket such as `(1)` in an alternative route. Extra information is aligned to those marking points where the PDF table layout makes that recoverable.
396	
397	The mark-scheme layer also records emphasis in the printed scheme. Bold spans are saved as `bold` emphasis, and detected underlined spans are saved as `underline` emphasis with `required_exact: true`, because underlined mark-scheme wording normally has to be used exactly.
398	
399	The visual crops are important: PDF text extraction can lose mathematical layout such as fraction bars, stacked formulae, and equation spacing. The searchable text is still useful, but the original crop is kept beside it so the reviewed database can preserve the actual printed maths and diagrams.
400	
401	The preview also saves detected maths in structured form where the PDF layout makes this possible. Examples include superscripts such as `P = I^{2} R` and simple stacked fractions such as `P = \frac{W}{t}`. These detected items are a helper layer, not a replacement for the original crop.
402	
403	Question answer spaces are also preserved where they are drawn as horizontal lines in the PDF. The review text inserts markers such as `[answer space: ______]` for inline blanks and labelled fill-in spaces, while long open-response ruled areas remain in the structured answer-space data and visual crops without cluttering the plain question text.
404	
405	Some equations are embedded as images rather than text in the source PDF. For those cases the review workflow can use notation overrides under `data/notation_overrides/`; the first example is the `05.2` nuclear equation in Trilogy 2024 P1H.
406	
407	Greek symbols in the PDF text layer are normalised into LaTeX-style commands inside detected maths, for example `\alpha`, `\beta`, `\theta`, `\lambda`, `\mu`, `\Delta`, and `\Omega`. If a Greek symbol is only present in an image, the visual crop preserves it for review.
408	
409	## Controlled Batch Runner
410	
411	The first controlled batch run covers the 2024 Trilogy Physics live papers:
412	
413	```powershell
414	.\tools\python\python.exe .\scripts\run_review_batch.py --course Trilogy --year 2024 --papers P1 P2 --tiers F H --batch-id trilogy_2024 --render-dpi 100
415	```
416	
417	Generated batch outputs:
418	
419	- `outputs/batches/trilogy_2024/summary.json`
420	- `outputs/review/trilogy_2024/index.html`
421	- per-paper review folders:
422	  - `outputs/review/trilogy_2024_p1f/index.html`
423	  - `outputs/review/trilogy_2024_p1h/index.html`
424	  - `outputs/review/trilogy_2024_p2f/index.html`
425	  - `outputs/review/trilogy_2024_p2h/index.html`
426	
427	The runner is checkpointed. It writes a summary after each paper set and skips existing stage outputs unless `--force` is supplied. This makes it safe to resume after interruption or rerun after a script fix.
428	
429	To run the full live Trilogy Physics batch currently in the source manifest:
430

439	```

486	## Edexcel 4SS0 Single Science Paper 1P
487	
488	The Edexcel 4SS0 Single Science Paper 1P archive is processed with the same
489	preview/review shape as the Trilogy extraction:
490	
491	```powershell
492	.\tools\python\python.exe .\scripts\extract_edexcel_4ss0_1p.py --render-dpi 100
493	```
494	
495	Generated batch outputs:
496	
497	- `outputs/batches/edexcel_4ss0_1p/summary.json`
498	- `outputs/review/edexcel_4ss0_1p/index.html`
499	- per-paper preview folders under `outputs/previews/edexcel_4ss0_1p_*/`
500	- per-paper review folders under `outputs/review/edexcel_4ss0_1p_*/`
501	
502	The current run covers the sample material plus 2019, 2020, 2021 June,
503	2021 November, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025 Paper 1P sources. It extracts 268
504	question parts, aligns all 268 to mark-scheme entries, and preserves page
505	renders for the review pages.
506	
507	The same notation layer also supports chemical formulae for later Synergy/chemistry-heavy papers. It records formulae such as `CO_{2}`, `H_{2}O`, `MgCl_{2}`, and charged ions such as `SO_{4}^{2-}` where they can be recovered from text and layout.
508	
509	Nuclide/isotope notation is also detected where mass and atomic numbers are stacked beside an element symbol, for example `^{197}_{79}Au`.
510	
511	## ESAT / ENGAA / NSAA Multiple-Choice Extraction
512	
513	The ESAT-family multiple-choice extractor processes the local ENGAA and NSAA
514	Section 1 question-paper / answer-key pairs under `Esat/`:
515	
516	```powershell
517	.\tools\python\python.exe .\scripts\run_esat_batch.py --assessments ENGAA NSAA --batch-id esat_engaa_nsaa_s1 --render-dpi 95 --crop-dpi 160 --ocr-low-confidence
518	```
519	
520	Generated outputs:
521	
522	- `outputs/batches/esat_engaa_nsaa_s1/summary.json`
523	- `outputs/review/esat_engaa_nsaa_s1/index.html`
524	- per-paper previews under `outputs/previews/esat_*_s1/`
525	- per-paper review pages under `outputs/review/esat_*_s1/`
526	- `outputs/exports/esat_engaa_nsaa_s1_flat.csv`
527	- `outputs/review/esat_pat_coverage/coverage.md`
528	- `reports/esat_extraction_probe.md`
529	
530	The current batch covers 16 source pairs, extracts 1042 multiple-choice
531	questions, parses 1042 answer-key rows, and aligns all 1042 labels with no
532	warnings. It handles the historical format changes: old ENGAA papers have 54
533	questions, recent ENGAA papers have 40, old NSAA papers have 90, and recent
534	NSAA papers have 80. The crops are the authoritative evidence for graphs,
535	diagrams, and stacked mathematical layout; searchable text remains a helper
536	layer. Section divider, blank, and title pages are filtered so they do not leak
537	into the previous question's text or crop.
538	
539	The ESAT flat export now carries the official UAT-UK specification marker:
540	`esat_in_spec` is `in_spec` or `out_of_spec`, and `out_of_spec_marked` records
541	whether the printed question number has the cross-through annotation. Visual
542	answer choices are explicit via `has_visual_options`, `visual_choice_labels`,
543	and per-choice `option_is_visual` in `choices_json`. Searchable text also has
544	`text_source`, `text_is_low_confidence`, and `text_quality_flags`. When run
545	with `--ocr-low-confidence`, low-confidence crops are also passed through local
546	Windows OCR and exported separately as `text_render`, `text_render_source`,
547	`text_render_status`, and `text_render_error`. The OCR render is supplemental:
548	crops remain the source of truth for mathematical layout, graphs, diagrams, and
549	visual options. Treat `text_render` as a prose-ordering aid; it is not reliable
550	machine-readable maths.
551	
552	## PAT Question-Only Extraction
553	
554	PAT papers in `Esat/` are a mixed source family rather than compact
555	question-paper / answer-key pairs. The current PAT extractor is therefore
556	question-only: it detects numbered questions, printed marks, visible
557	multiple-choice labels, rendered crops, and review pages, but does not attach
558	answers or mark schemes. The question-only scope is recorded as
559	`answer_status: question_only_no_answer_key`.
560	
561	Example pilot command:
562	
563	```powershell
564	.\tools\python\python.exe .\scripts\extract_pat_preview.py --paper PAT-2023.pdf --render-dpi 80 --crop-dpi 130 --ocr-low-confidence
565	```
566	
567	Generated outputs:
568	
569	- `outputs/previews/pat_2023/preview.json`
570	- `outputs/previews/pat_2023/question_preview.json`
571	- `outputs/previews/pat_2023/summary.json`
572	- `outputs/review/pat_2023/index.html`
573	
574	The same question-only path has been smoke-tested on the local 2017, 2018,
575	2019, 2020, 2022, and 2023 PAT question papers. `PAT-2021.pdf` has very poor
576	searchable text in the local copy and should be treated as an OCR/replacement
577	source problem before extraction.

#### Tool: Read

> Read: `C:\CodexProjects\PaperDatabases\Trilogy Categorisation\README.md`

**Output:**

```json
1	# Trilogy Categorisation — calculation question tagging
2	
3	This folder holds the per-question calculation tagging work for AQA GCSE Combined Science Trilogy (8464) and Synergy (8465) Physics past papers. It is one component of the broader `PaperDatabases` umbrella project that aims to build a structured, queryable database of exam questions.
4	
5	This README is the entry point for any AI or human picking up this work. Read it first.
6	
7	## What this folder contains
8	
9	- **`calculation tagging plan.md`** — the conceptual model (six layers per calculation part) and storage approach. Read this second.
10	- **`formula_catalogue.md`** — the authoritative catalogue of formula and technique codes. Six namespaces (FORMULA, RELATION, RULE, INTERPRET, METHOD, BRIDGE).
11	- **`vocabularies.md`** — closed enums for every controlled field across the six layers (calculation shape, arithmetic subtype, circuit shape, number source, unit handling, mark category, rearrangement steps, gate kind, energy and force types).
12	- **`catalogue additions log.md`** — running log of catalogue entries added during tagging passes, with the question that prompted each one and a review status.
13	- **`pilot tagging 2024 may.md`** — per-part tagging for all four 2024 papers (1F, 1H, 2F, 2H).
14	- **`trilogy tagging 2023.md`** — per-part tagging for all four 2023 papers.
15	- **`trilogy calculation tagging pilot.xlsx`** — combined spreadsheet view of all tagged parts so far, six tabs: Per-part summary, Formula uses, Number sources, Unit handling, Mark breakdown, Gate records.
16	
17	Pilot coverage as of writing: 125 calculation parts across 12 Trilogy papers (May/June 2023, May 2024, and May 2025 sittings). Cross-tier overlaps (e.g. 1F Q06 = 1H Q01 = same whisk question) are tagged consistently in both papers.
18	
19	## Where the source data lives
20	
21	The broader project root is `C:\CodexProjects\PaperDatabases\`. The Trilogy-relevant pieces are:
22	
23	**Past papers**: `Trilogy (and Synergy)/trilogy past papers, ms and examiners reports/` and the sister `synergy past papers, ms and examiners reports/` folder. PDFs of question papers (QP), mark schemes (MS), and examiner reports. Coverage is complete for Trilogy QP/MS from 2018 to 2025 across all four papers (1F, 1H, 2F, 2H), with examiner reports complete bar 2020 (Covid). Synergy is complete bar a known missing 2021 1F QP. See `audit-trilogy-synergy-2026-05-10.md` at the project root.
24	
25	**Inserts and spec**: `Trilogy (and Synergy)/syllabuses and equations sheets/` holds the 2023 Physics Equations Sheet (the post-Covid generous insert), the pre-Covid Physics Equations Insert (the minimal insert that gave only seven equations), and the Trilogy Specification PDF (which contains Appendix B — the authoritative recall + select-and-apply formula list).
26	
27	**Existing first-pass audit**: `Trilogy (and Synergy)/previous question categorisations/trilogy prefix and physics skills marks all papers to 2025.xlsx` is the original ChatGPT-produced prefix/sig-figs/units audit. The calculation tagging model is designed to subsume this audit — Layer 4 covers everything the audit captured plus the non-prefix unit handling cases.
28	
29	## How parsing works (read this — it is the bit I missed at first)
30	
31	Update: there is now a populated SQLite database. For extraction-plus-calculation queries, use `aqa_extraction_plus_calc.db` in this folder. `database/schema.sql` at the project root remains the core schema design, and `database/schema_calc_tagging.sql` is the additive calculation-tagging extension.
32	
33	But the Codex pipeline did produce a comprehensive structured extraction per paper, sitting in `outputs/previews/<slug>/`. The slug pattern is `trilogy_<year>_p<paper><tier>` (e.g. `trilogy_2024_p1f`) or `synergy_<year>_<paper><tier>` (e.g. `synergy_2024_1h`). For each paper:
34	
35	- **`question_preview.json`** — questions and parts already segmented. Each part has its label (e.g. `01.3`), text, marks, page numbers, asset references, answer-space blocks, and a `math_items` list with extracted formulae in both plain-text (`math_text`) and LaTeX (`math_latex`) form. If the question prints a formula, it appears here. If the question says "Use the Physics Equations Sheet", `math_items` is empty for that part (correct behaviour — the formula is on the separate insert PDF, not in the question paper).
36	- **`mark_scheme_preview.json`** — mark scheme entries per question part. Each entry has the `answers` text, `extra_information`, `marks` total, `mark_points` list (point_index, route_label, credit_source, answer_text, marks, emphasis_items, bounding box), `emphasis_items` for bold/underlined wording, AO codes and spec refs. **Important: `mark_points` is not always a reliable per-mark split — for some parts (e.g. 2F 2024 Q07.2 with 4 marks split as 4 separate "1" rows), only one `mark_points` entry appears and the per-mark detail is bundled into the `answers` text. Use `answers` plus `extra_information` as the per-mark source of truth, and `mark_points` only as a hint.**
37	- **`examiner_report_preview.json`** — examiner reports aligned to parts where present.
38	- **`preview.json`** — the raw block-by-block extraction underneath the others.
39	- **`summary.json`** — paper-level metadata and pipeline run info.
40	- **`pages/`** and **`assets/`** — page renders (PNG) and extracted images (PNGs and JPEGs of figures, diagrams).
41	- **`text/`** — flat text dumps per source document. Useful as a fallback only; prefer the structured JSON above.
42	
43	So for any tagging work, the workflow is:
44	
45	1. Open `question_preview.json` for the paper.
46	2. Walk `question_groups → parts` and pick out the calculation parts.
47	3. For each, read `text` (the question wording), `marks`, and `math_items` (printed formulae).
48	4. Open `mark_scheme_preview.json` and look up each part by `label` to get `answers`, `extra_information`, `marks`, and `emphasis_items`. The `answers` field is where per-mark content lives.
49	5. Tag the part across all six layers per the model in `calculation tagging plan.md`.
50	6. Append rows to the spreadsheet and update the per-sitting markdown.
51	
52	The pdftotext fallback is `/sessions/<session>/mnt/outputs/<paper>.txt` if you have generated one. Avoid it when JSON is available.
53	
54	## The six-layer tagging model (summary)
55	
56	Full detail is in `calculation tagging plan.md`. Briefly:
57	
58	1. **Shape**: `is_calculation`, `calculation_shape` (single_formula | multi_stage | graph_technique | formula_quote_only | arithmetic_only | mixed), `arithmetic_subtype` (mean | range | difference | sum | product | quotient | geometric_area | geometric_volume | rate_scaling | nuclide_arithmetic | from_graph), `circuit_shape`.
59	2. **Formula, relation, rule, interpretation, method, or bridge**: catalogue code(s) from the six namespaces, with `route_rank` (1 = shortest legitimate route), `step_index`, `rearrangement_steps` (ordered list of atomic algebraic operations), `is_chain` and `is_bridge` flags.
60	3. **Number sources**: per substituted variable, `source_category` (direct | prefix_strip | prefix_apply | difference | from_graph | from_table | from_previous_part | from_previous_part_shown | distant_in_stem | calculated_earlier_in_same_part).
61	4. **Input/output unit and notation handling**: per atomic action, `type` (prefix_strip | prefix_apply | base_unit_swap | std_form_input | std_form_output | resist_conversion | stay_in_non_si), prefix or unit pair, direction, `conjunctive_group_id` for several actions that together gate one mark.
62	5. **Mark categories**: per mark in the part, one of equation_quoted | substitution | rearrangement | substitution_and_rearrangement | non_final_evaluation | evaluation | evaluation_with_conclusion | prefix_conv | standard_form | sig_figs | unit | correct_to_n_dp | working_shown | energy_named | force_named | other_skill.
63	6. **Dependencies and ECF picture**: gate records with upstream and downstream endpoints (each either a part or a specific formula use), `gate_kind` (no_ecf_gating | ecf_allowed | ecf_silent | value_required_from), evidence text.
64	
65	Plus list-valued `energy_types` and `force_types` per part where relevant. Plus `required_count` for "give two..." identification parts.
66	
67	## How to extend (tagging a new paper)
68	
69	1. Identify the paper's pipeline slug (e.g. `trilogy_2024_p1f`).
70	2. Read `outputs/previews/<slug>/question_preview.json` and `mark_scheme_preview.json`.
71	3. Walk the parts. For each calculation part:
72	   - Layer 1: classify the shape (and circuit_shape / arithmetic_subtype if applicable).
73	   - Layer 2: identify the formula/relation/rule/interpret/method/bridge code(s). If a math_item is present in the question, that's a strong hint at the formula code. If not, the formula is "must recall" or "from insert"; check the catalogue.
74	   - Layer 3: walk the substituted variables in the formula; for each, classify the source.
75	   - Layer 4: identify any unit-handling actions needed.
76	   - Layer 5: read the MS `answers` field per part and split into per-mark categories.
77	   - Layer 6: scan MS `extra_information` for ECF wording ("allow ecf from...", "allow a correct ... using an incorrectly converted ...", "no further marks unless", "the equation X must have been used"). Tag accordingly.
78	4. If a new code is needed (a formula or technique not in the catalogue), add it to `formula_catalogue.md` and log it in `catalogue additions log.md` with the question that prompted it and the prevailing review status.
79	5. Append rows to the xlsx and update or create a per-sitting markdown file.
80	6. Run a sanity check: sum of mark_breakdown rows per part should equal the part's marks (allow ×N for N-route parts).
81	
82	## What is true now versus what is still to come
83	
84	**True now**: the catalogue is stable across the current tagged papers. No new FORMULA/RELATION/RULE/INTERPRET/METHOD/BRIDGE codes have been needed since the planning conversations. The vocabularies are similarly stable; only minor additions during piloting (`arithmetic_subtype = quotient`, `arithmetic_subtype = from_graph`, `evaluation_with_conclusion` mark category). The six-layer model has handled every calculation part encountered, including the rare anti-ECF gating cases and the multi-route mark schemes.
85	
86	**Still to come**:
87	- Continue tagging the remaining untagged sittings and specimen sets.
88	- Tag Synergy Physics calculation parts.
89	- Extend the SQLite database beyond the current tagged subset. The extraction JSON has been bulk-imported for the current AQA preview set, and calculation tagging is layered onto the papers tagged so far via the new tables proposed in `calculation tagging plan.md` (`formula_catalogue`, `calculation_part_facts`, `part_formula_uses`, `part_number_sources`, `part_unit_handling`, `part_mark_categories`, `calculation_gate_records`).
90	- Add a parallel pass for non-calculation questions (qualitative, multi-mark identification, level-of-response). This pass will reuse `energy_types`, `force_types`, `required_count`, the rule codes (`RULE.PARALLEL_RESISTANCE_LESS_THAN_INDIVIDUAL` is the one already added for this future pass), and a similar tag-each-mark approach with a different mark-category vocabulary.
91	
92	## Coding style and conventions
93	
94	- snake_case for codes and vocabulary values (`prefix_strip`, `no_ecf_gating`, `FORMULA.POWER_VI`).
95	- Six-namespace formula catalogue (FORMULA, RELATION, RULE, INTERPRET, METHOD, BRIDGE) with namespace-qualified codes.
96	- One row per atomic fact in the spreadsheet (one row per variable, one row per mark, one row per gate record).
97	- Markdown for per-sitting tagging files; structured tables for human review, with prose summaries calling out patterns.
98	
99	## Recurring patterns confirmed during pilot
100	
101	These are worth knowing before tagging more papers, because they show up across years and predict the data:
102	
103	- The "give the unit" mark consistently sits last in a calculation part where it appears, lifting the mark total by one.
104	- The sig-figs requirement embeds inside the evaluation mark when the question says "give your answer to N significant figures". When the question says "give your answer in standard form" instead, the standard-form requirement gates the evaluation mark via mark-scheme wording "only award if answer is in standard form".
105	- AQA's harsh anti-ECF gating ("this mark can only be scored if equation X has been used", "no further marks unless...") appears roughly once per Higher paper near the end, sometimes embedded as the sig-figs mark.
106	- Multi-route mark schemes (most common in electricity questions and in multi-step kinematics) use `route_rank` with 1 = shortest legitimate route.
107	- Cross-tier question sharing (the same question appearing as a Foundation Q05/06 and a Higher Q01) is common. Tag both papers identically.
108	
109	## When in doubt
110	
111	If the model doesn't cover a case, add to `catalogue additions log.md` with a clear description and the prompting question, then continue tagging. The user reviews the log and decides whether to accept, rename, or reject the addition.
112	
113	If the pipeline JSON is missing or wrong, fall back to `text/` flat dumps or pdftotext on the source PDF directly. Note the gap so it can be fixed in the pipeline later.
114	
115	The plan file (`calculation tagging plan.md`) is the authoritative reference for the model and the long-term storage approach. Edit it when the model evolves. Update this README only when the *workflow* or the *project structure* changes — for model-level changes, edit the plan and the vocabularies.
