1	-- Calculation question tagging schema extension.
2	-- Additive patch over schema.sql. Apply schema.sql first, then this file.
3	--
4	-- Adds the storage for the six-layer calculation tagging model designed for
5	-- Trilogy/Synergy Physics. The authoritative reference for the model lives at
6	-- Trilogy Categorisation/calculation tagging plan.md and the controlled
7	-- vocabularies live at Trilogy Categorisation/vocabularies.md.
8	--
9	-- Conventions:
10	--   * Closed-vocabulary fields use CHECK constraints listing the allowed
11	--     values. This keeps SQLite portable; for Postgres later, the same
12	--     CHECKs work and can be promoted to ENUM types if preferred.
13	--   * Every table that references question_parts uses ON DELETE CASCADE so
14	--     deletion of a part removes its tagging rows cleanly.
15	--   * route_rank = 1 is reserved for the shortest legitimate route.
16	--   * rearrangement_steps is stored as a JSON-encoded ordered list of step
17	--     codes, e.g. '["divide_by_factor","take_sqrt"]'. SQLite has native
18	--     JSON1 support; queries can use json_extract / json_each.
19	--   * energy_types and force_types are similarly JSON-encoded lists.
20	
21	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
22	-- Reference catalogue
23	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
24	
25	CREATE TABLE formula_catalogue (
26	  code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
27	  namespace TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (namespace IN (
28	    'FORMULA', 'RELATION', 'RULE', 'INTERPRET', 'METHOD', 'BRIDGE'
29	  )),
30	  word_form TEXT NOT NULL,
31	  symbol_form TEXT,
32	  latex TEXT,
33	  tier TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'core' CHECK (tier IN ('core', 'HT')),
34	  spec_ref TEXT,
35	  on_2023_insert INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (on_2023_insert IN (0, 1)),
36	  on_pre_covid_insert INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (on_pre_covid_insert IN (0, 1)),
37	  notes TEXT,
38	  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
39	);
40	
41	CREATE INDEX idx_formula_catalogue_namespace ON formula_catalogue(namespace);
42	CREATE INDEX idx_formula_catalogue_insert_status
43	  ON formula_catalogue(on_2023_insert, on_pre_covid_insert);
44	
45	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
46	-- Per-part facts: Layer 1 (shape) + part-level summary
47	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	
49	CREATE TABLE calculation_part_facts (
50	  question_part_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
51	  is_calculation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_calculation IN (0, 1)),
52	  calculation_shape TEXT CHECK (calculation_shape IN (
53	    'single_formula', 'multi_stage', 'graph_technique',
54	    'formula_quote_only', 'arithmetic_only', 'mixed'
55	  )),
56	  arithmetic_subtype TEXT CHECK (arithmetic_subtype IN (
57	    'mean', 'range', 'difference', 'sum', 'product', 'quotient',
58	    'geometric_area', 'geometric_volume', 'rate_scaling',
59	    'nuclide_arithmetic', 'from_graph'
60	  )),
61	  circuit_shape TEXT CHECK (circuit_shape IN (
62	    'simple_series', 'simple_parallel', 'parallel_in_series',
63	    'series_in_parallel', 'not_applicable'
64	  )),
65	  energy_types TEXT,
66	  force_types TEXT,
67	  required_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
68	  notes TEXT,
69	  tagging_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'inferred' CHECK (tagging_status IN ('inferred', 'reviewed', 'confirmed')),
70	  tagger TEXT,
71	  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
72	  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
73	);
74	
75	CREATE INDEX idx_calc_part_facts_shape ON calculation_part_facts(calculation_shape);
76	
77	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
78	-- Layer 2: formula uses per part
79	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
80	
81	CREATE TABLE part_formula_uses (
82	  part_formula_use_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
83	  question_part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
84	  route_label TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'main',
85	  route_rank INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
86	  step_index INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
87	  step_sub_index INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
88	  formula_code TEXT REFERENCES formula_catalogue(code),
89	  rearrangement_steps TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
90	  is_chain INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_chain IN (0, 1)),
91	  is_bridge INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_bridge IN (0, 1)),
92	  bridge_code TEXT REFERENCES formula_catalogue(code),
93	  notes TEXT
94	);
95	-- No UNIQUE on (route, step) because multiple codes legitimately share a step
96	-- (e.g. INTERPRET + METHOD pair, or alternative sub-routes within a step).
97	
98	CREATE INDEX idx_pfu_part ON part_formula_uses(question_part_id);
99	CREATE INDEX idx_pfu_formula ON part_formula_uses(formula_code);
100	CREATE INDEX idx_pfu_bridge ON part_formula_uses(bridge_code);
101	
102	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
103	-- Layer 3: number sources per substituted variable
104	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
105	
106	CREATE TABLE part_number_sources (
107	  part_number_source_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
108	  question_part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
109	  part_formula_use_id INTEGER REFERENCES part_formula_uses(part_formula_use_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
110	  variable_label TEXT NOT NULL,
111	  source_category TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source_category IN (
112	    'direct', 'prefix_strip', 'prefix_apply', 'difference',
113	    'from_graph', 'from_table', 'from_previous_part',
114	    'from_previous_part_shown', 'distant_in_stem',
115	    'calculated_earlier_in_same_part'
116	  )),
117	  value_text TEXT,
118	  notes TEXT
119	);
120	
121	CREATE INDEX idx_pns_part ON part_number_sources(question_part_id);
122	CREATE INDEX idx_pns_source_cat ON part_number_sources(source_category);
123	
124	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
125	-- Layer 4: input/output unit handling
126	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
127	
128	CREATE TABLE part_unit_handling (
129	  part_unit_handling_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
130	  question_part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
131	  handling_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (handling_type IN (
132	    'prefix_strip', 'prefix_apply', 'base_unit_swap',
133	    'std_form_input', 'std_form_output',
134	    'percent_strip', 'percent_apply',
135	    'resist_conversion', 'stay_in_non_si', 'couldnt_categorise'
136	  )),
137	  prefix_code TEXT,
138	  unit_pair TEXT,
139	  direction TEXT CHECK (direction IN ('strip', 'apply')),
140	  conjunctive_group_id TEXT,
141	  evidence TEXT,
142	  notes TEXT
143	);
144	
145	CREATE INDEX idx_puh_part ON part_unit_handling(question_part_id);
146	CREATE INDEX idx_puh_type ON part_unit_handling(handling_type);
147	
148	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
149	-- Layer 5: per-mark categorisation
150	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
151	
152	CREATE TABLE part_mark_categories (
153	  part_mark_category_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
154	  question_part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
155	  mark_index TEXT NOT NULL,
156	  mark_category TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (mark_category IN (
157	    'equation_quoted', 'substitution', 'rearrangement',
158	    'substitution_and_rearrangement', 'non_final_evaluation',
159	    'evaluation', 'evaluation_with_conclusion',
160	    'prefix_conv', 'standard_form', 'sig_figs', 'unit',
161	    'correct_to_n_dp', 'working_shown',
162	    'energy_named', 'force_named', 'other_skill'
163	  )),
164	  applies_to_formula_use_id INTEGER REFERENCES part_formula_uses(part_formula_use_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
165	  applies_to_route_rank INTEGER,
166	  conjunctive_group_id TEXT,
167	  evidence TEXT,
168	  notes TEXT,
169	  UNIQUE (question_part_id, mark_index)
170	);
171	
172	CREATE INDEX idx_pmc_part ON part_mark_categories(question_part_id);
173	CREATE INDEX idx_pmc_category ON part_mark_categories(mark_category);
174	
175	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
176	-- Layer 6: ECF and gating records
177	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
178	
179	CREATE TABLE calculation_gate_records (
180	  calculation_gate_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
181	  upstream_part_id TEXT REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
182	  upstream_formula_use_id INTEGER REFERENCES part_formula_uses(part_formula_use_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
183	  downstream_part_id TEXT REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
184	  downstream_formula_use_id INTEGER REFERENCES part_formula_uses(part_formula_use_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
185	  gate_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (gate_kind IN (
186	    'no_ecf_gating', 'ecf_allowed', 'ecf_silent', 'value_required_from'
187	  )),
188	  evidence_text TEXT NOT NULL,
189	  notes TEXT,
190	  CHECK ((upstream_part_id IS NOT NULL) <> (upstream_formula_use_id IS NOT NULL)),
191	  CHECK ((downstream_part_id IS NOT NULL) <> (downstream_formula_use_id IS NOT NULL))
192	);
193	
194	CREATE INDEX idx_cgr_upstream_part ON calculation_gate_records(upstream_part_id);
195	CREATE INDEX idx_cgr_downstream_part ON calculation_gate_records(downstream_part_id);
196	CREATE INDEX idx_cgr_kind ON calculation_gate_records(gate_kind);
197	
198	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
199	-- Cross-tier links: pair F and H parts that test the same calculation
200	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
201	--
202	-- Captures the AQA pattern of placing the same calculation in both the
203	-- Foundation and Higher paper of a given sitting. The strongest difficulty
204	-- signal in the calc-tagging model: a part with a `shared` link is at-most-F
205	-- difficulty by AQA's own judgement.
206	--
207	-- link_type distinguishes:
208	--   shared   - same question text, same numbers, same mark scheme
209	--   parallel - same formula and topic, different numerical values
210	--   reversed - same formula deployed in opposite direction across tiers
211	--              (e.g. F gives mass and asks for weight; H gives weight and
212	--              asks for mass via the same W = mg)
213	
214	CREATE TABLE cross_tier_links (
215	  cross_tier_link_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
216	  foundation_part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
217	  higher_part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES question_parts(question_part_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
218	  link_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (link_type IN (
219	    'shared', 'parallel', 'reversed'
220	  )),
221	  notes TEXT,
222	  UNIQUE (foundation_part_id, higher_part_id)
223	);
224	
225	CREATE INDEX idx_ctl_f ON cross_tier_links(foundation_part_id);
226	CREATE INDEX idx_ctl_h ON cross_tier_links(higher_part_id);
227	CREATE INDEX idx_ctl_type ON cross_tier_links(link_type);
228	
229	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
230	-- Provenance: tagging passes
231	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
232	
233	CREATE TABLE calc_tagging_passes (
234	  pass_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
235	  description TEXT NOT NULL,
236	  source_file TEXT,
237	  started_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
238	  completed_at TEXT,
239	  tagger TEXT,
240	  notes TEXT
241	);
242	
243	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
244	-- Per-question results: average marks per question-part from AQA QLM reports
245	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
246	--
247	-- Loaded from the QLM (Question Level Marking) CSVs AQA provides to centres
248	-- after each exam series. Each CSV gives one row per candidate plus five
249	-- summary rows at the bottom (Maximum mark / All AQA centres average /
250	-- Our centre average / Similar centres by classification average / Similar
251	-- centres by country/region average). We strip the candidate rows and keep
252	-- only the summaries to avoid storing personal data.
253	--
254	-- exam_paper_id is NULL for bio/chem rows until those papers are added to
255	-- exam_papers. Physics rows resolve to e.g. 'trilogy_2024_p1h'.
256	
257	CREATE TABLE question_part_results (
258	  result_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
259	  exam_paper_id TEXT,
260	  course TEXT NOT NULL,
261	  year TEXT NOT NULL,
262	  component_subject TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (component_subject IN ('Biology','Chemistry','Physics')),
263	  component_paper INTEGER NOT NULL,
264	  tier TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (tier IN ('F','H')),
265	  part_label TEXT NOT NULL,
266	  raw_part_label TEXT,
267	  max_mark REAL,
268	  all_centres_avg REAL,
269	  our_centre_avg REAL,
270	  similar_by_class_avg REAL,
271	  similar_by_region_avg REAL,
272	  candidates_in_our_centre INTEGER,
273	  source_csv TEXT,
274	  UNIQUE (course, year, tier, component_subject, component_paper, part_label)
275	);
276	
277	CREATE INDEX idx_qpr_paper ON question_part_results(exam_paper_id);
278	CREATE INDEX idx_qpr_subject ON question_part_results(component_subject);
279	
280	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
281	-- Convenience views for analytical queries
282	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
283	
284	-- Per-question results with facility / percentage fields.
285	-- Facilities are 0-1; percent fields are 0-100.
286	-- These are derived from average mark divided by max mark.
287	
288	CREATE VIEW v_question_part_results_facility AS
289	SELECT
290	  result_id,
291	  exam_paper_id,
292	  course,
293	  year,
294	  component_subject,
295	  component_paper,
296	  tier,
297	  part_label,
298	  raw_part_label,
299	  max_mark,
300	  all_centres_avg,
301	  our_centre_avg,
302	  similar_by_class_avg,
303	  similar_by_region_avg,
304	  candidates_in_our_centre,
305	  source_csv,
306	  CASE WHEN max_mark > 0 THEN all_centres_avg / max_mark END AS all_centres_facility,
307	  CASE WHEN max_mark > 0 THEN our_centre_avg / max_mark END AS our_centre_facility,
308	  CASE WHEN max_mark > 0 THEN similar_by_class_avg / max_mark END AS similar_by_class_facility,
309	  CASE WHEN max_mark > 0 THEN similar_by_region_avg / max_mark END AS similar_by_region_facility,
310	  CASE WHEN max_mark > 0 THEN 100.0 * all_centres_avg / max_mark END AS all_centres_percent,
311	  CASE WHEN max_mark > 0 THEN 100.0 * our_centre_avg / max_mark END AS our_centre_percent,
312	  CASE WHEN max_mark > 0 THEN 100.0 * similar_by_class_avg / max_mark END AS similar_by_class_percent,
313	  CASE WHEN max_mark > 0 THEN 100.0 * similar_by_region_avg / max_mark END AS similar_by_region_percent,
314	  CASE
315	    WHEN all_centres_avg IS NOT NULL AND our_centre_avg IS NOT NULL
316	      THEN our_centre_avg - all_centres_avg
317	  END AS our_lead_marks,
318	  CASE
319	    WHEN max_mark > 0 AND all_centres_avg IS NOT NULL AND our_centre_avg IS NOT NULL
320	      THEN 100.0 * (our_centre_avg - all_centres_avg) / max_mark
321	  END AS our_lead_percentage_points
322	FROM question_part_results;
323	
324	CREATE VIEW v_calculation_parts AS
325	SELECT
326	  cpf.question_part_id,
327	  qp.question_group_id,
328	  qp.part_label,
329	  qp.marks,
330	  cpf.calculation_shape,
331	  cpf.arithmetic_subtype,
332	  cpf.circuit_shape,
333	  cpf.energy_types,
334	  cpf.force_types,
335	  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pfu.formula_code) AS formula_codes,
336	  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pfu.bridge_code) AS bridge_codes
337	FROM calculation_part_facts cpf
338	JOIN question_parts qp ON qp.question_part_id = cpf.question_part_id
339	LEFT JOIN part_formula_uses pfu ON pfu.question_part_id = cpf.question_part_id
340	WHERE cpf.is_calculation = 1
341	GROUP BY cpf.question_part_id;
342	
343	CREATE VIEW v_mark_category_breakdown AS
344	SELECT
345	  question_part_id,
346	  COUNT(*) AS marks_categorised,
347	  GROUP_CONCAT(mark_category, ',') AS categories
348	FROM part_mark_categories
349	GROUP BY question_part_id;
350	
351	CREATE VIEW v_anti_ecf_gates AS
352	SELECT
353	  cgr.calculation_gate_id,
354	  cgr.gate_kind,
355	  cgr.evidence_text,
356	  COALESCE(cgr.upstream_part_id, 'use:' || cgr.upstream_formula_use_id) AS upstream,
357	  COALESCE(cgr.downstream_part_id, 'use:' || cgr.downstream_formula_use_id) AS downstream
358	FROM calculation_gate_records cgr
359	WHERE cgr.gate_kind = 'no_ecf_gating';
360	
361	-- Position of a question_part within its paper.
362	-- last_question_number_in_paper varies across sittings (Trilogy P1 has gone
363	-- from 6 to 8 questions across recent years), so position_from_end is the
364	-- normalised "lateness" signal: 0 means last group, 1 means second-to-last,
365	-- etc. normalised_position is question_number / last_question_number, so
366	-- 1.0 = last group in the paper, 0.5 = middle.
367	
368	-- last_question_number_in_paper is computed only over question_groups that
369	-- have at least one question_part attached. This filters out orphan groups
370	-- caused by upstream OCR mis-parsing of percentages, axis labels, or other
371	-- numerical text appearing in figures (e.g. "25", "50", "75" picked up as
372	-- spurious question numbers in Trilogy 2025 P1F).
373	
374	CREATE VIEW v_part_position AS
375	SELECT
376	  qp.question_part_id,
377	  ep.exam_paper_id,
378	  qg.question_number,
379	  qp.part_label,
380	  CAST(qg.question_number AS INTEGER) AS question_position,
381	  (SELECT MAX(CAST(qg2.question_number AS INTEGER))
382	   FROM question_groups qg2
383	   WHERE qg2.exam_paper_id = ep.exam_paper_id
384	     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM question_parts qp2 WHERE qp2.question_group_id = qg2.question_group_id)
385	  ) AS last_question_number_in_paper,
386	  ((SELECT MAX(CAST(qg2.question_number AS INTEGER))
387	    FROM question_groups qg2
388	    WHERE qg2.exam_paper_id = ep.exam_paper_id
389	      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM question_parts qp2 WHERE qp2.question_group_id = qg2.question_group_id)
390	   ) - CAST(qg.question_number AS INTEGER)) AS position_from_end,
391	  CAST(qg.question_number AS REAL) /
392	    (SELECT MAX(CAST(qg2.question_number AS INTEGER))
393	     FROM question_groups qg2
394	     WHERE qg2.exam_paper_id = ep.exam_paper_id
395	       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM question_parts qp2 WHERE qp2.question_group_id = qg2.question_group_id)
396	    ) AS normalised_position
397	FROM question_parts qp
398	JOIN question_groups qg ON qg.question_group_id = qp.question_group_id
399	JOIN exam_papers ep ON ep.exam_paper_id = qg.exam_paper_id;
400	
401	-- Join calc-tagged parts to their per-question results (physics only).
402	-- all_centres_facility = all_centres_avg / max_mark (0-1 scale).
403	-- our_lead             = our_centre_avg - all_centres_avg (positive = our cohort outperformed national).
404	
405	CREATE VIEW v_calc_with_results AS
406	SELECT
407	  cpf.question_part_id,
408	  cpf.calculation_shape,
409	  cpf.arithmetic_subtype,
410	  ep.exam_paper_id, ep.course, ep.year, ep.tier,
411	  qp.part_label, qp.marks,
412	  qpr.max_mark            AS results_max_mark,
413	  qpr.all_centres_avg,
414	  qpr.our_centre_avg,
415	  qpr.similar_by_class_avg,
416	  qpr.similar_by_region_avg,
417	  qpr.candidates_in_our_centre,
418	  CASE WHEN qpr.max_mark > 0 THEN qpr.all_centres_avg / qpr.max_mark END  AS all_centres_facility,
419	  CASE WHEN qpr.max_mark > 0 THEN qpr.our_centre_avg / qpr.max_mark END    AS our_centre_facility,
420	  CASE WHEN qpr.all_centres_avg IS NOT NULL AND qpr.our_centre_avg IS NOT NULL
421	       THEN qpr.our_centre_avg - qpr.all_centres_avg END                   AS our_lead
422	FROM calculation_part_facts cpf
423	JOIN question_parts qp ON qp.question_part_id = cpf.question_part_id
424	JOIN question_groups qg ON qg.question_group_id = qp.question_group_id
425	JOIN exam_papers ep ON ep.exam_paper_id = qg.exam_paper_id
426	LEFT JOIN question_part_results qpr ON qpr.exam_paper_id = ep.exam_paper_id
427	  AND qpr.part_label = qp.part_label;
428	
429	-- Cross-tier-augmented view of calculation parts: adds a boolean and the
430	-- linked partner's identifier where present.
431	
432	CREATE VIEW v_calc_with_cross_tier AS
433	SELECT
434	  cpf.question_part_id,
435	  cpf.calculation_shape,
436	  cpf.arithmetic_subtype,
437	  ep.exam_paper_id,
438	  ep.course,
439	  ep.year,
440	  ep.paper,
441	  ep.tier,
442	  qp.part_label,
443	  ctl_f.higher_part_id    AS partner_higher_part_id,
444	  ctl_f.link_type         AS partner_link_type_as_foundation,
445	  ctl_h.foundation_part_id AS partner_foundation_part_id,
446	  ctl_h.link_type         AS partner_link_type_as_higher,
447	  CASE
448	    WHEN ctl_f.cross_tier_link_id IS NOT NULL OR ctl_h.cross_tier_link_id IS NOT NULL
449	      THEN 1 ELSE 0
450	  END AS has_cross_tier_link,
451	  COALESCE(ctl_f.link_type, ctl_h.link_type) AS link_type
452	FROM calculation_part_facts cpf
453	JOIN question_parts qp ON qp.question_part_id = cpf.question_part_id
454	JOIN question_groups qg ON qg.question_group_id = qp.question_group_id
455	JOIN exam_papers ep ON ep.exam_paper_id = qg.exam_paper_id
456	LEFT JOIN cross_tier_links ctl_f ON ctl_f.foundation_part_id = cpf.question_part_id
457	LEFT JOIN cross_tier_links ctl_h ON ctl_h.higher_part_id    = cpf.question_part_id;
458	
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	ESAT / ENGAA / NSAA Section 1 question categoriser (first pass).
4	
5	Reads the flat extraction export and produces a per-question tagged table
6	with a granular, multi-axis taxonomy designed to support drilling and
7	misconception tracking.
8	
9	Axes produced per question:
10	  - subject            physics / maths / chemistry / biology  (mixed parts split)
11	  - subject_source     how subject was decided (label / nsaa_twin / vocab)
12	  - topic_code/topic   ESAT physics topic P1..P7 (physics only)
13	  - subtopic_code      best-effort ESAT sub-point (P3.1 etc.)
14	  - q_type             granular question type (controlled list)
15	  - option_format      numeric / algebraic / graph / diagram / statement_set / ...
16	  - option_count       number of answer options (difficulty signal)
17	  - cognitive_demand   D1 recall/single-step .. D3 extended/synthesis
18	  - math_demand        arithmetic / rearrange / powers_std_form / ratio / geometry
19	  - trap_signals       candidate misconception/distractor traps (best-effort)
20	  - confidence         high / medium / low
21	  - needs_review       1 if low confidence or composite/ambiguous
22	
23	This is a FIRST PASS. Per the project's review-first principle, low-confidence
24	rows and all misconception inferences are intended for human/crop review.
25	"""

35	def clean(s):
36	    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (s or "").replace("\n", " ")).strip()
37	
38	def norm(s):
39	    """aggressive normalisation for twin-matching"""
40	    s = clean(s).lower()
41	    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]", " ", s)
42	    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
43	    return s

2	"""Build IB Economics question categorisation workbook (batch 1: scaffold + 2022 May tagged)."""
3	import json, glob, re, os, collections
4	import openpyxl
5	from openpyxl import Workbook

12	
13	# ---------- 1. rebuild syllabus codes + resolver ----------
14	def uc(u):
15	    if u is None: return None
16	    m=re.match(r'\s*(\d+)\.(\d+)',str(u))
17	    if m: return f"{int(m.group(1))}.{int(m.group(2))}"
18	    if 'Unit 2' in str(u): return "2.0"
19	def depth(c):
20	    if c is None or str(c).strip()=='' : return 0
21	    m=re.match(r'(-+)\s',str(c).lstrip()); return len(m.group(1)) if m else 0
22	def LT(n):
23	    s=''
24	    while n>0: n,r=divmod(n-1,26); s=chr(97+r)+s
25	    return s
26	def RM(n):
27	    v=[(1000,'m'),(900,'cm'),(500,'d'),(400,'cd'),(100,'c'),(90,'xc'),(50,'l'),(40,'xl'),(10,'x'),(9,'ix'),(5,'v'),(4,'iv'),(1,'i')];o=''
28	    for a,s in v:
29	        while n>=a: o+=s; n-=a
30	    return o
31	def ren(p): return ".".join(str(v) if i%3==0 else LT(v) if i%3==1 else RM(v) for i,v in enumerate(p))
32	
33	wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(SRC,data_only=True); ws=wb['economics']
34	SYL=[]; lu=ls=None
35	for r in range(6,524):
36	    vals=[ws.cell(row=r,column=c).value for c in range(1,9)]
37	    if all(v in (None,'') for v in vals): continue
38	    lvl,unit,sub,cont=vals[0],vals[1],vals[2],vals[3]
39	    u=uc(unit) or lu; lu=u; se=sub if sub not in (None,'') else ls; ls=se
40	    SYL.append(dict(u=u,sub=se,cont=cont,depth=depth(cont),lvl=lvl))
41	cur=None;si=0;csk=None;cnt=[0,0,0,0]
42	for x in SYL:
43	    sk=(x['u'],str(x['sub']).strip() if x['sub'] else '')
44	    if x['u']!=cur: cur=x['u'];si=0;csk=None;cnt=[0,0,0,0]
45	    if sk!=csk: si+=1;csk=sk;cnt=[0,0,0,0]
46	    d=x['depth']
47	    for dd in range(d):
48	        if cnt[dd]==0: cnt[dd]=1
49	    cnt[d]+=1
50	    for dd in range(d+1,4): cnt[dd]=0
51	    x['code']=x['u']+"."+ren([si]+[cnt[i] for i in range(d+1)])
52	CODE2TOPIC={x['code']:(x['cont'] if x['cont'] not in (None,'') else f"[{x['sub']}]") for x in SYL}
53	
54	WARN=[]
55	def resolve(unit,kw):
56	    kw_l=kw.lower(); cands=[]
57	    for x in SYL:
58	        if x['u']!=unit: continue
59	        hay=((str(x['cont']) if x['cont'] else '')+' || '+(str(x['sub']) if x['sub'] else '')).lower()
60	        if kw_l in hay: cands.append(x)
61	    if not cands:
62	        WARN.append(f"UNRESOLVED {unit} :: {kw}"); return None
63	    cands.sort(key=lambda x:len(str(x['cont']) if x['cont'] else 'zzz'*9))
64	    return cands[0]['code']
65	
66	def codes(*pairs):
67	    out=[]
68	    for u,kw in pairs:
69	        c=resolve(u,kw)
70	        if c and c not in out: out.append(c)
71	    return out
72	
73	# ---------- 2. command-term / type helpers ----------

75	     'Describe','Determine','Discuss','Draw','Evaluate','Examine','Explain','Identify','Justify','Label','List',
76	     'Measure','Outline','Plot','Recommend','Sketch','State','Suggest','Analyse','Comment','Show']
77	def command_of(text):
78	    if not text: return ''
79	    s=str(text)
80	    for c in sorted(CMD,key=len,reverse=True):

383	## Review Workflow
384	
385	Open the generated review page in a browser:
386	
387	```text
388	outputs/review/trilogy_2024_p1h/index.html
389	```
390	
391	It shows each question part with its shared stem, extracted question text, aligned mark scheme answer, examiner-report comments, AO/spec references, extracted figures, visual crops, and links to the rendered question-paper, mark-scheme, and examiner-report pages. This is the main human-review surface for checking extraction quality before database import.
392	
393	The examiner-report preview splits comments by printed part labels such as `04.3` and keeps continuation paragraphs and example-response notes with the current part until the next printed label. It also crops the original report region for review, because examiner reports often include example responses, diagrams, or layout-sensitive comments.
394	
395	The mark-scheme preview now also keeps a row-level `mark_points` layer. This is meant to preserve which answer line earns which mark, whether the credit is printed in the right-hand mark column or shown as an inline bracket such as `(1)` in an alternative route. Extra information is aligned to those marking points where the PDF table layout makes that recoverable.
396	
397	The mark-scheme layer also records emphasis in the printed scheme. Bold spans are saved as `bold` emphasis, and detected underlined spans are saved as `underline` emphasis with `required_exact: true`, because underlined mark-scheme wording normally has to be used exactly.
398	
399	The visual crops are important: PDF text extraction can lose mathematical layout such as fraction bars, stacked formulae, and equation spacing. The searchable text is still useful, but the original crop is kept beside it so the reviewed database can preserve the actual printed maths and diagrams.
400	
401	The preview also saves detected maths in structured form where the PDF layout makes this possible. Examples include superscripts such as `P = I^{2} R` and simple stacked fractions such as `P = \frac{W}{t}`. These detected items are a helper layer, not a replacement for the original crop.
402	
403	Question answer spaces are also preserved where they are drawn as horizontal lines in the PDF. The review text inserts markers such as `[answer space: ______]` for inline blanks and labelled fill-in spaces, while long open-response ruled areas remain in the structured answer-space data and visual crops without cluttering the plain question text.
404	
405	Some equations are embedded as images rather than text in the source PDF. For those cases the review workflow can use notation overrides under `data/notation_overrides/`; the first example is the `05.2` nuclear equation in Trilogy 2024 P1H.
406	
407	Greek symbols in the PDF text layer are normalised into LaTeX-style commands inside detected maths, for example `\alpha`, `\beta`, `\theta`, `\lambda`, `\mu`, `\Delta`, and `\Omega`. If a Greek symbol is only present in an image, the visual crop preserves it for review.
408

544	`text_source`, `text_is_low_confidence`, and `text_quality_flags`. When run

546	Windows OCR and exported separately as `text_render`, `text_render_source`,
547	`text_render_status`, and `text_render_error`. The OCR render is supplemental:
548	crops remain the source of truth for mathematical layout, graphs, diagrams, and
549	visual options. Treat `text_render` as a prose-ordering aid; it is not reliable
550	machine-readable maths.

552	## PAT Question-Only Extraction
553	
554	PAT papers in `Esat/` are a mixed source family rather than compact
555	question-paper / answer-key pairs. The current PAT extractor is therefore
556	question-only: it detects numbered questions, printed marks, visible
557	multiple-choice labels, rendered crops, and review pages, but does not attach
558	answers or mark schemes. The question-only scope is recorded as
559	`answer_status: question_only_no_answer_key`.

1	# Calculation question tagging plan
2	
3	Working plan for categorising calculation questions across the Trilogy and Synergy past papers. Designed to subsume the existing first-pass prefix audit in `Trilogy (and Synergy)/previous question categorisations/trilogy prefix and physics skills marks all papers to 2025.xlsx`.
4	
5	Last revised after planning conversation on 2026-05-23.
6	
7	## What we record per calculation question part
8	
9	Six layers per part. Each is small on its own; consistency across the archive is where the value sits. Layer 4 was broadened during planning to absorb everything the old prefix audit captured, so the old workbook becomes derivable from the new tagging and can be retired.
10	
11	### Layer 1: shape of the part
12	
13	- `is_calculation`: yes / no. Everything below is filled only where this is yes.
14	- `calculation_shape`: one of `single_formula`, `multi_stage`, `graph_technique`, `formula_quote_only`, `mixed`.
15	- `circuit_shape`: for circuit questions, one of `simple_series`, `simple_parallel`, `parallel_in_series` (overall series chain with a parallel pair somewhere in it), `series_in_parallel` (overall parallel branches each containing a series sub-section), `not_applicable`. Treated as a starting list and refinable during the pilot.
16	
17	`formula_quote_only` covers the Foundation "write down the equation that links..." parts. `mixed` covers parts that combine a quote-the-equation mark with substitution work.
18	
19	### Layer 2: formula, relation, rule, interpretation, method, or bridge
20	
21	A controlled-vocabulary code per item. The catalogue spans six namespaces, split so that what something *means* is kept separate from how it is *computed*, and given equations are kept separate from non-given derived relations and circuit-analysis rules:
22	
23	- `FORMULA.*` — given equations on either insert, e.g. `FORMULA.EK`, `FORMULA.EP`, `FORMULA.PIV`, `FORMULA.PI2R`, `FORMULA.Q_IT`, `FORMULA.V_IR`, `FORMULA.W_FD`, `FORMULA.F_KE`, `FORMULA.RHO_M_V`.
24	- `RELATION.*` — non-given algebraic relations: `RELATION.STOPPING_DISTANCE` (stopping = thinking + braking), `RELATION.SERIES_RESISTANCE_SUM` (R_total = R_1 + R_2), `RELATION.SERIES_VOLTAGE_SUM`, `RELATION.PARALLEL_CURRENT_SUM`, and similar.
25	- `RULE.*` — circuit-analysis rules: `RULE.CIRCUIT_SERIES_CURRENT_CONSTANT`, `RULE.CIRCUIT_PARALLEL_VOLTAGE_CONSTANT`, `RULE.CIRCUIT_V_AND_I_PAIRED` (V and I in V=IR or P=VI must apply to the same component), `RULE.CIRCUIT_CHOOSE_V`, `RULE.CIRCUIT_CHOOSE_I`.
26	- `INTERPRET.*` — conceptual interpretations of graph features: `INTERPRET.AREA_VT_IS_DISPLACEMENT`, `INTERPRET.AREA_SPEED_TIME_IS_DISTANCE`, `INTERPRET.GRADIENT_VT_IS_ACCELERATION`, `INTERPRET.GRADIENT_DT_IS_SPEED`, `INTERPRET.GRADIENT_QT_IS_CURRENT`, `INTERPRET.AREA_FE_IS_ELASTIC_PE`, `INTERPRET.AREA_FD_IS_WORK`, `INTERPRET.GRADIENT_FE_IS_SPRING_CONSTANT`. List is enumerative; new entries added to the catalogue additions log as they come up.
27	- `METHOD.*` — procedural methods for computing an area or gradient. Granularity reflects the level of skill demand: `METHOD.SINGLE_TRIANGLE` (one triangle, ½ × base × height), `METHOD.COMPOUND_SHAPES` (triangles plus rectangles plus trapezia in any combination — decomposition left to the student), `METHOD.COUNT_SQUARES` (curved areas), `METHOD.TANGENT_RISE_OVER_RUN`, `METHOD.GRADIENT_OF_STRAIGHT_LINE`. A simple-rectangle area is not given a METHOD code — that case is just a FORMULA application (e.g. distance = speed × time).
28	- `BRIDGE.*` — conservation / equivalence statements that join two formulae together, e.g. `BRIDGE.EK_EP_GRAVITATIONAL`, `BRIDGE.EK_EE_ELASTIC`, `BRIDGE.WORK_ENERGY`, `BRIDGE.POWER_TIME_ENERGY`, `BRIDGE.EFFICIENCY_RATIO`.
29	
30	A graph-technique part typically carries both an `INTERPRET.*` code (the conceptual claim, usually load-bearing for one mark) and a `METHOD.*` code (the procedural choice the student made). Both are recorded, not one.
31	
32	Each catalogue entry records `on_2023_insert` and `on_pre_covid_insert` as separate booleans, so "must recall" is derivable for either era. The catalogue is a living document; new codes are added during tagging passes and logged in a `catalogue additions log` for the user to review without pausing tagging.
33	
34	Multiple legitimate routes for the same part are recorded with `route_rank`, where rank 1 is the shortest legitimate route and higher ranks are longer alternatives, including the route AQA's mark scheme happens to use when it is not the shortest.
35	
36	### Layer 3: where the numbers come from
37	
38	One entry per variable substituted into a formula. Source from:
39	
40	- `direct`: literal value given in the question text.
41	- `prefix_strip`: a value with a prefix that must be stripped to SI before substituting.
42	- `prefix_apply`: the answer must be returned in a prefixed unit.
43	- `difference`: must compute a difference such as Delta-v or Delta-theta before substituting.
44	- `from_graph`: read off a graph.
45	- `from_table`: read off a table.
46	- `from_previous_part`: "use your answer to part X" — the standard ECF candidate.
47	- `from_previous_part_shown`: a previous part was a "show that..." and the student is supplied the value to use; numerically like `direct` but distinct because it lets us spot AQA pushing the working into a show part to relieve later parts of computing it.
48	- `distant_in_stem`: the trap where the value sits at the top of a long question while substitution happens at the end.
49	- `calculated_earlier_in_same_part`: e.g. find I from V/R first, then use I in P=VI within the same part.
50	
51	The variable label is also recorded so we can later ask things like "how often is m the value that needs prefix conversion?".
52	
53	### Layer 4: input and output unit and notation handling
54	
55	Broadened from "prefix handling" to absorb the old prefix audit fully. One entry per handling action.
56	
57	Type values:
58	
59	- `prefix_strip` (strip a prefix from an input value).
60	- `prefix_apply` (apply a prefix to the output answer).
61	- `base_unit_swap` (min to s, hour to s, day to s, year to s — non-prefix unit swaps).
62	- `composite_unit_conversion` (m/s to km/h, N/cm^2 to Pa, g/cm^3 to kg/m^3 — compound units).
63	- `std_form_input` (the substituted value is given in standard form and must be parsed).
64	- `std_form_output` (answer required in standard form).
65	- `resist_conversion` (the bait-the-student traps, e.g. spring N/cm staying as N/cm).
66	- `stay_in_non_si` (working remains in a non-SI unit throughout, no conversion).
67	- `couldnt_categorise` (parity with the old audit; flagged for review).
68	
69	Each entry records prefix_code or unit_pair, direction (`strip` or `apply` where relevant), `conjunctive_group_id` so several actions can be tied to a single mark, and an evidence string.
70	
71	The old prefix audit becomes a SQL view over this table.
72	
73	### Layer 5: how the marks are awarded
74	
75	Per mark in the mark scheme for this part, a category from:
76	
77	- `equation_quoted`: a mark for writing down the equation.
78	- `substitution`: a mark for substituting values in correctly.
79	- `rearrangement`: a mark for the rearranged form (AQA typically bundles all rearranging into one mark).
80	- `non_final_evaluation`: a mark for an intermediate numerical answer in a multi-stage part.
81	- `evaluation`: a mark for the final numerical answer.
82	- `prefix_conv`: an explicit mark for handling a prefix conversion.
83	- `standard_form`: an explicit mark for expressing the answer in standard form.
84	- `sig_figs`: an explicit mark for the right number of significant figures.
85	- `unit`: an explicit mark for the unit.
86	- `correct_to_n_dp`: an explicit mark for the right number of decimal places.
87	- `working_shown`: an explicit mark for shown working.
88	- `other_skill`: catch-all, flagged for review.
89	
90	Each mark can point to which `part_formula_uses` row (route, step) it applies to, and to a `conjunctive_group_id` from Layer 4 so we can record "the substitution mark requires both prefix conversions correct".
91	
92	A separate per-formula-use field `rearrangement_type` records the algebraic work required even where the mark scheme bundles it into one rearrangement mark:
93	
94	- `none`: direct substitution into the given form.
95	- `mult_swap`: A = B x C, isolate B or C.
96	- `div_isolate_numerator`: A = B / C, isolate B.
97	- `div_isolate_denominator`: A = B / C, isolate C (harder for GCSE).
98	- `sqrt`: square root needed.
99	- `square`: squaring needed.
100	- `chain`: output of one equation goes into the next.
101	- `bridge`: an explicit `BRIDGE.*` statement is used to equate two formulae.
102	- `chain_bridge`: chain across more than two formulae with at least one bridge.
103	
104	When `bridge` or `chain_bridge` is in play, the row points to which `BRIDGE.*` code is used.
105	
106	Categorised marks should sum to the part's mark allocation — a free integrity check.
107	
108	### Layer 6: dependencies and ECF picture
109	
110	ECF / gating records identify both ends of the transition, not just the host part. Gating typically sits between two formula uses rather than between two parts, e.g. inside one multi-stage part the power-formula marks are gated on the energy-formula calculation being correct. So a gating record must say *which formula gates which*.
111	
112	A `calculation_gate_records` table with four endpoint columns handles both inter-part and intra-part cases uniformly:
113	
114	- `upstream_part_id` or `upstream_formula_use_id` (exactly one non-null) — the thing whose correctness is required.
115	- `downstream_part_id` or `downstream_formula_use_id` (exactly one non-null) — the thing whose marks are gated.
116	- `gate_kind` — one of the values below.
117	- `evidence_text` — the mark-scheme wording that supports the classification.
118	
119	Gate kinds:
120	
121	- `no_ecf_gating`: explicit anti-ECF wording in the mark scheme, e.g. "no further marks unless...".
122	- `ecf_allowed`: explicit positive ECF wording, e.g. "allow value calculated from their X".
123	- `ecf_silent`: the mark scheme says neither; AQA convention is no carry-forward, but the absence is itself information.
124	- `value_required_from`: must use a specific value from a named other part.
125	
126	The existing `part_dependencies` table is retained for the broader project's "this part needs this part" semantic dependencies and is not used for calculation gating. Default of "not recorded" means the part has not been reviewed for ECF yet, distinct from `ecf_silent`.
127	
128	## How this is stored
129	
130	Three concentric layers.
131	
132	**Innermost: small reference files in `Trilogy Categorisation/`.** A `formula_catalogue.md` covering FORMULA, TECHNIQUE, and BRIDGE namespaces; a `vocabularies.md` listing the closed enums for shape, source, unit-handling type, mark category, rearrangement type, and dependency type; a `catalogue additions log.md` capturing items added during passes. All version-controlled and hand-editable.
133	
134	**Middle: purpose-built database tables.** Rather than overload `taxonomy_tags` and `detected_features`, add:
135	
136	- `formula_catalogue` (code, name, latex, namespace `FORMULA|RELATION|RULE|INTERPRET|METHOD|BRIDGE`, on_2023_insert, on_pre_covid_insert, notes).
137	- `calculation_part_facts` (one row per question_part: is_calculation, calculation_shape, circuit_shape, notes).
138	- `part_formula_uses` (one row per part-route-step: route_label, route_rank, step_index, formula_code, rearrangement_type, bridge_code).
139	- `part_number_sources` (one row per substituted variable).
140	- `part_unit_handling` (one row per unit-handling action; replaces the prefix-only audit).
141	- `part_mark_categories` (one row per mark in the mark scheme).
142	- `calculation_gate_records` (one row per gate: upstream and downstream endpoints, gate_kind, evidence_text).
143	- `part_dependencies` (existing table, retained for broader semantic dependencies between parts; not used for calculation gating).
144	
145	`taxonomy_tags` remains for general topic/AO/working-scientifically tagging.
146	
147	**Outermost: a spreadsheet view** mirroring the shape of the existing "Question log" sheet, one row per (paper, question_part, layer-entry). Generated from the database after each pass. This is the layer reviewed by hand.
148	
149	## Sequencing
150	
151	1. **Build the formula, technique, and bridge catalogue.** Draft from the 2023 insert, the pre-Covid insert, the Trilogy spec, plus the user-supplied non-given techniques and circuit rules. Insert-version booleans filled. Reviewed before any tagging.
152	2. **Pilot on Trilogy 1H May 2024 and 1F May 2024 as a paired set.** Tag every calculation part across all six layers. Output the spreadsheet view. Use it to find missing categories, over- or under-used tags, naming issues. Pause for user review.
153	3. **Scale out, paper by paper, no per-paper pause once the pilot is settled.** New catalogue entries are added to the additions log as they come up rather than blocking the pass.
154	4. **Multi-stage second pass.** Re-walk multi-stage parts for alternative routes, bridging equations, and ECF state.
155	5. **Verification pass.** Categorised marks sum to part marks, every code exists in the catalogue, overlapping Foundation/Higher questions are tagged identically, and the old prefix-audit view reproduces the existing first-pass counts within an acceptable tolerance.
156	
157	## Source provenance
158	
159	- The prefix audit was a first-pass produced by ChatGPT.
160	- The underlying question database was produced by a Codex project pulling text and layout from the past-paper PDFs.
161	- Synergy papers mix biology, chemistry, and physics. Calculation tagging is biased to physics but errs on the side of over-categorising; obviously biology / chemistry items can be skipped without worrying about borderline cases.
162	
163	## Archive completeness
164	
165	Per `audit-trilogy-synergy-2026-05-10.md` Trilogy Physics QP and MS coverage is complete for 2018 to 2025 across all four papers, with examiner reports complete bar 2020 (Covid). Synergy is complete bar a missing 2021 1F question paper. There are no other known gaps. The pilot papers are in scope.
166

PaperDatabases is the shared extraction pipeline. Extraction and tagging are separate stages, and the subjects are at very different points on the tagging ladder:

Extraction complete (5136 parts in a 25.9 MB SQLite DB), syllabus tagging done for every paper 2018-2025, and on top of that a six-layer calculation-tagging scheme (formula, number sources, unit handling, mark categories, ECF gating) with 646 calc parts tagged so far.

**IB Physics** — this is where your "questions in tests" flag lands. The `3. Assessments` folder holds in-house material, not official past papers: Data Analysis Tests, the 2026 Y13 mocks, about 35 topic mini-tests, a Topic E test, and the Y10/Y12 school exams. Those need stripping out of scope. On top of that, IB Physics has no structured per-question syllabus tagging (the topic packs are pre-organised but there's no queryable tag DB), and extraction is only prototyped.

**4SS0 / Pre-IB Edexcel Single Science** — confirmed present: a big archive of 4SS0 and 4SD0 papers 2019-2026 plus the bio/chem siblings. **IB Chemistry, IB Maths, Other boards** are extraction-only inside this repo (Chemistry's category_code tagging lives in the chemistrydriller project, not here).

Let me think about the `when` grammar of feedback. From the data:
- `on: "option:H"`, `when: "used:full_solve"` — fires when option H is chosen AND the self-report for method full_solve is "used".
- `on: "option:G"`, `when: "used:M3"` — option G AND self-report "used" for M3.

- `on: "option:B"`, `when: "used:M3"`.

So the `when` grammar is `<state>:<method_ref>`. And `on` is `option:<label>` or `any_wrong` or `any_correct`.

Feedback matching:
```
_matchFeedback(chosenLabel, isRight, selfReports) {
  // selfReports = { method_ref: state }
  const rec = this._analysis;
  if (!rec || !rec.feedback) return null;
  for (const fb of rec.feedback) {
    // match 'on'
    let onOk = false;
    if (fb.on === 'any_wrong') onOk = !isRight;
    else if (fb.on === 'any_correct') onOk = isRight;
    else if (fb.on && fb.on.indexOf('option:') === 0) onOk = fb.on.slice(7).toUpperCase() === chosenLabel.toUpperCase();
    if (!onOk) continue;
    // match 'when'
    if (this._whenMatches(fb.when, selfReports)) return fb;
  }
  return null;
}
_whenMatches(when, selfReports) {
  if (!when) return true;
  const i = when.indexOf(':');
  if (i > 0) {
    const state = when.slice(0, i), ref = when.slice(i+1);
    return selfReports[ref] === state;
  }
  // bare derived flag: rough match — does the flag start with a known state?
  // NOTE-TO-SELF: reconcile with misconceptions_core.yaml derived flags
  for (const ref in selfReports) {
    const st = selfReports[ref];
    // e.g. 'did_not_sketch' ~ state 'did_not_see'; crude prefix match on state before last '_'
    if (when.indexOf(st.split('_').slice(0,2).join('_')) === 0) return true;
  }
  return false;
}
```

  Viewer.prototype._renderInterrogation = function () {
    const cfg = this.cfg;
    const box = this.q(".ppq-interrogation");
    box.innerHTML = "";
    if (!cfg.modules.postQuestionReview || !cfg.analysisOf) return;
    const rec = cfg.analysisOf(this.cur);
    if (!rec) return; /* graceful absence: most questions have no analysis yet */
    this._analysis = rec;
    this._analysisSelfReports = {};

    const STATE_LABELS = {
      used: "I used this",
      saw_and_used: "Saw it, used it",
      saw_and_discarded: "Saw it, didn't use it",
      barely_considered: "Barely considered it",
      did_not_see: "Didn't see it",
      saw_and_got_stuck: "Tried it, got stuck"
    };

    box.style.display = "block";
    box.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-title" }, "What this question is really about"));

    /* --- the probe --- */
    if (rec.probe && rec.probe.text) {
      const probe = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-probe" });
      probe.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-probe-text" }, esc(rec.probe.text)));
      const chips = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-chips" });
      if (rec.probe.difficulty_source) chips.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-chip" }, "difficulty: " + esc(rec.probe.difficulty_source)));
      if (rec.probe.trick_type) chips.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-chip" }, esc(rec.probe.trick_type)));
      probe.appendChild(chips);
      box.appendChild(probe);
    }

    /* --- the chosen option's error path --- */
    const chosen = this._chosenLabel;
    if (chosen && rec.options && rec.options.length) {
      const opt = rec.options.filter((o) => String(o.label).toUpperCase() === chosen)[0];
      if (opt && opt.error_path) {
        const op = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option " + (opt.is_correct ? "right" : "wrong") });
        op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-head" }, "You picked " + esc(opt.label) + (opt.is_correct ? " — the right answer" : "")));
        op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-path" }, esc(opt.error_path)));
        if (opt.misconception_slugs && opt.misconception_slugs.length) {
          const sl = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-slugs" });
          opt.misconception_slugs.forEach((s) => sl.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-slug" }, esc(s))));
          op.appendChild(sl);
        }
        box.appendChild(op);
      }
    }

    /* --- methods, quick route highlighted --- */
    if (rec.methods && rec.methods.length) {
      box.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-subhead" }, "Ways through it"));
      rec.methods.forEach((m) => {
        const md = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method" + (m.defeats_trap ? " quick" : "") });
        const head = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method-head" });
        head.appendChild(el("b", null, esc(m.id)));
        head.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-kind" }, esc(m.kind)));
        if (m.speed) head.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-speed" }, esc(m.speed)));
        if (m.defeats_trap) head.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-defeats" }, "beats the trap"));
        md.appendChild(head);
        md.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method-desc" }, esc(m.description)));
        box.appendChild(md);
      });
    }

    /* --- one primary self-report prompt (the shortcut-awareness ladder) --- */
    if (rec.self_report_prompts && rec.self_report_prompts.length) {
      const p = rec.self_report_prompts[0]; /* NOTE-TO-SELF 2: first only, for now */
      const pr = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-prompt" });
      pr.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-prompt-text" }, esc(p.prompt)));
      const states = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-states" });
      const self = this;
      (p.states || Object.keys(STATE_LABELS)).forEach((st) => {
        const b = el("button", { class: "ppq-iq-state", "data-state": st }, esc(STATE_LABELS[st] || st));
        b.addEventListener("click", () => {
          self._analysisSelfReports[p.method_ref] = st;
          states.querySelectorAll(".ppq-iq-state").forEach((x) => x.classList.remove("sel"));
          b.classList.add("sel");
          self._fireReport({ status: "interrogation", qtype: "self_report", extra_json: JSON.stringify({ method_ref: p.method_ref, state: st }) });
          self._renderInterrogationFeedback(box);
        });
        states.appendChild(b);
      });
      pr.appendChild(states);
      box.appendChild(pr);
    }

    /* --- feedback lands here --- */
    box.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-feedback" }));

  Viewer.prototype._renderInterrogationFeedback = function (box) {
    const fbBox = box.querySelector(".ppq-iq-feedback");
    if (!fbBox) return;
    const fb = this._matchInterrogationFeedback();
    if (!fb) { fbBox.innerHTML = ""; return; }
    fbBox.innerHTML = "";
    fbBox.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-feedback-text" }, esc(fb.text)));
  };

  Viewer.prototype._matchInterrogationFeedback = function () {
    const rec = this._analysis;
    if (!rec || !rec.feedback) return null;
    const chosen = this._chosenLabel, isRight = this._wasRight, sr = this._analysisSelfReports;
    for (let i = 0; i < rec.feedback.length; i++) {
      const fb = rec.feedback[i];
      let onOk = false;
      if (fb.on === "any_wrong") onOk = isRight === false;
      else if (fb.on === "any_correct") onOk = isRight === true;
      else if (fb.on && fb.on.indexOf("option:") === 0) onOk = fb.on.slice(7).toUpperCase() === chosen;
      else if (!fb.on) onOk = true;
      if (!onOk) continue;
      if (this._interrogationWhenMatches(fb.when, sr)) return fb;
    }
    return null;
  };

  Viewer.prototype._interrogationWhenMatches = function (when, sr) {
    if (!when) return true;
    const ci = when.indexOf(":");
    if (ci > 0) {
      const state = when.slice(0, ci), ref = when.slice(ci + 1);
      /* method_ref may be a method id (M3) or a kind (full_solve); match either the
         prompt's method_ref or, loosely, the method kind the learner said they used. */
      if (sr[ref] === state) return true;
      return false;
    }
    /* NOTE-TO-SELF 3: bare derived flag (e.g. did_not_sketch). Crude prefix match on
       the state's first two tokens. Replace with misconceptions_core.yaml look-up. */
    for (const ref in sr) {
      const st = sr[ref];
      const prefix = String(st).split("_").slice(0, 2).join("_");
      if (prefix && when.indexOf(prefix) === 0) return true;
    }
    return false;
  };

  // --------------------------------------------------------------- structured paper (module)
  Viewer.prototype._blockParts = function (q) {
    const cfg = this.cfg, block = cfg.blockKeyOf(q);
    if (!block) return [];
    return this.questions.filter((item) => { const id = cfg.idOf(item); return id === block || String(id).indexOf(block + "(") === 0; });

My honest answer should be nuanced. Let me think about what tagging actually decomposes into:

Tagging has layers of increasing judgement:
- **Structural extraction** (which question, how many marks, what text) — fully codable, already done by the pipeline.
- **Topic/syllabus code assignment** — partly codable. A model can propose candidate codes with high recall. But picking the PRIMARY code, and deciding secondary vs framing, is judgement. The machine is good at "this question touches 6.1.1.4 and 6.2.6.1" but less reliable at "the primary demand is the rearrangement, the equation is framing."
- **Facet tagging** (calculation shape, formula codes, unit handling, mark categories) — highly codable because it's closed-vocabulary and has integrity checks. This is where Codex shines.
- **Misconception/trap/error-path tagging** (the ESAT analysis layer) — this is the hardest, most expert layer. This is NOT really "codable" in the sense of a bulk pass; it's per-question expert analysis. A model can draft it, but it needs the subject expert's eye. This is the layer that makes the interrogation actually teach.

So the answer to "does the two-pass division make sense?" — yes, and it's already the estate's established pattern (Economics handoff says exactly this; Trilogy calc tagging used a ChatGPT first pass). The machine first pass is worth it because it converts a blank page into a reviewable draft, which is much faster than tagging from scratch, and it's cheap.

But the answer to "is it worth trying to code that?" depends on the layer:
- For the structural and closed-vocabulary layers (calc facets, candidate syllabus codes), yes, absolutely code it. High value, low risk, automatic checks.
- For the judgement layers (primary code, misconception, trap), a machine first pass is a useful draft but you must not mistake it for done. The Economics batch is the warning: 2737 auto-coded questions, zero reviewed, so effectively zero usable for a viewer that needs trustworthy filtering. The first pass created a review debt, not an asset.

So the real risk Smith is sniffing at: does a cheap first pass create the ILLUSION of progress while the expensive part (review) piles up? That's the honest tension. My view: a first pass is worth it ONLY IF there's a review path that will actually be walked, and ONLY for the layers where review is tractable. For the deep misconception layer, you don't bulk-first-pass it; you do it question by question for the questions that matter (which is exactly how the ESAT analysis store grew — 33 questions, carefully, not 1042 in a batch).

Also worth noting: the four subjects are at different points and have different value/risk:
- **IB Physics**: first needs the in-house tests stripped out (a coding job — a filter, deterministic), THEN a topic-tagging pass. The topic packs are already pre-organised by topic, so actually IB Physics has a head start — the topic-pack structure IS a coarse tag. - **4SS0/Pre-IB**: extraction-only, no syllabus structure in the repo. A first pass needs the Edexcel spec as the controlled vocabulary first. Worth a first pass but needs the vocabulary built.
- **IB Chemistry**: the category_code tagging lives in chemistrydriller, not PaperDatabases. So "tagging Chemistry" might already partly exist — need to reconcile, not re-tag. A first pass here might be the wrong framing; it's more a reconciliation job.
- **IB Maths**: extraction-only, huge (53 + 199 papers). Maths syllabus tagging is judgement-heavy (which topic is a question "really" testing). A candidate-code first pass is worth it, but Maths has the added complication of formula OCR. 

So my recommendation: yes, the two-pass model makes sense and it's already your house style. But I'd frame it as: Codex first pass is worth it for the CLOSED-VOCABULARY, CHECKABLE layers (candidate syllabus codes, calc facets, and the deterministic cleanup like stripping IB Physics tests). It is a stack of layers with very different automatability, and whether a Codex first pass pays off depends entirely on which layer you point it at.

At the bottom is structural extraction (which question, how many marks, what text), which is fully codable and the pipeline already does. Above that is candidate syllabus-code assignment, which a model does with high recall: it is good at "this question touches 6.1.1.4 and 6.2.6.1", less reliable at deciding which one is the primary demand and which is just framing. At the top is the misconception / trap / error-path layer, the ESAT analysis stuff, which is expert judgement per question and is not really a bulk-coding job at all.

So my honest read: a Codex first pass is absolutely worth it for the closed-vocabulary, checkable layers, and for the deterministic cleanups like stripping the in-house tests out of IB Physics. There the machine converts a blank page into a reviewable draft cheaply, and the checks catch most of its mistakes. **On the guess vs 4 correction — he's right, and here's the deeper point:**

The 1-6 scale is a scale of UNDERSTANDING and DURABILITY, not of outcome. A multiple-choice guess severs the link between the outcome (the letter you picked) and your understanding. If you guess and it's right, the outcome says "right" but your understanding is a 1. If the pupil then self-rates honestly, they'd say 1 — but there's a temptation, having seen they got it right, to inflate to a 4 or 5. So the scale relies on the pupil being honest and sophisticated enough to rate their understanding, not their result.

4 specifically: "got it right, but it's not stable — I might miss it tomorrow." This is a pupil who UNDERSTOOD it (genuinely, today) but knows their grasp is fragile — it's the feeling of "I followed it, I could do it now, but ask me next week and I'm not sure it'll still be there." That's a real and important state, especially in exam prep where timing and repetition matter. It's NOT a guess. A guesser doesn't understand it today either. So 4 presupposes today-understanding plus tomorrow-doubt. A guess is no-understanding-today. Completely different. I was wrong to blur them.

So the guess question is more fundamental: it's asking "did you actually know this, or did you gamble?" And it needs to be asked in a way that a lucky guesser can't hide behind the right answer.

**On before/after — this is the clever move, and here's why:**

A single after-rating has a contamination problem: once you've seen the answer and the markscheme, your memory of how you felt before gets rewritten. You think "oh yes, I basically knew that," when actually you didn't. Hindsight bias. The "3" tries to capture the transition ("I got it wrong but now I get it"), but it's a single after-the-fact judgement that asks the pupil to reconstruct their prior state, which they're bad at.

A genuine before-rating, captured BEFORE they reveal the answer, freezes the prior state honestly. Then the after-rating captures the post-markscheme state. The PAIR is the data. And from the pair, several things fall out:

1. The guess is exposed. Before: "no idea" (1). They pick an answer. It's right. After: "okay I see why now." The before-1 tells you it was a guess regardless of the right letter. You can't fake a before-rating because you haven't seen the answer yet.

2. The "3" becomes a transition, not a bucket. Before low + after "I get it now" IS the 3. So you might not need 3 as a standalone option; it's the name for a particular before→after path. He said exactly this: "The 3 then disappears... 3 is supposed to be that: 'Okay, I understand it now.'" He's recognising that 3 is really a delta, a movement, and a before/after instrument captures the movement directly rather than asking the pupil to label it.

3. Overconfidence is exposed. Before: "I'm solid on this" (5). They get it wrong. That's a calibration signal — they thought they knew and didn't. That's arguably the most valuable signal for exam prep, because it's the dangerous case (the pupil who thinks they're fine and isn't).

4. The durable-5 vs fragile-4 distinction gets sharper too, potentially, if you add a time dimension — but that's the "might miss it tomorrow" which is forward-looking and can't be captured in a single sitting except by the pupil's own prediction.

Viewer.prototype._elimChips = function (m, labels) {
  const text = m.eliminates || "";
  if (!text) return null;
  // green: the letter the method lands on / leaves
  let green = null;
  const gm = text.match(/(?:lands(?:\s+\w+)?\s+on|straight\s+to|leaving|leaves(?:\s+only)?|everything\s+but|kills?\s+everything\s+but)\s*([A-H])\b/i);
  if (gm) green = gm[1].toUpperCase();
  // red: standalone letters in list contexts
  const red = {};
  let mm; const re = /(?:^|[\s,&(\/])([A-H])(?=[\s,&)\/.;]|$)/g;
  while ((mm = re.exec(text)) !== null) { const L = mm[1].toUpperCase(); if (L !== green) red[L] = true; }
  if (!green && !Object.keys(red).length) return null; // unparseable, prose only
  const wrap = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-elim" });
  labels.forEach((L) => {
    let cls = "ppq-iq-elim-chip";
    if (green === L) cls += " land"; else if (red[L]) cls += " out"; else cls += " dim";
    wrap.appendChild(el("span", { class: cls }, esc(L)));
  });
  return wrap;
};
```

718	  Viewer.prototype._renderInterrogationFeedback = function (box) {
719	    const fbBox = box.querySelector(".ppq-iq-feedback");
720	    if (!fbBox) return;

722	    if (!fb) { fbBox.innerHTML = ""; return; }
723	    fbBox.innerHTML = "";

725	  };

727	  Viewer.prototype._matchInterrogationFeedback = function () {
728	    const rec = this._analysis;
729	    if (!rec || !rec.feedback) return null;
730	    const chosen = this._chosenLabel, isRight = this._wasRight, sr = this._analysisSelfReports;
731	    for (let i = 0; i < rec.feedback.length; i++) {
732	      const fb = rec.feedback[i];
733	      let onOk = false;
734	      if (fb.on === "any_wrong") onOk = isRight === false;
735	      else if (fb.on === "any_correct") onOk = isRight === true;
736	      else if (fb.on && fb.on.indexOf("option:") === 0) onOk = fb.on.slice(7).toUpperCase() === chosen;
737	      else if (!fb.on) onOk = true;
738	      if (!onOk) continue;
739	      if (this._interrogationWhenMatches(fb.when, sr)) return fb;
740	    }
741	    return null;
742	  };

744	  Viewer.prototype._interrogationWhenMatches = function (when, sr) {
745	    if (!when) return true;
746	    const ci = when.indexOf(":");
747	    if (ci > 0) {
748	      const state = when.slice(0, ci), ref = when.slice(ci + 1);
749	      /* Direct: the learner's reported state for the prompted method_ref. */
750	      if (sr[ref] === state) return true;
751	      /* NOTE-TO-SELF 3 (rough): feedback may reference a method by KIND rather than
752	         by the prompted method_ref, e.g. when:"used:full_solve". full_solve is the
753	         default route, so infer it was used when the learner did NOT report taking a
754	         prompted shortcut. Reconcile with misconceptions_core.yaml, do not keep. */
755	      const rec = this._analysis;
756	      if (rec && rec.methods && state === "used" && ref === "full_solve") {
757	        const isKind = rec.methods.some((m) => m.kind === "full_solve");
758	        if (isKind) {
759	          const tookShortcut = Object.keys(sr).some((k) => sr[k] === "used" || sr[k] === "saw_and_used");
760	          return !tookShortcut;
761	        }
762	      }
763	      return false;
764	    }
765	    /* NOTE-TO-SELF 3: bare derived flag (e.g. did_not_sketch). Crude prefix match on
766	       the state's first two tokens. Replace with misconceptions_core.yaml look-up. */
767	    for (const ref in sr) {
768	      const st = sr[ref];
769	      const prefix = String(st).split("_").slice(0, 2).join("_");
770	      if (prefix && when.indexOf(prefix) === 0) return true;
771	    }
772	    return false;
773	  };

Viewer.prototype._renderInterrogation = function () {
    const cfg = this.cfg;
    /* QoderWork 2026-07-22: the interrogation now opens as a POP-UP (modal) rather
       than sitting a long way down the page (Smith: "it gets lost a long way down
       there"). It reuses the image-zoom modal shell. */

    if (!rec) return; /* graceful absence: most questions have no analysis yet */
    this._analysis = rec;
    this._analysisSelfReports = {};

    const STATE_LABELS = {
      used: "I used this",
      saw_and_used: "Saw it, used it",
      saw_and_discarded: "Saw it, didn't use it",
      barely_considered: "Barely considered it",
      did_not_see: "Didn't see it",
      saw_and_got_stuck: "Tried it, got stuck"
    };

    const iq = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq" });
    iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-title" }, "What this question is really about"));

    /* --- the probe --- */
    if (rec.probe && rec.probe.text) {
      const probe = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-probe" });
      probe.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-probe-text" }, esc(rec.probe.text)));
      const chips = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-chips" });
      if (rec.probe.difficulty_source) chips.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-chip" }, "difficulty: " + esc(rec.probe.difficulty_source)));
      if (rec.probe.trick_type) chips.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-chip" }, esc(rec.probe.trick_type)));
      probe.appendChild(chips);
      iq.appendChild(probe);
    }

    /* --- the chosen option's error path --- */
    const chosen = this._chosenLabel;
    if (chosen && rec.options && rec.options.length) {
      const opt = rec.options.filter((o) => String(o.label).toUpperCase() === chosen)[0];
      if (opt && opt.error_path) {
        const op = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option " + (opt.is_correct ? "right" : "wrong") });
        op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-head" }, "You picked " + esc(opt.label) + (opt.is_correct ? " — the right answer" : "")));
        op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-path" }, esc(opt.error_path)));
        if (opt.misconception_slugs && opt.misconception_slugs.length) {
          const sl = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-slugs" });
          opt.misconception_slugs.forEach((s) => sl.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-slug" }, esc(s))));
          op.appendChild(sl);
        }
        iq.appendChild(op);
      }
    }

    /* --- methods, with red/green elimination chips + "Use this" --- */
    const labels = this._optionLabels(this.cur) || [];
    const correctLetter = (cfg.correctOf(this.cur) || "").toString().toUpperCase();
    if (rec.methods && rec.methods.length) {
      iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-subhead" }, "Ways through it"));
      const self = this;
      rec.methods.forEach((m) => {
        const md = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method" + (m.defeats_trap ? " quick" : "")});
        const head = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method-head" });
        head.appendChild(el("b", null, esc(m.id)));
        head.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-kind" }, esc(m.kind)));
        if (m.speed) head.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-speed" }, esc(m.speed)));
        if (m.defeats_trap) head.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-defeats" }, "beats the trap"));
        md.appendChild(head);
        md.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method-desc" }, esc(m.description)));
        /* red/green elimination chips (best-effort parse of the free-prose
           `eliminates` field — see _elimChips; analysts should add a structured

        /* "Use this" adoption tick (Smith: recommended method, can be ignored). */
        const use = el("button", { class: "ppq-iq-use" + (m.defeats_trap ? " recommended" : "") }, m.defeats_trap ? "Use this ✓" : "Use this");
        use.addEventListener("click", () => {
          use.classList.toggle("on");
          self._fireReport({ status: "interrogation", qtype: "method_adopt", extra_json: JSON.stringify({ method_id: m.id, method_ref: m.method_ref || m.id, adopted: use.classList.contains("on") }) });
        });
        md.appendChild(use);
        iq.appendChild(md);
      });
    }

    /* --- one primary self-report prompt (the shortcut-awareness ladder) --- */
    if (rec.self_report_prompts && rec.self_report_prompts.length) {
      const p = rec.self_report_prompts[0]; /* NOTE-TO-SELF 2: first only, for now */
      const pr = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-prompt" });
      pr.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-prompt-text" }, esc(p.prompt)));
      const states = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-states" });
      const self = this;
      (p.states || Object.keys(STATE_LABELS)).forEach((st) => {
        const b = el("button", { class: "ppq-iq-state", "data-state": st }, esc(STATE_LABELS[st] || st));
        b.addEventListener("click", () => {
          self._analysisSelfReports[p.method_ref] = st;
          states.querySelectorAll(".ppq-iq-state").forEach((x) => x.classList.remove("sel"));
          b.classList.add("sel");
          self._fireReport({ status: "interrogation", qtype: "self_report", extra_json: JSON.stringify({ method_ref: p.method_ref, state: st }) });
          self._renderInterrogationFeedback();
        });
        states.appendChild(b);
      });
      pr.appendChild(states);
      iq.appendChild(pr);

    /* --- feedback lands here --- */
    iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-feedback" }));

    /* --- optional "come back to this" flag (Smith: review / more like this) --- */
    const flag = el("button", { class: "ppq-iq-flag" }, "Flag this — come back / more like this");
    const self2 = this;
    flag.addEventListener("click", () => {
      flag.classList.toggle("on");
      flag.textContent = flag.classList.contains("on") ? "Flagged ✓ — we'll bring more like this" : "Flag this — come back / more like this";
      self2._fireReport({ status: "flag_review", qtype: "review_flag", extra_json: JSON.stringify({ flagged: flag.classList.contains("on") }) });
    });
    iq.appendChild(flag);

    /* --- mount into the modal shell and open --- */
    const body = this.q(".ppq-modal-body");
    body.innerHTML = "";
    body.appendChild(iq);
    this.q(".ppq-modal").classList.add("show");
    this._iqBox = iq;
  };

Viewer.prototype._elimChipsEl = function (m, labels, correctLetter) {
    const wrap = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-elim" });
    const txt = (m.eliminates || "").toString();
    if (!txt && !m.defeats_trap) return wrap; /* nothing to show */

    /* green = the letter this method lands on / takes you straight to */
    let green = [];
    const gMatch = txt.match(/(?:lands?\s+(?:\w+\s+)?on|(?:goes?|takes?\s+you)?\s*straight\s+to|leav(?:es|ing|e)(?:\s+only)?|down\s+to|narrows?\s+to|everything\s+but|all\s+but|kills?\s+everything\s+but)\s*([A-H])\b/i);
    if (gMatch) green.push(gMatch[1].toUpperCase());
    /* a trap-beating method with no explicit letter lands on the right answer */
    if (!green.length && m.defeats_trap && correctLetter) green.push(correctLetter);

    /* red = letters this method kills. Two heuristics: a parenthesised letter
       list, and an explicit elimination verb. */
    let red = [];
    const addRed = (L) => { L = (L || "").toUpperCase(); if (L && red.indexOf(L) < 0 && green.indexOf(L) < 0) red.push(L); };
    const paren = txt.match(/\(([A-H](?:\s*[,\/&]\s*[A-H])*)\)/g) || [];
    paren.forEach((g) => { (g.match(/[A-H]/g) || []).forEach(addRed); });
    let vm;
    const verbRe = /(?:rules?\s+out|kills?|eliminates?|removes?|discards?|excludes?|cuts?\s+out)\s+([A-H](?:\s*(?:,|\/|&|and)\s*[A-H])*)/gi;
    while ((vm = verbRe.exec(txt)) !== null) { (vm[1].match(/[A-H]/g) || []).forEach(addRed); }

    /* "narrows to one" phrasing means everything not landed-on is killed */
    const narrows = /(?:everything\s+but|all\s+but|leav(?:es|ing|e)\s+only|down\s+to|narrows?\s+to|kills?\s+everything\s+but)/i.test(txt);
    if (narrows && green.length) {
      labels.forEach((L) => { L = String(L).toUpperCase(); if (green.indexOf(L) < 0 && red.indexOf(L) < 0) red.push(L); });
    }

    const parsed = green.length || red.length;
    if (!parsed) {
      /* couldn't parse any letters — show the raw prose rather than guess */
      if (txt) wrap.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-elim-prose" }, "rules out: " + esc(txt)));
      return wrap;
    }

    const row = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-elim-row" });
    (labels.length ? labels : []).forEach((L) => {
      L = String(L).toUpperCase();
      let cls = "dim";
      if (red.indexOf(L) >= 0) cls = "red";
      else if (green.indexOf(L) >= 0) cls = "green";
      row.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-elim " + cls }, L));
    });
    wrap.appendChild(row);
    /* keep the prose alongside as a footnote when we had to interpret it */
    if (txt) wrap.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-elim-prose" }, esc(txt)));
    return wrap;
  };

#### Tool: Bash

```bash
node -e "
const fs=require('fs');const p='C:/Claude (not on Gdrive, nor OneDrive)/ESAT Prep App/data/analysis/';
const files=['esat_engaa_2016_s1.js','esat_nsaa_2016_s1.js','esat_engaa_2017_s1.js','esat_nsaa_2017_s1.js','esat_nsaa_2018_s1.js'];
let all=[];files.forEach(f=>{let s=fs.readFileSync(p+f,'utf8');s=s.replace(/window\.ESAT_ANALYSIS_\w+\s*=/,'globalThis.X=');eval(s);(globalThis.X||[]).forEach(r=>{(r.methods||[]).forEach(m=>all.push(m.eliminates||''));});});
function parse(txt){
  const green=[];
  const gMatch=txt.match(/(?:lands?\s+(?:\w+\s+)?on|(?:goes?|takes?\s+you)?\s*straight\s+to|leav(?:es|ing|e)(?:\s+only)?|down\s+to|narrows?\s+to|everything\s+but|all\s+but|kills?\s+everything\s+but)\s*([A-H])\b/i);
  if(gMatch)green.push(gMatch[1].toUpperCase());
  const red=[];
  const addRed=(L)=>{L=(L||'').toUpperCase();if(L&&red.indexOf(L)<0&&green.indexOf(L)<0)red.push(L);};
  (txt.match(/\(([A-H](?:\s*[,\/&]\s*[A-H])*)\)/g)||[]).forEach(g=>{(g.match(/[A-H]/g)||[]).forEach(addRed);});
  const verbRe=/(?:rules?\s+out|kills?|eliminates?|removes?|discards?|excludes?|cuts?\s+out)\s+([A-H](?:\s*(?:,|\/|&|and)\s*[A-H])*)/gi;
  let vm;while((vm=verbRe.exec(txt))!==null){(vm[1].match(/[A-H]/g)||[]).forEach(addRed);}
  const narrows=/(?:everything\s+but|all\s+but|leav(?:es|ing|e)\s+only|down\s+to|narrows?\s+to|kills?\s+everything\s+but)/i.test(txt);
  return {green:red.length||green.length?green:green,red,narrows,parsed:green.length||red.length};
}
let parsedCount=0,proseCount=0;
all.forEach((t,i)=>{const r=parse(t);if(r.parsed)parsedCount++;else proseCount++;});
console.log('parsed (chips):',parsedCount,'/ 128 ; prose fallback:',proseCount);
console.log('--- first 25 with result ---');
all.slice(0,25).forEach((t,i)=>{const r=parse(t);console.log(i+': G=['+r.green+'] R=['+r.red+']'+(r.narrows?' (narrows)':'')+(r.parsed?'':'  PROSE')+'  <= '+JSON.stringify(t));});
"
```

183	      if (item && item.type === "mcq" && Array.isArray(item.choices)) {
184	        return String(item.choices[item.answer_index] !== undefined ? item.choices[item.answer_index] : "");
185	      }
186	      const mp = item && item.markpoints && item.markpoints[0];
187	      const ph = mp && mp.any_phrases && mp.any_phrases[0];
188	      return typeof ph === "string" ? ph : (ph && ph.phrase) || "";
189	    } catch (e) { return ""; }
190	  }
191	
192	  function firstBucketRoot(result) {
193	    const mp = result && result.markpoints && result.markpoints[0];
194	    return mp && mp.bucket ? String(mp.bucket).split(".")[0] : "";
195	  }
196	
197	  function reportAttempt(strand, item, result, attempt) {
198	    try { post(buildAttemptPayload(strand, item, result, attempt)); } catch (e) { /* never break marking */ }
199	  }
200	
201	  function sendSessionStart() {
202	    try {
203	      const payload = basePayload();
204	      payload.item_id = ""; payload.topic = ""; payload.qtype = ""; payload.mode = "";
205	      payload.level = ""; payload.picked_id = ""; payload.misconception_id = "";
206	      payload.status = "session_start";
207	      payload.build = LL.build || "";
208	      post(payload);
209	    } catch (e) {}
210	  }
211	
212	  // Log out = clear the LINGUICS class only (the gate reasks; the shared
213	  // name + anonymous_id stay, so physics is untouched and the name prefills).
214	  function signOut() {
215	    try { localStorage.removeItem(COHORT_KEY); } catch (e) {}
216	  }
217	
218	  LL.pulse = {
219	    classes: () => INTERIM_CLASSES.slice(),
220	    identity, signedIn, signIn, signOut, onStatus, reportAttempt, sendSessionStart,
221	    _buildAttemptPayload: buildAttemptPayload,   // exposed for the test harness
222	    _statusFor: statusFor
223	  };
224	})();
