Design of `example/ppq-login.js`:

```js
/* ppq-login.js — estate shared sign-in + attempt pulse for ppqviewer comparison pages.
   Adopts the estate's shared login (EdTech packet: shared_login_and_pulse_adoption):
   - one shared Apps Script endpoint, one workbook; project tag routes to its own tab;
   - identity SHARED with the physics drillers via localStorage smithics_fields_identity_v1
     (anonymous_id + display_name common); cohort SCOPED per page (held under its own key,
     never written into the shared object), sent as `cohort` on every POST;
   - class comes from a supplied dropdown list (interim hardcoded until TeacherViewer M2 doGet);
   - fail-soft: a pulse must never break the viewer. */
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var REPORT_URL = "https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbwQ2NxNi-AWGCpBVDa6nT9DDYsS66F53ENZvtZozDwuWkKaivqgLaGUyjSFd_InJ4Kt/exec";
  var SHARED_IDENTITY_KEY = "smithics_fields_identity_v1"; // estate-wide shared identity

  function uuid() { try { return crypto.randomUUID(); } catch (e) {
    return "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx".replace(/[xy]/g, function (c) {
      var r = Math.random() * 16 | 0; return (c === "x" ? r : (r & 0x3 | 0x8)).toString(16); }); } }

  function readShared() { try { var o = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(SHARED_IDENTITY_KEY)); return (o && typeof o === "object") ? o : {}; } catch (e) { return {}; } }
  function writeShared(o) { try { localStorage.setItem(SHARED_IDENTITY_KEY, JSON.stringify(o)); } catch (e) {} }

  function sessionId() { try { var s = sessionStorage.getItem("ppq_session_id"); if (!s) { s = uuid(); sessionStorage.setItem("ppq_session_id", s); } return s; } catch (e) { return "no-session-storage"; } }

  // A login instance is scoped to one page (one project tag + one cohort key + one class list).
  function createLogin(opts) {
    var projectTag = opts.projectTag;
    var cohortKey = opts.cohortKey;           // e.g. "ppqviewer_esat_cohort_v1"
    var classes = opts.classes || [];          // interim supplied list
    var identity = null;                        // {anonymous_id, display_name, cohort}

    function cohort() { try { return localStorage.getItem(cohortKey) || ""; } catch (e) { return ""; } }
    function current() {
      var sh = readShared();
      return { anonymous_id: sh.anonymous_id || "", display_name: sh.display_name || "", cohort: cohort() };
    }
    function signedIn() { var id = current(); return !!(id.display_name && id.cohort); }

    function post(payload) {
      if (!REPORT_URL || REPORT_URL.indexOf("script.google.com") === -1) return;
      try {
        fetch(REPORT_URL, { method: "POST", mode: "no-cors",
          headers: { "Content-Type": "text/plain;charset=utf-8" },
          body: JSON.stringify(payload), keepalive: true })
          .then(function () { flash("sent"); }).catch(function () { flash("offline"); });
      } catch (e) { flash("offline"); }
    }
    function flash(msg) { if (opts.onStatus) { try { opts.onStatus(msg); } catch (e) {} } }

    function basePayload() {
      var id = current();
      return { project: projectTag, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        anonymous_id: id.anonymous_id, display_name: id.display_name, cohort: id.cohort,
        google_email: "", session_id: sessionId() };
    }
    function report(partial) { if (!signedIn()) return; post(Object.assign(basePayload(), partial || {})); }
    function sendSessionStart() {
      var p = basePayload();
      p.item_id = ""; p.topic = ""; p.qtype = ""; p.mode = "ppq_viewer"; p.level = "";
      p.status = "session_start"; p.picked_id = ""; p.misconception_id = "";
      post(p);
    }

    // Sign in: preserve every unknown key in the shared object (physics drillers);
    // never touch shared.cohort (that's the physics class); our cohort lives under cohortKey.
    function signIn(displayName, cohortVal) {
      var sh = readShared();
      if (!sh.anonymous_id) sh.anonymous_id = uuid();
      sh.display_name = String(displayName || "").trim();
      if (sh.google_email === undefined) sh.google_email = "";
      writeShared(sh);
      try { localStorage.setItem(cohortKey, String(cohortVal || "")); } catch (e) {}
      sendSessionStart();
      return current();
    }
    function signOut() { try { localStorage.removeItem(cohortKey); } catch (e) {} } // keep shared name+id

    // Wire a gate: name input (pre-filled from shared identity), class <select>, start button.
    function wireGate(els, onEnter) {
      // pre-fill name from the shared estate identity (signed in once across drillers)
      var sh = readShared();
      if (els.name && sh.display_name) els.name.value = sh.display_name;
      // build the class dropdown from the supplied list
      if (els.classSelect) {
        els.classSelect.innerHTML = "";
        var ph = document.createElement("option"); ph.value = ""; ph.textContent = "Choose your class…"; els.classSelect.appendChild(ph);
        classes.forEach(function (c) { var o = document.createElement("option"); o.value = c; o.textContent = c; els.classSelect.appendChild(o); });
        var pre = cohort(); if (pre) els.classSelect.value = pre;
      }
      if (els.start) els.start.addEventListener("click", function () {
        var name = els.name ? els.name.value.trim() : "";
        var cls = els.classSelect ? els.classSelect.value : "";
        if (!name) { if (els.name) els.name.focus(); return; }
        if (!cls) { if (els.classSelect) els.classSelect.focus(); return; }
        signIn(name, cls);
        if (onEnter) onEnter(current());
      });
    }

    return { current: current, signedIn: signedIn, signIn: signIn, signOut: signOut,
             report: report, sendSessionStart: sendSessionStart, wireGate: wireGate, classes: classes };
  }

  window.PPQLogin = { createLogin: createLogin };
})();
```

```js
    /* ===== Backend wiring: shared estate Apps Script endpoint ===== */
    var REPORT_URL  = "https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbwQ2NxNi-AWGCpBVDa6nT9DDYsS66F53ENZvtZozDwuWkKaivqgLaGUyjSFd_InJ4Kt/exec";

    var IDENTITY    = null;

    function flash(msg) {
      var el = document.getElementById("report-flash");
      if (!el) return;
      el.textContent = msg; el.style.opacity = "1";
      setTimeout(function () { el.style.opacity = "0"; }, 1500);
    }

    function report(partial) {
      if (!REPORT_URL || REPORT_URL.indexOf("script.google.com") === -1) return;
      if (!IDENTITY) return;
      var payload = Object.assign({
        project: PROJECT_TAG, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        anonymous_id: IDENTITY.anonymous_id, display_name: IDENTITY.display_name,
        cohort: IDENTITY.cohort, google_email: "",

        level: "", status: "", picked_id: "", misconception_id: ""
      }, partial || {});
      try {
        fetch(REPORT_URL, { method: "POST", mode: "no-cors",
          headers: { "Content-Type": "text/plain;charset=utf-8" },
          body: JSON.stringify(payload), keepalive: true })
          .then(function () { flash("sent"); })
          .catch(function () { flash("offline"); });
      } catch (e) { /* best-effort */ }
    }

    /* ===== Sign-in gate ===== */
    var saved = null;
    try { saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_KEY)); } catch (e) {}
    if (saved && saved.display_name) { IDENTITY = saved; enterApp(); }

    document.getElementById("si-start").addEventListener("click", function () {
      var name = document.getElementById("si-name").value.trim();
      var cohort = document.getElementById("si-class").value.trim();
      if (!name) { document.getElementById("si-name").focus(); return; }
      IDENTITY = {
        display_name: name,
        cohort: cohort || "unknown",
        anonymous_id: "ppq_" + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)
      };
      localStorage.setItem(LS_KEY, JSON.stringify(IDENTITY));
      enterApp();
      report({ status: "session_start" });
    });

    function enterApp() {
      document.getElementById("sign-in-gate").style.display = "none";
      document.getElementById("ppq-root").style.display = "block";
      mountViewer();
    }
```

```js
Viewer.prototype._commitTimer = function () {
  this._stopTimer();
  const t = this.cfg.timer;
  if (!t) { this._timerCtx = null; return; }
  const elapsed = Date.now() - this.shownAt;
  let ctx = { time_ms: elapsed };
  if (t.mode === "down") {
    const budget = this._qBudgetMs || (t.perQuestionSec * 1000);
    const remaining = budget - elapsed;
    ctx.time_remaining_ms = Math.max(0, remaining);
    ctx.time_pressure = remaining <= 0 ? "forced" : (remaining <= t.pressureSec * 1000 ? "tight" : "ok");
    if (t.banking) this._timeBankMs = Math.max(0, (this._timeBankMs || 0) + (budget - elapsed) - (this._qBankAtStart||0));
  }
  this._timerCtx = ctx;
};
```

Hmm, the bank update is getting tangled. Let me simplify the bank model:
- `this._timeBankMs` = current pool.
- At question start (`_startTimer`): `this._qBudgetMs = t.perQuestionSec*1000 + this._timeBankMs`.
- On commit: surplus = this._qBudgetMs - elapsed ... no wait. The budget includes the bank. If I add (budget - elapsed) back to the bank, I'm double-counting the bank.

Let me redefine cleanly:
- Pool `this._timeBankMs` (carries forward).
- Per-question allocation `alloc = t.perQuestionSec*1000`.
- At question start: available = alloc + pool. Snapshot `this._qBudgetMs = available`.
- On commit after `elapsed`:
  - If elapsed <= alloc: surplus = alloc - elapsed; pool += surplus. (Finished within allocation → bank the surplus.)
  - If elapsed > alloc: deficit = elapsed - alloc; pool = max(0, pool - deficit). (Overran → draw down the bank.)
  - Equivalent: pool = max(0, pool + (alloc - elapsed)).
- Display during question: remaining = this._qBudgetMs - elapsed = (alloc + pool_at_start) - elapsed.

So: `this._timeBankMs = Math.max(0, this._timeBankMs + (alloc - elapsed));` where alloc = perQuestionSec*1000. Clean. The pool only changes on commit.

Let me verify: pool=0, alloc=90s. Q1 answered in 30s → pool = 0 + (90-30) = 60s. Q2 budget = 90+60=150s. Q2 answered in 120s → pool = 60 + (90-120) = 60-30=30s. Q3 budget=90+30=120s. Good — time saved on Q1 let Q2 overrun, and the pool tracks correctly.

Edge case: pool can't go negative (max 0). If a question overruns beyond alloc+pool, remaining hits 0 (forced), and the pool drains to 0. Good.

Next, `_startTimer()`:
```js
Viewer.prototype._startTimer = function () {
  this._stopTimer();
  const t = this.cfg.timer;
  const tel = this.q(".ppq-timer");
  if (!t) { if (tel) tel.style.display = "none"; return; }
  if (this._timeBankMs == null) this._timeBankMs = (t.bankSec || 0) * 1000;
  const alloc = t.perQuestionSec * 1000;
  this._qBudgetMs = (t.mode === "down") ? alloc + this._timeBankMs : 0;
  // prominence
  if (tel) {
    tel.className = "ppq-timer ppq-timer--" + t.prominence;
    tel.style.display = (t.prominence === "hidden") ? "none" : "";
    tel.textContent = "";
  }
  const self = this;
  this._tickTimer();
  this._timerInterval = setInterval(function () { self._tickTimer(); }, 250);
};
```

`_tickTimer()`:
```js
Viewer.prototype._tickTimer = function () {
  const t = this.cfg.timer; const tel = this.q(".ppq-timer");
  if (!t || !tel || t.prominence === "hidden") return;
  const elapsed = Date.now() - this.shownAt;
  if (t.mode === "down") {
    const remaining = (this._qBudgetMs || 0) - elapsed;
    tel.textContent = this._fmtClock(Math.max(0, remaining));
    tel.classList.toggle("ppq-timer--tight", remaining <= t.pressureSec * 1000);
    tel.classList.toggle("ppq-timer--forced", remaining <= 0);
  } else {
    tel.textContent = this._fmtClock(elapsed);
  }
};
```

`_fmtClock(ms)`:
```js
Viewer.prototype._fmtClock = function (ms) {
  const s = Math.floor(ms / 1000);
  const m = Math.floor(s / 60);
  const r = s % 60;
  return m + ":" + (r < 10 ? "0" : "") + r;
};
```

`_stopTimer()`:
```js
Viewer.prototype._stopTimer = function () {
  if (this._timerInterval) { clearInterval(this._timerInterval); this._timerInterval = null; }
};
```

```json
  // --------------------------------------------------------------- exam timer (module, QoderWork 2026-07-22)
  /* Silent capture (time_ms) is always on; this is the optional visible clock plus
     time-banking plus the time-pressure context. All methods no-op unless
     config.timer is set. NOTE-TO-SELF: per-question allocation is a single
     perQuestionSec for every question — ESAT may want per-subject/per-paper
     budgets; banking is a simple surplus-carries-forward pool (floored at 0). */
  Viewer.prototype._startTimer = function () {
    this._stopTimer();
    const t = this.cfg.timer;
    const tel = this.q(".ppq-timer");
    if (!t) { if (tel) tel.style.display = "none"; return; }
    if (this._timeBankMs == null) this._timeBankMs = (t.bankSec || 0) * 1000;
    const alloc = t.perQuestionSec * 1000;
    this._qBudgetMs = (t.mode === "down") ? alloc + this._timeBankMs : 0;
    this._timerCtx = null;
    if (tel) {
      tel.className = "ppq-timer ppq-timer--" + t.prominence;
      tel.style.display = (t.prominence === "hidden") ? "none" : "";
      tel.textContent = "";
    }
    const self = this;
    this._tickTimer();
    this._timerInterval = setInterval(function () { self._tickTimer(); }, 250);
  };
  Viewer.prototype._stopTimer = function () {
    if (this._timerInterval) { clearInterval(this._timerInterval); this._timerInterval = null; }
  };
  Viewer.prototype._tickTimer = function () {
    const t = this.cfg.timer;
    const tel = this.q(".ppq-timer");
    if (!t || !tel || t.prominence === "hidden") return;
    const elapsed = Date.now() - this.shownAt;
    if (t.mode === "down") {
      const remaining = (this._qBudgetMs || 0) - elapsed;
      tel.textContent = this._fmtClock(Math.max(0, remaining));
      tel.classList.toggle("ppq-timer--forced", remaining <= 0);
      tel.classList.toggle("ppq-timer--tight", remaining > 0 && remaining <= t.pressureSec * 1000);
    } else {
      tel.textContent = this._fmtClock(elapsed);
    }
  };
  Viewer.prototype._fmtClock = function (ms) {
    const s = Math.max(0, Math.floor(ms / 1000));
    const m = Math.floor(s / 60);
    const r = s % 60;
    return m + ":" + (r < 10 ? "0" : "") + r;
  };
  Viewer.prototype._commitTimer = function () {
    this._stopTimer();
    const t = this.cfg.timer;
    if (!t) { this._timerCtx = null; return; }
    const elapsed = Date.now() - this.shownAt;
    const ctx = { time_ms: elapsed };
    if (t.mode === "down") {
      const alloc = t.perQuestionSec * 1000;
      const remaining = (this._qBudgetMs || alloc) - elapsed;
      ctx.time_remaining_ms = Math.max(0, remaining);
      ctx.time_pressure = remaining <= 0 ? "forced" : (remaining <= t.pressureSec * 1000 ? "tight" : "ok");
      /* banking: time saved under the allocation carries forward; overrunning draws
         the bank down (floored at 0). */
      if (t.banking) this._timeBankMs = Math.max(0, (this._timeBankMs || 0) + (alloc - elapsed));
    }
    this._timerCtx = ctx;
  };
```

```json
/* QoderWork 2026-07-22: optional exam timer (config.timer). Silent time capture is
   always on; this is the visible clock. "prominence" is the in-your-face-ness axis:
   subtle = small, tucked right, muted; prominent = large, centred, boxed; hidden is
   handled inline (no clock, still records). tight/forced warn as the clock runs out. */
.ppq-timer { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.ppq-timer--subtle { align-self: flex-end; font-size: 0.95rem; color: var(--ppq-muted); margin-top: -0.6rem; }
.ppq-timer--prominent { align-self: center; font-size: 1.9rem; color: var(--ppq-ink); padding: 0.25rem 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--ppq-line); border-radius: 12px; background: var(--ppq-bg); margin-top: -0.4rem; }
.ppq-timer--tight { color: var(--ppq-bad); }
.ppq-timer--forced { color: var(--ppq-bad); animation: ppq-timer-pulse 1s ease-in-out infinite; }
@keyframes ppq-timer-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.35; } }
```

#### Tool: Bash

```bash
node -e "
// replicate _commitTimer banking + pressure logic
function sim(perQuestionSec, pressureSec, answers){
  let bank=0; const alloc=perQuestionSec*1000; const log=[];
  answers.forEach((elapsedSec,i)=>{
    const elapsed=elapsedSec*1000;
    const budget=alloc+bank;
    const remaining=budget-elapsed;
    const pressure=remaining<=0?'forced':(remaining<=pressureSec*1000?'tight':'ok');
    bank=Math.max(0,bank+(alloc-elapsed));
    log.push('Q'+(i+1)+': answered in '+elapsedSec+'s, budget '+(budget/1000)+'s, remaining '+(Math.max(0,remaining)/1000).toFixed(1)+'s -> '+pressure+'; bank now '+(bank/1000)+'s');
  });
  return log;
}
console.log('=== 90s/question, banking, 10s pressure ===');
sim(90,10,[30,120,85,95]).forEach(l=>console.log(l));
console.log('');
console.log('=== guess-like: 8s answer with plenty of clock ===');
sim(90,10,[8]).forEach(l=>console.log(l));
"
```

```json
Q2: answered in 120s, budget 150s, remaining 30.0s -> ok; bank now 30s
Q3: answered in 85s, budget 120s, remaining 35.0s -> ok; bank now 35s
Q4: answered in 95s, budget 125s, remaining 30.0s -> ok; bank now 30s

=== guess-like: 8s answer with plenty of clock ===
Q1: answered in 8s, budget 90s, remaining 82.0s -> ok; bank now 82s
```

#### Thinking

The logic is working correctly:
- Q1: Answered in 30 seconds → 60 seconds deposited into the bank.
- Q2: Budget 150 seconds (90 + 60 banked), answered in 120 seconds (exceeded the 90-second allocation by drawing down the bank) → remaining 30 seconds, bank decreased to 30 seconds.
- An 8-second answer with 82 seconds remaining → "ok" pressure, meaning downstream it reads as "answered fast with plenty of time left" — this is the ambiguous case (either knew it, or guessed), and it's distinguished from "forced" (0 seconds remaining). This is exactly the nuance Smith wanted: a fast answer records the time-remaining context, so it's not blindly treated as a guess, and a forced answer (0 seconds remaining) is flagged as "forced".

The time-pressure context captures this: an 8-second answer with 82 seconds remaining → time_pressure "ok", time_remaining_ms 82000. A forced answer → time_pressure "forced", time_remaining_ms 0. Downstream guess detection can use this.

```json
# CHANGELOG: ppqviewer

Universal engine changes are recorded here and notified into each consumer's inbox. Newest at the top.

## 2026-07-22 (QoderWork, latest) — estate shared login + exam timer with guess-disambiguation (v0.2.3)
Two additions, both driven by Smith. No storage/schema change; the attempt row shape is untouched (new fields ride in `extra_json`).

### Estate shared login (the tracking-system bridge, NOT a new auth tier)
- New shared module `example/ppq-login.js` exposing `window.PPQLogin.createLogin({projectTag, cohortKey, classes, onStatus})`. It replicates the exact mechanism Linguics adopted from the EdTech Overview shared-login spec — it does NOT invent a new system.
- Identity is SHARED across the whole estate via the localStorage key `smithics_fields_identity_v1` (`{anonymous_id, display_name, google_email}`), so a pupil's name prefills on every driller. `google_email` stays empty estate-wide (real Google-OAuth is the teacher-read tier, not this).
- Cohort/class is SCOPED per page (its own `cohortKey`, never written into the shared identity object — that holds the pupil's physics class). Class is chosen from a supplied DROPDOWN.
- On sign-in it fires a `session_start` row; every event POSTs to the one shared `teacher-tracking.gs` endpoint with the page's `project` tag (`ppqviewer_esat` / `ppqviewer_chemistry`), which the script routes to its own tab automatically (no redeploy). Fail-soft: the pulse never breaks the app (sent/offline flash only).
- POST pattern is the estate standard: `text/plain` + `no-cors` + `keepalive` (Apps Script rejects preflighted JSON; the response is opaque, so "sent" means dispatched, not confirmed).
- Wired into BOTH comparison pages: `esat-compare.html` (`ppqviewer_esat` / `ppqviewer_esat_cohort_v1`) and `chem-compare.html` (`ppqviewer_chemistry` / `ppqviewer_chem_cohort_v1`). The old inline identity/report/gate code in each page was deleted and replaced by the shared module.
- FLAG FOR SMITH: the class dropdowns use INTERIM hardcoded lists — ESAT `["Test","Y12 ESAT","Y13 ESAT"]`, Chemistry `["Test","Y10 Chemistry","Y11 Chemistry"]`. Give me the real class names and I'll swap them; when TeacherViewer milestone M2 ships its single-source `doGet`, point the dropdown at that instead.

### Exam timer (the feature that tells a fast answer apart from a guess)
- New optional `config.timer` = `{mode:"up"|"down", perQuestionSec, banking, bankSec, prominence:"hidden"|"subtle"|"prominent", pressureSec}`. Off unless supplied. Wired into `esat-compare.html` as `{mode:"down", perQuestionSec:90, banking:true, prominence:"subtle", pressureSec:10}`.
- Silent capture is ALWAYS on (the engine already records `time_ms`); the timer config only governs whether a visible clock is shown and how prominent it is. `prominence:"hidden"` records everything and shows nothing — per Smith's earlier "avoid surfacing the time" preference.
- Time-banking (down mode): surplus time carries forward into a pool floored at 0. Answer Q1 in 30s of a 90s budget → +60s banked; Q2's budget becomes 150s.
- Guess-disambiguation (Smith's point: "people guess after 10 minutes of thought; these kids would only guess with 8 seconds if they really only had 8 seconds left"). A fast answer is AMBIGUOUS — instant knowledge vs. ran out of clock — so the engine records the CONTEXT of the speed, not just the speed. On every "answered" report, `extra_json` now also carries `time_remaining_ms` and `time_pressure`: `"forced"` (clock at/below 0), `"tight"` (≤ pressureSec left), or `"ok"` (plenty left). An 8s answer with 82s on the clock logs `"ok"`; an 8s answer at 0s logs `"forced"` — downstream analysis can now separate a confident snap from a desperate guess.
- Visible clock styles: `--subtle` (small, muted, top-right) and `--prominent` (large, boxed, centred); `--tight` recolours, `--forced` recolours + pulses.
```

**Login** — I used the estate's shared system, not a new one. There's now a small shared module, `example/ppq-login.js`, that does exactly what Linguics does: one shared identity across all drillers (`smithics_fields_identity_v1`, so the pupil's name prefills everywhere), class chosen from a dropdown and kept scoped to the page, a `session_start` row on sign-in, and every event posted to the one `teacher-tracking.gs` endpoint with a `project` tag that routes itself to its own tab. **Timer** — this is the guess-disambiguation you described. The clock itself is optional and has three prominence levels (`hidden` / `subtle` / `prominent`); `hidden` records everything and shows nothing, matching your "don't surface the time" preference. The key part: every answer now logs not just `time_ms` but `time_remaining_ms` and a `time_pressure` tag — `forced` (clock at zero), `tight`, or `ok`. So an 8-second answer with 82 seconds still on the clock logs `ok` (a confident snap), while an 8-second answer at 0 seconds logs `forced` (a desperate guess). Down mode also does time-banking — surplus carries forward, floored at zero. ESAT is wired with `90s/question, banking on, subtle, 10s pressure`.

Everything passes `node --check` and both pages' inline scripts parse clean. CHANGELOG has a v0.2.3 entry.

Now I've got the full picture. The method descriptions are short one-liners containing algebra like "Subtract 6, x(-2) with flip => 28 > x." — Smith finds the algebra hard to read and wants multiple lines. The descriptions contain commas and "=>" — I can split on "," / ";" / "=>" to lay out the steps vertically. Good approach: split the description on `,`, `;`, `=>`, and render each fragment as its own line (step-style). "Subtract 6, x(-2) with flip => 28 > x." → lines: "Subtract 6" / "x(-2) with flip" / "28 > x". That's much more readable. Render as `.ppq-iq-method-line` divs, maybe with a bullet/arrow. Split on comma and semicolon and "=>", preserving the "=>" as an arrow at the start of the line. Simple: split on /[,;]|\s*=>\s*/, and for "=>" prepend "⇒ " to the following fragment. Let's implement:

```js
function methodLines(desc) {
  const parts = String(desc || "").split(/[,;]|\s*=>\s*/);
  ...
}
```
But I need to track whether the separator was "=>" in order to render the arrow. Simpler: first replace "=>" with " ⇒ ", then split on /[,;]/, trim each fragment, filter out empties, and render each as a line. If the fragment starts with "⇒", style it as a result line. Good enough as a first pass that half-works.

Wait — but some descriptions might have commas inside meaningful units... e.g. "Add x/2 first: x/2 < 14 => x < 28, no negative multiply, no flip." → lines: "Add x/2 first: x/2 < 14" / "⇒ x < 28" / "no negative multiply" / "no flip". Readable. OK.

All the necessary information is in place. Now to implement. The change list for the engine `ppqviewer.js`:

**1. `_buildDom`** — multi-filter support + defaultOrder:
- Inside the `cfg.filters.forEach` loop: if `f.multi` → build a multi-filter widget instead of a select. Give it `data-fidx` so filterQuestions can read it. Store the selection state in `this._multiSel[i]` (null = all, otherwise a Set).
- After orderSel is built: `if (cfg.defaultOrder === "shuffle") orderSel.value = "shuffle";`

Multi-filter widget structure:
```js
const wrap = el("div", { class: "ppq-multifilter", "data-fidx": i });
const btn = el("button", { class: "ppq-select ppq-multi-btn", type: "button" }, summary);
const panel = el("div", { class: "ppq-multi-panel", style: "display:none;" });
// "All" checkbox + one per value
```
Wait — `.ppq-select` has a change listener attached via `this.qa(".ppq-select")` — button elements don't fire change, so it's safe. But `filterQuestions` reads `this.q('.ppq-select[data-fidx="' + i + '"]').value` — in the multi case we need to branch. Let me restructure filterQuestions:

```js
const self = this;
...
this.view = this.questions.filter((qq) => {
  for (let i = 0; i < cfg.filters.length; i++) {
    const f = cfg.filters[i];
    if (f.multi) {
      const set = self._multiSel[i];
      if (set && !set.has(String(qq[f.field]))) return false;
    } else {
      const v = this.q('.ppq-select[data-fidx="' + i + '"]').value || "ALL";
      if (v !== "ALL" && String(qq[f.field]) !== v) return false;
    }
  }
  ...
```

Multi-filter behaviour:
- `_multiSel[i]` initialisation: `f.default ? new Set(f.default.map(String)) : null`.
- Panel checkboxes: "All" checkbox (checked when set is null) + each value. Checking "All" → set to null, uncheck the others. Checking a value → if set is null, set = new Set(all values except...? hmm). Standard behaviour: when "All" is on and the user checks a specific box... Let's do this: individual check → if set==null, set = new Set([that value])? Feels weird — they'd uncheck everything else. Better UX: "All" is a shortcut: clicking All selects everything (set=null means all). Individual checkboxes reflect membership: when set==null all are checked. Unchecking one while all are checked → set = all minus that one. Checking one while in null state can't happen (already checked). Simple and predictable.
- Button label: set==null → allLabel; otherwise join friendly labels with " + " (if more than 3, show "3 selected"?). Keep the join; ESAT has 4 subjects, default 2 → "Maths + Physics".
- On change: update label, `self.groupFilter = null; self.filterQuestions();`
- Toggle the panel on button click. Close on outside click: add a document listener once — or more simply: leave the panel open until the button is clicked again? Add a small document-click close in _wireControls: `document.addEventListener("click", e => { if (!e.target.closest(".ppq-multifilter")) hide all panels })`. `closest` is fine in modern browsers.

**2. `filterQuestions`** — as above; plus a counter chip for the active groupFilter:
```js
let counterHtml = this.view.length + " questions";
if (this.groupFilter) counterHtml += ' · <button class="ppq-filterchip" title="Clear topic filter">' + esc(this._groupFilterLabel || this.groupFilter) + " ✕</button>";
this.q(".ppq-counter").innerHTML = counterHtml;
```
And wire the chip's click (delegate on the counter): inside _wireControls: `this.q(".ppq-counter").addEventListener("click", (e) => { if (e.target.closest(".ppq-filterchip")) { self.groupFilter = null; self.filterQuestions(); } });`

**3. `setGroupFilter`** — grab the label:
```js
Viewer.prototype.setGroupFilter = function (key) {
  this.groupFilter = (this.groupFilter === key) ? null : key;
  if (this.groupFilter) {
    const catEl = this.q('.ppq-cat[data-key="' + key + '"] .ppq-cat-name');
    this._groupFilterLabel = catEl ? catEl.textContent.replace(/\(\d+\)\s*$/, "").trim() : key;
  } else { this._groupFilterLabel = null; }
  this.filterQuestions();
};
```
Note: data-key inside the attribute — the key is a topic code like "P3" — safe.

**4. `_showEmpty`** — richer:
```js
Viewer.prototype._showEmpty = function (msg) {

  this.q(".ppq-card").style.display = "none";

};
Viewer.prototype.clearAllFilters = function () {
  this.groupFilter = null; this._groupFilterLabel = null;

  cfg.filters.forEach((f, i) => { if (f.multi) { this._multiSel[i] = null; this._syncMultiFilter(i); } });
  this.filterQuestions();
};
```

```js
Viewer.prototype.closeModal = function () {

    }
  }
};
```

```js
Viewer.prototype._methodLinesEl = function (desc) {
  const box = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method-desc" });

  parts.forEach(p => box.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method-line" + (p.indexOf("⇒") === 0 ? " result" : "") }, esc(p))));
  return box;
};
```

```js
  Viewer.prototype._renderInterrogation = function () {
    const cfg = this.cfg;
    /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (v0.2.4 pass, based on Smith's live review):
       - never reveal right/wrong (no judgment on the option you picked),
       - lay out the solution method line by line (the algebra was hard to read),
       - a "used it" checkbox on every method (replaces the single 6-choice ladder and the one green "Use this"),
       - no "beats the trap" / "~15s" labels (Smith: "I don't know what beat the trap means"),
       - the 1-6 self-evaluation now lives inside the popup (it used to be "outside"),
         and the popup has its own Next. If you close the popup without finishing,
         the outer 1-6 row comes back so you're never stuck. */
    if (!cfg.modules.postQuestionReview || !cfg.analysisOf) return;
    const rec = cfg.analysisOf(this.cur);
    if (!rec) return; /* graceful absence: most problems don't have an analysis yet */
    this._analysis = rec;
    this._analysisSelfReports = {};

    const self = this;
    const iq = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq" });
    iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-title" }, "What this question is really about"));

    /* --- probe --- */
    if (rec.probe && rec.probe.text) {
      const probe = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-probe" });
      probe.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-probe-text" }, esc(rec.probe.text)));
      const chips = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-chips" });
      if (rec.probe.difficulty_source) chips.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-chip" }, "difficulty: " + esc(rec.probe.difficulty_source)));
      if (rec.probe.trick_type) chips.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-chip" }, esc(rec.probe.trick_type)));
      probe.appendChild(chips);
      iq.appendChild(probe);
    }

    /* --- the path of the option you picked, neutral (never say right/wrong) --- */
    const chosen = this._chosenLabel;
    if (chosen && rec.options && rec.options.length) {
```

```json
  Viewer.prototype._bindGlobalKeys = function () {
    const self = this;
    this._keyHandler = function (e) {
      if (!self.cur || !self._shouldHandleKey(e)) return;
      if (self.q(".ppq-modal").classList.contains("show") && e.key === "Escape") { self.closeModal(); return; }
      /* QoderWork 2026-07-22: while the interrogation pop-up holds the 1-6, route
         Enter/number keys to the pop-up and close it before arrow-navigating. */
      if (self._iqOpen) {
        if (e.key === "Enter") { const nb = self._iqBox && self._iqBox.querySelector(".ppq-iq-next"); if (nb && nb.style.display !== "none") nb.click(); return; }
        if (e.key === "ArrowLeft" || e.key === "ArrowRight") { self.closeModal(); }
      }
      if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") { self.prev(); return; }
      if (e.key === "ArrowRight") { self.next(); return; }
      if (e.key === "s" || e.key === "S") { if (!self.answered) self.skip(); return; }
      if (e.key === "r" || e.key === "R") { if (!self.answered && (self._curType === "flashcard" || self._curType === "imageSelfMark")) self.reveal(); return; }
      if (e.key === "Enter") { if (self.answered) self.next(); else if (self._curType === "flashcard") self.reveal(); return; }
```

Hmm, the interaction between the All checkbox and the individual checkboxes. Let me define the semantics clearly:
- `_multiSel[i] === null` → all (no filter). UI: All is checked, all individuals also checked.
- Otherwise it's a Set of selected values. UI: All is unchecked, individuals are checked according to membership.

Change handling:
- If the change was on the All checkbox and it became checked → set to null.
- If All became unchecked → set = currently checked individuals (if all individuals are checked → keep null? if the user unchecks All while all individuals are checked... they probably want to deselect everything? Ambiguous. Simpler: All is a pure shortcut: checking All → null (select all). Unchecking All → set to the checked individuals as-is (no change, since all are checked → set of all values = effectively all, but displayed as explicit selection). Hmm, then the filter would be a set of all values — functionally identical to all. Fine.
- If the change was on an individual: if All was checked (state null) → new set = all values except the one that was unchecked? No wait: if state is null (all checked, all individuals visually checked) and the user unchecks value X → they want "everything except X": set = all values minus X. If state is a Set and the user toggles X → add/remove; if the set ends up containing all values → collapse to null (All checked).
- After computing the new state: `_multiSel[i] = newState; self._syncMultiFilter(i); self.groupFilter = null; self.filterQuestions();`

```js
  Viewer.prototype._syncMultiFilter = function (i) {
    const cfg = this.cfg;
    const f = cfg.filters[i];
    const wrap = this.q('.ppq-multifilter[data-fidx="' + i + '"]');
    if (!wrap) return;

    });
    wrap.querySelector(".ppq-multi-btn").textContent = (set == null) ? allLabel + " ▾" : (chosen.join(" + ") + " ▾");
  };
```

```js
    const cfg = this.cfg;
    const self = this;
    const order = this.q(".ppq-order").value || "order";
    const start = parseInt(this.q(".ppq-start").value, 10) || 1;
    this.view = this.questions.filter((qq) => {
      for (let i = 0; i < cfg.filters.length; i++) {
        const f = cfg.filters[i];
```

```json
        else { const v = self.q('.ppq-select[data-fidx="' + i + '"]').value || "ALL"; if (v !== "ALL" && String(qq[f.field]) !== v) return false; }
      }
      if (this.groupFilter && cfg.groupKey(qq) !== this.groupFilter) return false;
      return true;
    });
    if (order === "shuffle") { shuffleInPlace(this.view); this.idx = -1; }
    else {
      const cmp = cfg.sort || function (a, b) { return String(cfg.idOf(a)).localeCompare(String(cfg.idOf(b)), undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: "base" }); };
      this.view.sort(cmp);
      this.idx = (start > 1 && start <= this.view.length) ? start - 2 : -1;

    this.q(".ppq-counter").innerHTML = counterHtml;
    this.next();

  Viewer.prototype.setGroupFilter = function (key) {
    this.groupFilter = (this.groupFilter === key) ? null : key;
    if (this.groupFilter) {
      const nameEl = this.q('.ppq-cat[data-key="' + key + '"] .ppq-cat-name');
      this._groupFilterLabel = nameEl ? nameEl.textContent.replace(/\(\d+\)\s*$/, "").trim() : key;
```

```json
# CHANGELOG: ppqviewer

Universal engine changes are recorded here and notified into each consumer's inbox. Newest at the top.

## 2026-07-22 (QoderWork, latest) — Smith's live-review pass: no verdicts, "wasn't sure", pop-up rebuild, shuffle + Maths&Physics default, count-up timer, stuck-filter fix (v0.2.4)
Engine + stylesheet + esat-compare wiring. All of it from Smith talking through the running page. chem-compare is untouched (every change is opt-in config, so it keeps today's behaviour).

### Never tell them right or wrong (Smith: "the most important thing")
- New `config.revealCorrect` (default true, so existing consumers are unchanged). esat-compare sets it `false`: picking an answer no longer colours correct/incorrect, the answer line says "Answer saved." instead of "Correct, X / Marked wrong", the pop-up shows the chosen option NEUTRALLY (no "— the right answer", no red/green border), and the mastery ribbon shows a neutral dot per attempt instead of ✔/✘. Correctness is still RECORDED in every attempt row — only the display is suppressed. The voluntary Reveal button is untouched (pupil-initiated).

### NEW "Actually, I wasn't sure" (uncertainty confession)
- After answering, an option sits to the RIGHT of the answer line: "Actually, I wasn't sure". Tapping it opens letter chips ("I thought it was…") so the pupil can mark the options they were torn between — "I thought it was B or D" — then Done. Fires `status:"interrogation", qtype:"unsure"` with `{unsure:true, wavering:["B","D"]}`. This is the lucky-guess detector: it works even when the answer was right, and independently of speed.

### Pop-up rebuild (from Smith talking through it)
- Methods are set out on MULTIPLE LINES — the one-line algebra was "quite hard to read". Split on commas/semicolons; "=>" becomes a "⇒ …" result line. On the 128 ESAT methods, 117 now break into lines. (NOTE-TO-SELF: a real per-method `steps:[…]` field would beat this regex pass.)
- Every method gets a little "used it" TICKBOX (multi-select across methods), replacing the single 6-state shortcut-awareness ladder and the one green "Use this" button ("I don't know why one is green and one's not"). Fires `qtype:"self_report"` with `state:"used"/"not_used"` per method.
- "beats the trap" and the "~15s" speed labels are GONE ("I don't know what beat the trap means could you please get rid of this 15 second stuff"). All methods now look equal.
- A small encouraging line under "Ways through it": there's more than one route, collecting alternatives is the point.
- The 1-6 self-rating now lives INSIDE the pop-up ("that one, two, three, four, five, six is back outside. Probably should be inside it there"), with its own "Next question →" button. The outer 1-6 row is hidden while the pop-up is open; closing the pop-up early (×/Escape/outside) brings it back so nobody is stranded, syncing any rating picked inside. Keyboard: Enter advances from the pop-up once rated, 1-6 rate inside it, arrows close it then navigate.

### Filters + timer (esat-compare)
- Shuffle is now the STANDARD order (`config.defaultOrder:"shuffle"`).
- The subject filter is a new multi-select DROPDOWN defaulting to Maths + Physics (Smith teaches both now); Chemistry and Biology are a tick away in the same dropdown. Engine support: any filter may set `multi:true` + `default:[…]`; ticking everything collapses back to "All".
- The exam timer now counts UP ("you're counting down, no, count up… and just to have a log of how long"): a subtle elapsed clock, and every answer records `time_ms`. The down mode (banking + forced/tight/ok pressure tags) stays in the engine for later.
- STUCK FILTER FIXED: Smith clicked P3 Mechanics (a physics topic) while filtered to maths, got "No questions match these filters", and couldn't see the filter was on or how to undo it. Now the active topic filter shows as a removable chip next to the question counter ("P3 Mechanics ✕"), the empty state names the stuck filter and offers "Clear all filters", and the active mastery category is highlighted more loudly.

### Deferred (noted, not built)
- A first analysis page (the mastery dashboard exists; the new unsure/used-it/flag/timing events give it more to show) — next pass.
- Probe/method/slug wording is still analyst-facing (Smith: "that will be fixed, that's not your problem").

- Identity is SHARED across the whole estate via the localStorage key `smithics_fields_identity_v1` (`{anonymous_id, display_name, google_email}`), so a pupil's name prefills on every driller. `google_email` stays empty estate-wide (real Google-OAuth is the teacher-read tier, not this).
```

Done — that whole pass is built, verified, and in the CHANGELOG as v0.2.4. Everything you talked through, in order:

**Never tell them right or wrong.** On ESAT the app now shows no verdict anywhere: no green/red on the options, the answer line just says "Answer saved.", the pop-up shows your picked option neutrally, and the mastery panel shows plain dots instead of ticks and crosses. Correctness is still silently logged on every attempt — the teachers see it, the pupil never does. One judgment call to flag: I left the voluntary Reveal button alone, since that's the pupil deliberately asking; say the word and it goes too.

**"Actually, I wasn't sure".** To the right of the answer line there's now exactly that option. Tap it and it opens the letters — "I thought it was…" — they tick B and D, hit Done, and it logs `unsure` with the wavering letters. That's your lucky-guess catcher: it fires even when the answer was right, and it has nothing to do with how fast they were.

**The pop-up.** Methods now break onto multiple lines — commas and semicolons become line breaks and `=>` becomes a "⇒ …" result line; 117 of the 128 methods split cleanly. Every method has a little "used it" tickbox (multi-select — the single green one and the six-state ladder are gone), and "beats the trap" and the "~15s" labels are gone; all methods look equal now, with one small line saying there's more than one route through. The 1–6 is inside the pop-up with its own "Next question →"; if they bail out of the pop-up early, the old 1–6 row comes back underneath so nobody gets stranded.

**Filters and timer.** Shuffle is the standard. The subject filter is now a dropdown defaulting to Maths + Physics, with Chemistry and Biology a tick away in the same list. The timer counts up — a quiet elapsed clock, and every answer logs its time. And the stuck filter: the active topic now sits next to the question counter as a "P3 Mechanics ✕" chip you can remove in one click, and the "no questions match" screen names the stuck filter and offers "Clear all filters".

Rough edges, stated plainly: the method line-splitting is a regex pass — a real `steps` field from the analysts would beat it; the probe/method/misconception wording is still analyst-facing (yours to fix, as agreed); the interim class lists on the login still need real names from you; and the first analysis page is noted as the next pass, not built. Let me carefully parse this correction from Smith.

"Oh, that was a miss. I never said we don't tell them right or wrong. I said that was a flaw, not that it was true."

So I misunderstood him. He wasn't saying "we mustn't tell them right or wrong." He was pointing out a flaw in the current design — namely, that the first thing shown after answering was "What is this question really about?" (the probe), which is abstract and off-point. The flaw was the ordering/framing, not the verdict itself.

"I was saying it wasn't the first thing being shown to them. Because the headline was 'What is this question really about?' That's a bit abstract and off-point."

So the actual complaint was: after answering, the first thing the popup shows is "What is this question really about?" — which is abstract. The right/wrong verdict should be told to them (it's fine, even desirable), but it wasn't the first thing — the abstract probe headline was first.

"No, do tell them what it's about." — tell them right/wrong. So revert revealCorrect:false — ESAT should show the verdict.

"There is a question, and the question is: do we force it? There was probably a general thing, I think: do we want pre-declared guesses, or post-declared guesses?"

This is a design question he's raising: do we force pupils to declare "I'm guessing" before answering (pre-declare), or ask them afterwards whether they guessed (post-declare)? This connects to the "Actually, I wasn't sure" feature I built (that's a post-declaration). He's musing about whether guess-declaration should be pre- or post-answer. This is an open question — he's not asking me to build pre-declaration now. He's flagging it as a design decision to consider (and probably to ask the analyst about too).

Right. My mistake on the verdict thing — I read your "we can't tell them" as an instruction to suppress right/wrong entirely, when you were identifying the *fault*: the abstract "What is this question really about?" headline landing before they even know whether they got it right. Corrected now (v0.2.5): verdicts are on, and the verdict block ("You picked B — the answer is G", red/green border) leads the pop-up ahead of the probe. The `revealCorrect` switch stays in the engine as an opt-in for a future test mode, but ESAT doesn't set it.

**Pre- vs post-declare guesses.** What's built is post-declare: after they see the verdict, "Actually, I wasn't sure" lets them confess and pick the letters they were torn between. The alternative (pre-declare) would be a "I'm guessing here" checkbox *before* they lock in their answer. Post-declare is harder to game (they've already seen whether they're right, so the confession is honest reflection rather than hedging), but pre-declare captures the raw moment of uncertainty before outcome knowledge contaminates it. Worth the analyst's view on which produces more useful data — or whether both, at different points, serve different purposes.

**Can you just send the HTML?** No — the live page pulls in the engine JS/CSS via relative paths, the catalogue, five analysis-store files, and the question images via absolute `file:///` paths on your machine. None of that travels with the HTML. Instead I've generated a single self-contained file (208 kB, no external dependencies, opens from anywhere) that renders all 33 analysed questions exactly as the pop-up shows them — verdict blocks, probes, methods with the multi-line split and red/green elimination chips, feedback — grouped by paper. It also has a "What we need from you" section at the top with the six asks:

1. Structured `eliminates: ["A","C","F"]` + `lands_on: "G"` per method (the regex stopgap only parses 67/128).
2. Per-method `steps: […]` arrays for proper multi-line layout control.
3. Pupil-facing wording for probes, methods, and misconception slugs (raw identifiers like `inequality_sign_flip_omitted` are currently shown verbatim).
4. Feedback review: strip praise (estate voice), reconcile `when` grammar with the "used it" tickbox model, check `fires` alignment with misconceptions_core.yaml.
5. Error-path content for correct options (currently describes the solution method — should it be a "why it's right" note or blank?).
6. Their view on pre-declare vs post-declare guesses.

Send them `analyst-preview.html` — it's in `ppqviewer/example/` and I've also put a copy here:

```json
  Viewer.prototype._populateGuessPanel = function (labels) {

    (labels || []).forEach((L) => {

  /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (v0.2.6): redistribute guess percentages. If `changed`
     is null (a checkbox was toggled), split 100 equally among ticked options.
     If `changed` is a specific input, adjust the OTHERS proportionally so the
     total stays 100. Smith: "if they tick 2, 50/50… they can use a little slider
     to increase or type in a bigger number. It will automatically decrease the
     other numbers proportionally." */
  Viewer.prototype._guessRedistribute = function (changed) {
    const rows = this.qa(".ppq-guess-row");
    const ticked = [];
    rows.forEach((r) => {
      const cb = r.querySelector("input[type=checkbox]");
      const pct = r.querySelector(".ppq-guess-pct");
      pct.disabled = !cb.checked;
      if (cb.checked) ticked.push({ cb: cb, pct: pct, row: r });
    });
    if (!ticked.length) return;
    if (!changed) {
      /* equal split */
      const share = Math.floor(100 / ticked.length);
      const remainder = 100 - share * ticked.length;
      ticked.forEach((t, i) => { t.pct.value = String(share + (i < remainder ? 1 : 0)); });
    } else {
      /* proportional adjustment of the others */
      const newVal = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, parseInt(changed.value, 10) || 0));
      changed.value = String(newVal);
      const others = ticked.filter((t) => t.pct !== changed);
      if (!others.length) return;
      const oldOthersTotal = others.reduce((s, t) => s + (parseInt(t.pct.value, 10) || 0), 0);
      const newOthersTotal = 100 - newVal;
      if (oldOthersTotal === 0) {
        /* others were all zero; split equally */
        const share = Math.floor(newOthersTotal / others.length);
        const rem = newOthersTotal - share * others.length;
        others.forEach((t, i) => { t.pct.value = String(share + (i < rem ? 1 : 0)); });
      } else {
        let allocated = 0;
        others.forEach((t, i) => {
          if (i === others.length - 1) { t.pct.value = String(newOthersTotal - allocated); }
          else {
            const v = Math.round((parseInt(t.pct.value, 10) || 0) / oldOthersTotal * newOthersTotal);
            t.pct.value = String(Math.max(0, v));
            allocated += v;
          }
        });
      }
    }
  };
```

- Exposes `window.ESAT_ANALYSIS_V2.records`, `.by_id`, `.interaction_defaults`

- Render v2 fields directly:
  - insight: `pupil_analysis.first_notice`, `why_it_matters`, `next_move`

  - green chip: `methods[].lands_on`

- Don't regex-parse v2 steps or eliminations
- Don't show internal fields (error_tags, category paths, mechanism codes, diagnostic confidence, difficulty chips, strategy tags)
- The "used it" button stays as supplementary evidence

- Faithfully render the provided v2 pupil fields, don't rewrite the voice
- Don't add a JS cleanup layer for praise/jargon/tone
- The viewer owns the generic interface chrome

Let me write the largest-remainder allocator first:

```js
/* Largest-remainder allocation: distribute `total` integer units among n slots
   proportionally to `weights`, each slot getting at least `minEach`. Returns an
   array of non-negative integers summing exactly to total. */
function allocateLargestRemainder(total, weights, minEach) {
  const n = weights.length;
  if (!n) return [];
  minEach = minEach || 0;
  const base = minEach * n;
  let pool = total - base;
  if (pool < 0) { pool = 0; }  // can't satisfy minEach; caller should clamp
  const wSum = weights.reduce((s, w) => s + w, 0);
  let alloc;
  if (wSum <= 0) {
    // equal split of pool
    const share = Math.floor(pool / n);
    let rem = pool - share * n;
    alloc = weights.map(() => share);
    for (let i = 0; i < n && rem > 0; i++) { alloc[i]++; rem--; }
  } else {
    const ideal = weights.map((w) => (w / wSum) * pool);
    alloc = ideal.map((x) => Math.floor(x));
    let rem = pool - alloc.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0);
    // order by fractional part descending
    const order = ideal.map((x, i) => ({ i: i, frac: x - Math.floor(x) })).sort((a, b) => b.frac - a.frac);
    for (let k = 0; k < order.length && rem > 0; k++) { alloc[order[k].i]++; rem--; }
  }
  return alloc.map((x) => x + minEach);
}
```

This guarantees non-negative values and that the sum is exactly total (as long as pool >= 0).

- distribute remaining among others proportionally to their current values, each ≥ 1

```json
  /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (analyst handoff): largest-remainder allocation. Spread
     `total` integer units over the slots proportionally to `weights`, each slot
     getting at least `minEach`. Always returns non-negative integers summing to
     exactly `total` (when total >= minEach*n). Replaces the old proportional
     pass that could drive the final option negative. */
  function allocateLargestRemainder(total, weights, minEach) {
    const n = weights.length;
    if (!n) return [];
    minEach = minEach || 0;
    let pool = total - minEach * n;
    if (pool < 0) pool = 0;
    const wSum = weights.reduce((s, w) => s + (w > 0 ? w : 0), 0);
    let alloc;
    if (wSum <= 0) {
      const share = Math.floor(pool / n);
      let rem = pool - share * n;
      alloc = weights.map(() => share);
      for (let i = 0; rem > 0 && i < n; i++) { alloc[i]++; rem--; }
    } else {
      const ideal = weights.map((w) => ((w > 0 ? w : 0) / wSum) * pool);
      alloc = ideal.map((x) => Math.floor(x));
      let rem = pool - alloc.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0);
      const order = ideal.map((x, i) => ({ i: i, frac: x - Math.floor(x) })).sort((a, b) => b.frac - a.frac);
      for (let k = 0; rem > 0 && k < order.length; k++) { alloc[order[k].i]++; rem--; }
    }
    return alloc.map((x) => x + minEach);
  }

  /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (analyst handoff): the prompt/label text for a guess
     stage. Prefers the analysis-v2 interaction_defaults; falls back to the
     settled strings ("I'm guessing" / "Actually, it was a guess"). */
  Viewer.prototype._guessPrompt = function (stage) {
    const d = this.cfg.guessDefaults && this.cfg.guessDefaults[stage];
    if (stage === "pre_answer") return (d && d.candidate_prompt) || "Which options are still in the running?";
    return (d && d.candidate_prompt) || "Which options were still in the running?";
  };
  Viewer.prototype._guessLabel = function (stage) {
    const d = this.cfg.guessDefaults && this.cfg.guessDefaults[stage];
    if (stage === "pre_answer") return (d && d.label) || "I'm guessing";
    return (d && d.label) || "Actually, it was a guess";
  };

  /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (analyst handoff): shared guess picker used by BOTH the
     pre-answer widget and the post-answer correction inside the modal.
     opts: { labels, preselect, stage, prompt, onDone(payload), onSkip() }.
     Percentages are OPTIONAL, behind an "Add percentages (optional)" control.
     Done validates (>=2 options; if percentages, each >=1 and sum exactly 100)
     and keeps the panel open with an inline message on failure. */
  Viewer.prototype._buildGuessPicker = function (opts) {
    const self = this;
    const MIN_EACH = 1, SUM = 100, MIN_OPTIONS = 2;
    const labels = (opts.labels || []).map(String);
    const panel = el("div", { class: "ppq-gpick" });
    panel.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-gpick-prompt" }, esc(opts.prompt || "")));

    const rows = {};
    const optsBox = el("div", { class: "ppq-gpick-options" });
    labels.forEach((L) => {
      const row = el("label", { class: "ppq-gpick-row" });
      const cb = el("input", { type: "checkbox", value: L });
      if ((opts.preselect || []).indexOf(L) >= 0) cb.checked = true;
      row.appendChild(cb);
      row.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-gpick-letter" }, esc(L)));
      const wrap = el("span", { class: "ppq-gpick-pctwrap", style: "display:none;" });
      const pct = el("input", { type: "number", class: "ppq-gpick-pct", min: String(MIN_EACH), max: String(SUM), value: "0", disabled: "disabled" });
      wrap.appendChild(pct);
      wrap.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-gpick-pctsign" }, "%"));
      row.appendChild(wrap);
      optsBox.appendChild(row);
      rows[L] = { cb: cb, pct: pct, wrap: wrap };
    });
    panel.appendChild(optsBox);

    const msg = el("div", { class: "ppq-gpick-msg", style: "display:none;" });
    panel.appendChild(msg);

    let pctOn = false;
    const pctToggle = el("button", { class: "ppq-gpick-pcttoggle", type: "button" }, "Add percentages (optional)");
    panel.appendChild(pctToggle);

    function checked() { return labels.filter((L) => rows[L].cb.checked); }
    function showMsg(text) { msg.textContent = text; msg.style.display = text ? "" : "none"; }
    function refreshPct() {
      labels.forEach((L) => {
        const r = rows[L];
        r.wrap.style.display = pctOn ? "" : "none";
        r.pct.disabled = !(pctOn && r.cb.checked);
      });
    }
    function equalSplit() {
      const c = checked();
      const alloc = allocateLargestRemainder(SUM, c.map(() => 1), MIN_EACH);
      c.forEach((L, i) => { rows[L].pct.value = String(alloc[i]); });
    }
    function redistributeFrom(changedPct) {
      const c = checked();
      const others = c.filter((L) => rows[L].pct !== changedPct);
      const maxForChanged = SUM - others.length * MIN_EACH;
      let v = parseInt(changedPct.value, 10);
      if (isNaN(v)) v = MIN_EACH;
      v = Math.max(MIN_EACH, Math.min(maxForChanged, v));
      changedPct.value = String(v);
      const remaining = SUM - v;
      const weights = others.map((L) => parseInt(rows[L].pct.value, 10) || 0);
      const alloc = allocateLargestRemainder(remaining, weights, MIN_EACH);
      others.forEach((L, i) => { rows[L].pct.value = String(alloc[i]); });
    }

    optsBox.addEventListener("change", (e) => {
      if (e.target.type !== "checkbox") return;
      showMsg("");
      if (pctOn) {
        if (e.target.checked) { equalSplit(); }
        else { const c = checked(); if (c.length) { const alloc = allocateLargestRemainder(SUM, c.map(() => 1), MIN_EACH); c.forEach((L, i) => { rows[L].pct.value = String(alloc[i]); }); } }
      }
    });
    optsBox.addEventListener("input", (e) => {
      if (!e.target.classList.contains("ppq-gpick-pct")) return;
      showMsg("");
      redistributeFrom(e.target);
    });
    pctToggle.addEventListener("click", () => {
      pctOn = !pctOn;
      pctToggle.classList.toggle("on", pctOn);
      pctToggle.textContent = pctOn ? "Remove percentages" : "Add percentages (optional)";
      refreshPct();
      if (pctOn && checked().length) equalSplit();
      showMsg("");
    });

    const actions = el("div", { class: "ppq-gpick-actions" });
    const done = el("button", { class: "ppq-gpick-done", type: "button" }, "Done");
    const skip = el("button", { class: "ppq-gpick-skip", type: "button" }, "Skip");
    actions.appendChild(done);
    actions.appendChild(skip);
    panel.appendChild(actions);

    done.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const c = checked();
      if (c.length < MIN_OPTIONS) { showMsg("Pick at least " + MIN_OPTIONS + " options, or Skip."); return; }
      const payload = {
        guess_declared: true,
        declared_stage: opts.stage,
        candidate_options: c.slice(),
        attempt_id: self._attemptId || ""
      };
      if (pctOn) {
        const pcts = {};
        let sum = 0, ok = true;
        c.forEach((L) => {
          let v = parseInt(rows[L].pct.value, 10);
          if (isNaN(v) || v < MIN_EACH) ok = false;
          pcts[L] = isNaN(v) ? 0 : v;
          sum += pcts[L];
        });
        if (!ok || sum !== SUM) { showMsg("Percentages must each be at least " + MIN_EACH + " and total exactly " + SUM + "."); return; }
        payload.candidate_percentages = pcts;
      }
      showMsg("");
      if (opts.onDone) opts.onDone(payload);
    });
    skip.addEventListener("click", () => { showMsg(""); if (opts.onSkip) opts.onSkip(); });

    refreshPct();
    return panel;
  };

  /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (analyst handoff): store the pre-answer declaration on
     the instance, fire the event, and reflect it on the toggle button. The
     snapshot is later attached to the answer event and the stored attempt. */
  Viewer.prototype._commitPreGuess = function (payload) {
    this._preGuessDeclaration = payload;
    const btn = this.q(".ppq-guess-btn");
    btn.textContent = "Guessing: " + payload.candidate_options.join(", ") + " ✓";
    btn.classList.add("done");
    this._fireReport({ status: "interrogation", qtype: "guess_declaration", extra_json: JSON.stringify(payload) });
  };
```

Now I have a complete understanding of the v2 record structure. Let me organize the key fields to render:

**v2 record fields (for student-facing display):**
- `identity.correct_answer`, `identity.option_labels[]`
- `pupil_analysis.first_notice`, `why_it_matters`, `next_move`, `check_prompt`
- `options[].label`, `is_correct`, `error_path` (render this), `diagnostic_confidence` (hide), `error_tags` (hide), `bait`, `relations`
- `methods[].id`, `role`, `kind`, `title`, `pupil_steps[]` (render directly), `eliminates[]` (letters, red chip), `lands_on` (letter or null, green chip), `requires`, `useful_when`, `calculation_load`, `strategy_tags` (hide)
- `self_report_prompts[]`: `id`, `primary`, `method_refs[]`, `prompt`, `states[]`
- `requirements.post_question_checks[]`: `id`, `primary`, `requirement_refs[]`, `prompt`, `states[]`
- `feedback[]`: `id`, `selected_options[]`, `prompt_id`, `states[]`, `guess_declared` (optional bool), `text`

**Modal order (per the handoff):**
1. Concrete verdict (`You chose B — the answer is D`) — always render even if error_path is empty
2. Optional post-answer guess correction
3. Student insight (first_notice, why_it_matters, next_move)
4. Methods and structured eliminations
5. Primary self-report/check + matched feedback
6. 1-6 feeling rating and Next

**v2 feedback matching logic:**
- `selected_options[]`: matches if the chosen option is in the list
- `prompt_id`: matches the answered self-report prompt (null = no prompt constraint)
- `states[]`: matches the state the learner reported for that prompt (empty = no state constraint)
- `guess_declared`: optional bool — if true, matches only if a guess was declared (post-answer correction or pre-answer); if false, only if not declared; if absent, no constraint.

Let me think about feedback matching. The feedback items have:
- `selected_options`: array of option labels. If non-empty, the chosen option must be in it. If empty/absent, no constraint.
- `prompt_id`: references a self_report_prompt id. If set, the learner must have answered that prompt.
- `states`: array of states. If non-empty, the learner's reported state for that prompt must be in it.
- `guess_declared`: if `true`, a guess must have been declared (post-answer or pre-answer snapshot). If `false`, must not have been. If absent, no constraint.

So matching is:
```
for each fb in rec.feedback:
  if fb.selected_options && fb.selected_options.length && !fb.selected_options.includes(chosen): continue
  if fb.guess_declared === true && !guessDeclared: continue
  if fb.guess_declared === false && guessDeclared: continue
  if fb.prompt_id:
     state = selfReportStateForPrompt(fb.prompt_id)
     if !state: continue  // prompt not answered yet
     if fb.states && fb.states.length && !fb.states.includes(state): continue
  else:
     // no prompt constraint; states should be empty
  return fb
```

```
Viewer.prototype._renderInterrogation = function () {
  const cfg = this.cfg;
  if (!cfg.modules.postQuestionReview || !cfg.analysisOf) return;
  const rec = cfg.analysisOf(this.cur);
  if (!rec) return;
  this._analysis = rec;
  this._analysisSelfReports = {};
  this._promptStates = {};  // prompt_id -> selected state (for v2 feedback matching)

  const self = this;
  const iq = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq" });
  const isV2 = this._isV2(rec);

  const chosen = this._chosenLabel;
  const correctLetter = isV2
    ? String((rec.identity.correct_answer || "")).toUpperCase()
    : (cfg.correctOf(this.cur) || "").toString().toUpperCase();

  /* 1. Verdict first — always render even if error_path is empty */
  iq.appendChild(this._verdictEl(rec, isV2, chosen, correctLetter));

  /* 2. Post-answer guess correction (optional, non-blocking) */
  iq.appendChild(this._postGuessEl(chosen, correctLetter, isV2));

  if (isV2) {
    /* 3. Student insight */
    this._appendInsightV2(iq, rec);
    /* 4. Methods + structured eliminations */
    this._appendMethodsV2(iq, rec, correctLetter);
    /* 5. Primary self-report + knowledge check + feedback */
    this._appendSelfReportV2(iq, rec);
  } else {
    /* Legacy path — keep existing probe/methods rendering */
    ...
  }

  /* Feedback box (both paths) */
  iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-feedback" }));

  /* 6. 1-6 rating + Next (shared) */
  ...
};
```

Let me write `_verdictEl`:
```
Viewer.prototype._verdictEl = function (rec, isV2, chosen, correctLetter) {
  const box = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-verdict" });
  // Find the chosen option record
  let opt = null;
  if (chosen && rec.options && rec.options.length) {
    opt = rec.options.filter((o) => String(o.label).toUpperCase() === chosen)[0] || null;
  }
  const isRight = opt ? !!opt.is_correct : (chosen === correctLetter);
  const head = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option " + (isRight ? "right" : "wrong") });
  head.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-head" },
    "You chose " + esc(chosen || "?") + (isRight ? " — the right answer" : (correctLetter ? " — the answer is " + esc(correctLetter) : ""))));
  // Explanation is optional
  if (opt && opt.error_path) {
    head.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-path" }, esc(opt.error_path)));
  }
  box.appendChild(head);
  return box;
};
```

```json
536	
537	  /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (analyst handoff): largest-remainder allocation. Spread
538	     `total` integer units over the slots proportionally to `weights`, each slot
539	     getting at least `minEach`. Always returns non-negative integers summing to
540	     exactly `total` (when total >= minEach*n). Replaces the old proportional
541	     pass that could drive the final option negative. */
542	  function allocateLargestRemainder(total, weights, minEach) {
543	    const n = weights.length;
544	    if (!n) return [];
545	    minEach = minEach || 0;
546	    let pool = total - minEach * n;
547	    if (pool < 0) pool = 0;
548	    const wSum = weights.reduce((s, w) => s + (w > 0 ? w : 0), 0);
549	    let alloc;
550	    if (wSum <= 0) {
551	      const share = Math.floor(pool / n);
552	      let rem = pool - share * n;
553	      alloc = weights.map(() => share);
554	      for (let i = 0; rem > 0 && i < n; i++) { alloc[i]++; rem--; }
555	    } else {
556	      const ideal = weights.map((w) => ((w > 0 ? w : 0) / wSum) * pool);
557	      alloc = ideal.map((x) => Math.floor(x));
558	      let rem = pool - alloc.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0);
559	      const order = ideal.map((x, i) => ({ i: i, frac: x - Math.floor(x) })).sort((a, b) => b.frac - a.frac);
560	      for (let k = 0; rem > 0 && k < order.length; k++) { alloc[order[k].i]++; rem--; }
561	    }
562	    return alloc.map((x) => x + minEach);
563	  }
```

I'll restructure `_renderInterrogation` and add helpers. The main design:

1. `_isV2(rec)` — returns `!!(rec && rec.identity && rec.pupil_analysis)`.

2. `_renderInterrogation` — new ordering:
   - verdict (always)
   - post-answer guess correction (optional collapsible)
   - insight (v2) or probe (legacy)
   - methods (v2 structured or legacy)
   - self-report/check + feedback (v2) or feedback (legacy)

3. `_verdictEl(rec, isV2, chosen, correctLetter)` — always renders the verdict heading, error_path is optional.

4. `_postGuessEl(chosen, isRight)` — collapsible "Actually, it was a guess" button + panel using `_buildGuessPicker` with `stage:"post_answer"`, `preselect:[chosen]`. onDone → `_commitPostGuess`.

5. `_commitPostGuess(payload, chosen, isRight)` — adds `chosen_option` and `correct`, fires `qtype:"guess_declaration"`, sets `this._postGuessDeclared = true`, re-renders feedback.

6. v2 insight: `_appendInsightV2(iq, rec)` — renders first_notice, why_it_matters, next_move.

7. v2 methods: `_appendMethodsV2(iq, rec, labels)` — renders title + pupil_steps directly, eliminates[] as red chips, lands_on as green chip. No regex parsing. Keep the "used it" tickbox as supplementary.

8. v2 self-report: `_appendSelfReportV2(iq, rec)` — primary self_report_prompt + primary post_question_check, each with tappable state options. On selection, save to `this._promptStates[prompt_id]` and re-render feedback.

```
Viewer.prototype._matchFeedbackV2 = function (rec) {
  const chosen = this._chosenLabel;
  const guessDeclared = !!(this._postGuessDeclared || this._preGuessDeclaration);
  for (let i = 0; i < rec.feedback.length; i++) {
    const fb = rec.feedback[i];
    // selected_options constraint
    if (fb.selected_options && fb.selected_options.length) {
      const opts = fb.selected_options.map((o) => String(o).toUpperCase());
      if (opts.indexOf(String(chosen || "").toUpperCase()) < 0) continue;
    }
    // guess_declared constraint
    if (fb.guess_declared === true && !guessDeclared) continue;
    if (fb.guess_declared === false && guessDeclared) continue;
    // prompt_id + states constraint
    if (fb.prompt_id) {
      const st = this._promptStates[fb.prompt_id];
      if (!st) continue; // prompt not answered yet
      if (fb.states && fb.states.length && fb.states.indexOf(st) < 0) continue;
    }
    return fb;
  }
  return null;
};
```

Wait, there's a subtlety with feedback ordering and specificity. Feedback entries are checked in order, first match wins. The `correct_guess` entry has `guess_declared: true` and `selected_options: ["G"]`. The `correct_fragile_route` entry has `prompt_id` + `states`. If the learner picked G and declared a guess, `correct_guess` matches first (good). If they picked G, didn't guess, and reported `did_not_see` on the route prompt, `correct_fragile_route` matches. Good. The order in the array matters and the analyst has control over it. First-match-wins in array order is the right semantics.

```js
  Viewer.prototype._renderInterrogation = function () {
    const cfg = this.cfg;
    if (!cfg.modules.postQuestionReview || !cfg.analysisOf) return;
    const rec = cfg.analysisOf(this.cur);
    if (!rec) return; /* graceful absence: most questions have no analysis yet */
    this._analysis = rec;
    this._analysisSelfReports = {};
    this._promptStates = {}; /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (analyst handoff): prompt_id -> chosen state, drives v2 feedback */
    this._postGuessDeclared = false;

    const self = this;
    const isV2 = this._isV2(rec);
    const iq = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq" });

    const chosen = this._chosenLabel;
    const correctLetter = isV2
      ? String((rec.identity && rec.identity.correct_answer) || "").toUpperCase()
      : (cfg.correctOf(this.cur) || "").toString().toUpperCase();

    /* --- 1. the verdict FIRST and ALWAYS (analyst handoff): the concrete
       "You chose X — the answer is Y" leads. The error_path explanation beneath
       it is optional; the verdict line itself is not. --- */
    iq.appendChild(this._verdictEl(rec, isV2, chosen, correctLetter));

    /* --- 2. post-answer guess correction (optional, non-blocking). Sits right
       after the verdict so a guess can be on record BEFORE guess-aware feedback
       is matched. Replaces the outer "Actually, I wasn't sure" control. --- */
    iq.appendChild(this._postGuessEl(chosen, this._wasRight));

    if (isV2) {
      /* --- 3. the pupil insight (first_notice / why_it_matters / next_move) --- */
      this._appendInsightV2(iq, rec);
      /* --- 4. methods: title + structured pupil_steps + elimination chips --- */
      this._appendMethodsV2(iq, rec);
      /* --- 5. primary self-report + knowledge check (feed the feedback match) --- */
      this._appendSelfReportV2(iq, rec);
    } else {
      /* legacy analysis-store path (probe + free-prose methods) */
      this._appendProbeLegacy(iq, rec);
      this._appendMethodsLegacy(iq, rec, correctLetter);
    }

    /* --- feedback lands here (reacts to self-report + guess declaration) --- */
    iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-feedback" }));
    this._iqFeedbackEl = iq.querySelector(".ppq-iq-feedback");

    /* --- 6. the 1-6 self-rating, INSIDE the pop-up --- */
    ... (existing rating code) ...

    /* --- optional "come back to this" flag --- */
    ... (existing flag code) ...

    /* --- mount --- */
    ... (existing mount code) ...
  };
```

```js
     its identity + pupil_analysis blocks. Legacy analysis-store records have a
```

```js
  Viewer.prototype._verdictEl = function (rec, isV2, chosen, correctLetter) {
    const box = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-verdict" });
    let opt = null;
    if (chosen && rec.options && rec.options.length) {
      opt = rec.options.filter((o) => String(o.label).toUpperCase() === String(chosen).toUpperCase())[0] || null;
    }
    const isRight = opt ? !!opt.is_correct : (String(chosen).toUpperCase() === correctLetter);
    const op = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option " + (isRight ? "right" : "wrong") });
    op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-head" },
      "You chose " + esc(chosen || "?") +
      (isRight ? " — the right answer" : (correctLetter ? " — the answer is " + esc(correctLetter) : ""))));
    /* the explanation is optional; the verdict line above is not */
    if (opt && opt.error_path) op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-path" }, esc(opt.error_path)));
    /* legacy records carry misconception slugs on the option; v2 hides its tags */
    if (!isV2 && opt && opt.misconception_slugs && opt.misconception_slugs.length) {
      const sl = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-slugs" });
      opt.misconception_slugs.forEach((s) => sl.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-slug" }, esc(s))));
      op.appendChild(sl);
    }
    box.appendChild(op);
    return box;
  };
```

```js
  Viewer.prototype._postGuessEl = function (chosen, isRight) {
    const self = this;
    const wrap = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-postguess" });
    const labels = this._answerLabels && this._answerLabels.length ? this._answerLabels : (this._optionLabels(this.cur) || []);
    if (labels.length < 2) return wrap; /* nothing to declare between */
    const btn = el("button", { class: "ppq-iq-postguess-btn", type: "button" }, this._guessLabel("post_answer"));
    const panel = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-postguess-panel", style: "display:none;" });
    btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const showing = panel.style.display !== "none";
      if (!showing && !panel.childElementCount) {
        /* the chosen option stays IN the picker and starts selected (analyst
           handoff: preselect it, do not remove it). */
        panel.appendChild(self._buildGuessPicker({
          labels: labels,
          preselect: chosen ? [String(chosen).toUpperCase()] : [],
          stage: "post_answer",
          prompt: self._guessPrompt("post_answer"),
          onDone: (payload) => { self._commitPostGuess(payload, chosen, isRight); panel.style.display = "none"; btn.classList.remove("open"); },
          onSkip: () => { panel.style.display = "none"; btn.classList.remove("open"); }
        }));
      }
      panel.style.display = showing ? "none" : "";
      btn.classList.toggle("open", !showing);
    });
    wrap.appendChild(btn);
    wrap.appendChild(panel);
    return wrap;
  };
```

```js
  Viewer.prototype._commitPostGuess = function (payload, chosen, isRight) {
    /* the post-answer declaration additionally records the committed option and
       its result, independently of the candidate set (analyst handoff). */
    payload.chosen_option = String(chosen || "").toUpperCase();
    payload.correct = !!isRight;
    this._postGuessDeclared = true;
    this._postGuessDeclaration = payload;
    const btn = this._iqBox ? this._iqBox.querySelector(".ppq-iq-postguess-btn") : null;
    if (btn) { btn.textContent = "Recorded: " + payload.candidate_options.join(", ") + " ✓"; btn.classList.add("done"); }
    this._fireReport({ status: "interrogation", qtype: "guess_declaration", extra_json: JSON.stringify(payload) });
    this._renderInterrogationFeedback(); /* guess-aware feedback can now match */
  };
```

```js
  Viewer.prototype._elimChipsV2El = function (m, labels) {
    const wrap = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-elim" });

    const green = m.lands_on ? String(m.lands_on).toUpperCase() : null;

    return wrap;
  };
```

```js
  Viewer.prototype._appendSelfReportV2 = function (iq, rec) {
    const self = this;
    /* the PRIMARY method-awareness prompt (analyst handoff) */
    const srp = (rec.self_report_prompts || []).filter((p) => p.primary)[0];
    if (srp) iq.appendChild(this._promptBlockV2(srp, "method"));
    /* the PRIMARY knowledge/technique check, when present */
    const checks = ((rec.requirements || {}).post_question_checks) || [];

  Viewer.prototype._promptBlockV2 = function (p, kind) {
    const self = this;
    const box = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-prompt" });
    box.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-prompt-text" }, esc(p.prompt || "")));
    const chips = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-prompt-states" });
    (p.states || []).forEach((st) => {
      const chip = el("button", { class: "ppq-iq-state", type: "button", "data-state": st }, self._stateLabel(st));
      chip.addEventListener("click", () => {
        chips.querySelectorAll(".ppq-iq-state").forEach((c) => c.classList.remove("sel"));
        chip.classList.add("sel");
        self._promptStates[p.id] = st;
        self._fireReport({ status: "interrogation", qtype: "self_report", extra_json: JSON.stringify({ prompt_id: p.id, prompt_kind: kind, state: st, attempt_id: self._attemptId || "" }) });
        self._renderInterrogationFeedback();
      });
      chips.appendChild(chip);
    });
    box.appendChild(chips);
    return box;
  };

  Viewer.prototype._stateLabel = function (st) {
    const s = String(st || "").replace(/_/g, " ");
    return s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1);
  };
```

```js
  Viewer.prototype._verdictEl = function (rec, isV2, chosen, correctLetter, isRight) {
    const box = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-verdict" });
    let opt = null;
    if (chosen && rec.options && rec.options.length) {
      opt = rec.options.filter((o) => String(o.label).toUpperCase() === String(chosen).toUpperCase())[0] || null;
    }
    const op = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option " + (isRight ? "right" : "wrong") });
    op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-head" },
      "You chose " + esc(chosen || "?") +
      (isRight ? " — the right answer" : (correctLetter ? " — the answer is " + esc(correctLetter) : ""))));
    if (opt && opt.error_path) op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-path" }, esc(opt.error_path)));
    if (!isV2 && opt && opt.misconception_slugs && opt.misconception_slugs.length) {
      const sl = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-slugs" });
      opt.misconception_slugs.forEach((s) => sl.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-slug" }, esc(s))));
      op.appendChild(sl);
    }
    box.appendChild(op);
    return box;
  };
```
