  Viewer.prototype._renderInterrogation = function () {
    const cfg = this.cfg;
    if (!cfg.modules.postQuestionReview || !cfg.analysisOf) return;
    const rec = cfg.analysisOf(this.cur);
    if (!rec) return; /* graceful absence: most questions have no analysis yet */
    this._analysis = rec;
    this._analysisSelfReports = {};

    const self = this;
    const iq = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq" });
    iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-title" }, "What this question is really about"));

    /* --- the verdict FIRST (v0.2.5): the concrete "You picked X — the answer is Y"
       leads, ahead of the abstract probe headline. Smith's v0.2.4 point was about
       this ORDERING, never about hiding the verdict (misread, now corrected). --- */
    const chosen = this._chosenLabel;
    const correctLetter = (cfg.correctOf(this.cur) || "").toString().toUpperCase();
    if (chosen && rec.options && rec.options.length) {
      const opt = rec.options.filter((o) => String(o.label).toUpperCase() === chosen)[0];
      if (opt && opt.error_path) {
        const op = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option " + (opt.is_correct ? "right" : "wrong") });
        op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-head" }, "You picked " + esc(opt.label) + (opt.is_correct ? " — the right answer" : (correctLetter ? " — the answer is " + esc(correctLetter) : ""))));
        op.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-option-path" }, esc(opt.error_path)));
        if (opt.misconception_slugs && opt.misconception_slugs.length) {
          const sl = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-slugs" });
          opt.misconception_slugs.forEach((s) => sl.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-slug" }, esc(s))));
          op.appendChild(sl);
        }
        iq.appendChild(op);
      }
    }

    /* --- the probe (what the question is really about) --- */
    if (rec.probe && rec.probe.text) {
      const probe = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-probe" });
      probe.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-probe-text" }, esc(rec.probe.text)));
      const chips = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-chips" });
      if (rec.probe.difficulty_source) chips.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-chip" }, "difficulty: " + esc(rec.probe.difficulty_source)));
      if (rec.probe.trick_type) chips.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-chip" }, esc(rec.probe.trick_type)));
      probe.appendChild(chips);
      iq.appendChild(probe);
    }

    /* --- methods: all equal, set out line by line, each with a "used it" tick --- */
    const labels = this._optionLabels(this.cur) || [];
    if (rec.methods && rec.methods.length) {
      iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-subhead" }, "Ways through it"));
      iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-encourage" }, "Most of these have more than one route through — collecting alternatives is the point."));
      rec.methods.forEach((m) => {
        const md = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method" });
        const head = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-method-head" });
        head.appendChild(el("b", null, esc(m.id)));
        head.appendChild(el("span", { class: "ppq-iq-kind" }, esc(m.kind)));
        /* "used it" tickbox — multi-select across methods (Smith: "we just sort of
           need a little tick box to see by them, like a multi select box"). */
        const used = el("button", { class: "ppq-iq-used", type: "button" }, "used it");
        used.addEventListener("click", () => {
          const on = used.classList.toggle("on");
          const ref = m.method_ref || m.id;
          if (on) self._analysisSelfReports[ref] = "used"; else delete self._analysisSelfReports[ref];
          self._fireReport({ status: "interrogation", qtype: "self_report", extra_json: JSON.stringify({ method_id: m.id, method_ref: ref, state: on ? "used" : "not_used" }) });
          self._renderInterrogationFeedback();
        });
        head.appendChild(used);
        md.appendChild(head);
        md.appendChild(self._methodLinesEl(m.description));
        /* red = options this method kills, green = the one it lands on (Smith). */
        md.appendChild(self._elimChipsEl(m, labels, correctLetter));
        iq.appendChild(md);
      });
    }

    /* --- feedback lands here (reacts to the "used it" ticks) --- */
    iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-feedback" }));

    /* --- the 1-6 self-rating, INSIDE the pop-up (was "back outside") --- */
    const rate = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-rate" });
    rate.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-rate-prompt" }, esc(cfg.selfReport.prompt)));
    const scale = el("div", { class: "ppq-scale ppq-iq-scale" });
    const meanings = cfg.selfReport.meanings || [];
    for (let v = 1; v <= cfg.selfReport.levels; v++) {
      const lbl = cfg.selfReport.labels ? cfg.selfReport.labels[v - 1] : String(v);
      const meaning = meanings[v - 1] || "";
      scale.appendChild(el("button", { class: "ppq-scale-btn ppq-iq-scale-btn", "data-val": String(v), title: meaning ? (v + " — " + meaning) : "" }, esc(lbl)));
    }
    rate.appendChild(scale);
    if (meanings.length) {
      rate.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-scale-legend" }, meanings.map(function (mm, i) { return '<span class="ppq-scale-legend-item"><b>' + (i + 1) + "</b> " + esc(mm) + "</span>"; }).join("")));
    }
    const prior = this.store.scores[cfg.idOf(this.cur)];
    if (prior) { const sb = scale.querySelector('.ppq-iq-scale-btn[data-val="' + prior + '"]'); if (sb) sb.classList.add("sel"); }
    const iqNext = el("button", { class: "ppq-btn ppq-primary ppq-iq-next", type: "button", style: "display:none;" }, "Next question →");
    iqNext.addEventListener("click", () => { self.closeModal(); self.next(); });
    scale.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
      const b = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest(".ppq-iq-scale-btn") : null;
      if (!b) return;
      const val = parseInt(b.dataset.val, 10);
      scale.querySelectorAll(".ppq-iq-scale-btn").forEach((x) => x.classList.remove("sel"));
      b.classList.add("sel");
      if (self.cur) {
        self.store.scores[self.cfg.idOf(self.cur)] = val; self._saveStore();
        self._fireReport({ status: "rated", qtype: "self_report", extra_json: JSON.stringify({ rating: val }) });
      }
      iqNext.style.display = "inline-block"; iqNext.focus();
    });
    rate.appendChild(iqNext);
    iq.appendChild(rate);

    /* --- optional "come back to this" flag (Smith: review / more like this) --- */
    const flag = el("button", { class: "ppq-iq-flag" }, "Flag this — come back / more like this");
    flag.addEventListener("click", () => {
      flag.classList.toggle("on");
      const on = flag.classList.contains("on");
      flag.textContent = on ? "Flagged ✓ — we'll bring more like this" : "Flag this — come back / more like this";
      self._fireReport({ status: "flag_review", qtype: "review_flag", extra_json: JSON.stringify({ flagged: on }) });
    });
    iq.appendChild(flag);

    /* --- mount into the modal shell and open the pop-up. While it holds the 1-6,
       the outer 1-6 row is hidden; closeModal restores it if they bail early. --- */
    const body = this.q(".ppq-modal-body");
    body.innerHTML = "";
    body.appendChild(iq);
    this.q(".ppq-modal").classList.add("show");
    this._iqBox = iq;
    this._iqOpen = true;
    this.q(".ppq-competence").style.display = "none";
  };

    const cfg = this.cfg;
    if (!cfg.modules.postQuestionReview || !cfg.analysisOf) return;

    if (!rec) return; /* graceful absence: most questions have no analysis yet */

    this._promptStates = {};
    this._postGuessDeclared = false;

    const self = this;
    const isV2 = this._isV2(rec);
    const iq = el("div", { class: "ppq-iq" });

    const chosen = this._chosenLabel;
    const correctLetter = isV2
      ? String((rec.identity && rec.identity.correct_answer) || "").toUpperCase()
      : (cfg.correctOf(this.cur) || "").toString().toUpperCase();

    /* --- 1. the verdict FIRST and ALWAYS (analyst handoff): the concrete
       "You chose X — the answer is Y" leads. The error_path explanation beneath
       it is optional; the verdict line itself is not. The old abstract
       "What this question is really about" headline no longer precedes it. --- */
    iq.appendChild(this._verdictEl(rec, isV2, chosen, correctLetter, this._wasRight));

    /* --- 2. post-answer guess correction (optional, non-blocking). Sits right
       after the verdict so a guess is on record BEFORE guess-aware feedback is
       matched. Replaces the outer "Actually, I wasn't sure" control. --- */
    iq.appendChild(this._postGuessEl(chosen, this._wasRight));

    if (isV2) {
      /* --- 3. the pupil insight (first_notice / why_it_matters / next_move) --- */
      this._appendInsightV2(iq, rec);
      /* --- 4. methods: title + structured pupil_steps + elimination chips --- */
      this._appendMethodsV2(iq, rec);
      /* --- 5. primary self-report + knowledge check (feed the feedback match) --- */
      this._appendSelfReportV2(iq, rec);
    } else {
      /* legacy analysis-store path: probe + free-prose methods */
      this._appendProbeLegacy(iq, rec);
      this._appendMethodsLegacy(iq, rec, correctLetter);

    /* --- feedback lands here (reacts to the self-report + guess declaration) --- */
    iq.appendChild(el("div", { class: "ppq-iq-feedback" }));

    /* --- 6. the 1-6 self-rating, INSIDE the pop-up (was "back outside") --- */

The v2 lookup should be `q.slug + "_Q" + nn` (2 digits). But wait — the v2 record's identity has `part: "A"`. Is it possible for the catalogue to have multiple parts (A, B) for the same question number? In ESAT MCQ, each question is a single MCQ, so part is probably always "A" or empty. But the v2 ID doesn't include part, so if there were two parts with the same number, they'd collide. Actually, to be safe, let me first try with a part suffix (in case some IDs have parts), then fall back to without a suffix. But from the grep results, there are no IDs with part suffixes. Let's just use `slug + "_Q" + nn`. Actually, let's mirror the robustness of the legacy function: first try `base + "_" + q.part`, then try `base`. For v2, we'll check `V2.by_id[base + "_" + q.part]`, then `V2.by_id[base]`. That way we handle both.

Now, the new `analysisOf` should prioritize v2:
```js
function analysisOf(q) {
  if (!q || !q.slug) return null;
  var nn = String(parseInt(q.question_number, 10));
  nn = nn.length < 2 ? "0" + nn : nn;
  var base = q.slug + "_Q" + nn;
  /* QoderWork 2026-07-22 (analyst handoff): prefer the analysis-v2 record when
     present; fall back to the legacy analysis store for questions not yet
     migrated; otherwise null (plain viewer). */
  var V2 = window.ESAT_ANALYSIS_V2;
  if (V2 && V2.by_id) {
    if (q.part && V2.by_id[base + "_" + q.part]) return V2.by_id[base + "_" + q.part];
    if (V2.by_id[base]) return V2.by_id[base];
  }
  if (q.part && ANALYSIS[base + "_" + q.part]) return ANALYSIS[base + "_" + q.part];
  return ANALYSIS[base] || null;
}
```

# CHANGELOG: ppqviewer

Universal engine changes are recorded here and notified into each consumer's inbox. Newest at the top.

## 2026-07-22 (QoderWork, latest) — analyst handoff: guess semantics repaired, verdict literally first, analysis-v2 consumed (v0.2.7)
Integration pass implementing the categorisation analysts' "Handoff to the ppqviewer implementer". This is NOT a rewrite — the functioning viewer, filtering, timer, reporting, modal, plain-question fallback and non-ESAT consumers are all preserved. chem-compare is untouched (every change is opt-in config).

### Settled guess-declaration semantics (now implemented)
- One declaration offered at BOTH stages: pre-answer ("I'm guessing") and post-answer ("Actually, it was a guess"). A guess is any set from 2 up to every option — not a special "guess between two".
- Percentages are OPTIONAL, behind an "Add percentages (optional)" toggle. Equal splitting is only a starting value once that toggle is chosen; a pupil can record just the candidate set.
- After answering, the chosen option stays IN the picker and starts PRESELECTED (it is no longer removed).
- Both stages fire `qtype:"guess_declaration"` with one payload shape in `extra_json`: `{guess_declared:true, declared_stage:"pre_answer"|"post_answer", candidate_options:[...], attempt_id:"...", candidate_percentages?}`. The post-answer event additionally carries `chosen_option` and `correct`. The legacy `qtype:"unsure"` and its `declared/wavering` payloads are superseded.
- Every displayed attempt gets a stable `attempt_id`; the answer event and the stored attempt carry it plus any pre-answer declaration snapshot, so repeated attempts at one question stay distinguishable.
- `Done` no longer silently closes on <2 options — the panel stays open with an inline validation message. No event fires for an empty post-answer selection.

### Two bugs fixed
- `_shouldHandleKey` now ignores `INPUT`/`SELECT`/`TEXTAREA`/content-editable targets, so typing "10", "50" or "80" into a percentage box never commits answer A/E/H.
- Percentage redistribution uses a largest-remainder allocation (`allocateLargestRemainder`) — every value is a non-negative integer and the total is exactly 100 (the old proportional pass could drive the final option negative).

### Modal order — the verdict is now literally first
The pop-up order is: (1) concrete verdict "You chose B — the answer is D", ALWAYS rendered even when the chosen option has an empty `error_path` (the explanation is optional, the verdict is not); (2) the optional post-answer guess correction; (3) the pupil insight; (4) methods + structured eliminations; (5) the primary self-report/knowledge check + matched feedback; (6) the 1-6 rating + Next. The old "What this question is really about" headline no longer precedes the verdict. The outer "Actually, I wasn't sure" control is superseded (hidden, DOM retained) — the correction now sits inside the modal where guess-aware feedback can see it.

### Analysis-v2 consumption (with old-data fallback)
- The engine detects a v2 record by its `identity` + `pupil_analysis` blocks and renders its fields DIRECTLY: insight (`first_notice`/`why_it_matters`/`next_move`), chosen-option `error_path`, method `title` + `pupil_steps`, red chips from `methods[].eliminates`, green chip from `methods[].lands_on`, the primary `self_report_prompts[]` item, the primary `requirements.post_question_checks[]` item, and structured feedback on `selected_options`/`prompt_id`/`states`/`guess_declared`.
- NO regex parsing of v2 steps or eliminations (the `_methodLinesEl`/`_elimChipsEl` stopgaps are legacy-only now). Internal taxonomy is hidden from pupils: `error_tags`, category paths, mechanism codes, diagnostic confidence, difficulty chips, strategy tags.
- Feedback matching for v2 is first-match-wins over the array, on the structured constraints; a `guess_declared:true` entry only fires once a guess is on record. The per-method "used it" tickbox stays as supplementary evidence (it does not drive v2 feedback).
- `esat-compare.html` loads the generated bundle (`window.ESAT_ANALYSIS_V2`), `analysisOf` prefers `by_id` and falls back to the legacy analysis store for unmigrated questions, and `guessDefaults` is sourced from `interaction_defaults.guess_declaration`. Questions with no analysis of either kind remain the plain viewer.

### Content ownership
The viewer renders the analysts' v2 pupil prose faithfully (escaped, laid out) and does NOT rewrite it — no JS cleanup layer for praise/jargon/tone. The viewer owns only generic chrome: "I'm guessing", "Actually, it was a guess", validation messages, headings, buttons, and the humanised state-chip labels.

---

class FakeEl {

    this.tagName = String(tag||"").toUpperCase();
    this.children = [];
    this.parentNode = null;

    this.style = { cssText: "", display: "", setProperty(){} };

Let's implement style like this:
```js
function makeStyle() {
  var props = {};
  return {
    get cssText() { return Object.keys(props).map(k=>k+":"+props[k]+";").join(""); },
    set cssText(v) {
      props = {};
      String(v||"").split(";").forEach(function(pair){ var i=pair.indexOf(":"); if(i>0){ var k=pair.slice(0,i).trim(), val=pair.slice(i+1).trim(); if(k) props[k]=val; } });
    },
    // dynamic props
  };
}
```
But dynamic property get/set (style.display) needs a Proxy. Let's use a Proxy:
```js
function makeStyle() {
  var store = {};
  return new Proxy(store, {
    get: function(t, k){ if(k==="cssText"){ return Object.keys(t).map(function(p){return p+":"+t[p]+";";}).join(""); } return t[k]||""; },
    set: function(t, k, v){ if(k==="cssText"){ // parse
        Object.keys(t).forEach(function(p){delete t[p];});
        String(v||"").split(";").forEach(function(pair){ var i=pair.indexOf(":"); if(i>0){ var kk=pair.slice(0,i).trim(), vv=pair.slice(i+1).trim(); if(kk) t[kk]=vv; } });
        return true; } t[k]=v; return true; }
  });
}
```
This handles both cssText parsing and individual property access. Good.

```js
var VOID_TAGS = { br:1, img:1, input:1, hr:1, meta:1, link:1, col:1, area:1, base:1, embed:1, param:1, source:1, track:1, wbr:1 };
function parseHTML(str, doc) {
  var roots = [];
  var stack = [];
  var i = 0;
  var tagRe = /<!--[\s\S]*?-->|<\/\s*([a-zA-Z0-9-]+)\s*>|<([a-zA-Z0-9-]+)((?:\s+[^<>]*?)?)\/?>/g;
  var last = 0;
  var m;
  function top() { return stack.length ? stack[stack.length-1] : null; }
  function add(node) { var p = top(); if (p) p.appendChild(node); else roots.push(node); }
  while ((m = tagRe.exec(str)) !== null) {
    if (m.index > last) {
      var txt = str.slice(last, m.index);
      if (txt.trim() !== "" || txt !== "") {
        var t = new FakeEl("#text"); t.data = decodeEntities(txt); add(t);
      }
    }
    last = tagRe.lastIndex;
    if (m[0].slice(0,4) === "<!--") continue;
    if (m[1]) { // closing tag
      // pop until matching
      for (var s = stack.length-1; s >= 0; s--) {
        if (stack[s].tagName.toLowerCase() === m[1].toLowerCase()) { stack.length = s; break; }
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (m[2]) { // opening tag
      var elx = new FakeEl(m[2]);
      parseAttrs(m[3] || "", elx);
      add(elx);
      var selfClosed = /\/\s*>$/.test(m[0]);
      if (!selfClosed && !VOID_TAGS[m[2].toLowerCase()]) stack.push(elx);

Now I have a full picture of the timer:

**What esat-compare sets up:**
- `timingMode: "none"` (line 214) — this is the old/legacy timing knob, set to none.
- `timer: { mode: "up", prominence: "subtle" }` (line 277) — the new exam timer module, count-up, subtle display.

**What the engine provides (all no-ops unless config.timer is set):**
- `_startTimer` / `_stopTimer` / `_tickTimer` / `_commitTimer`
- Count-up mode (mode:"up") — counts up from 0.
- Count-down mode (mode:"down", presumably) — with time banking and time-pressure context (forced/tight/ok based on `pressureSec`).
- On commit, stores `_timerCtx` with `time_remaining_ms` and `time_pressure`, and attaches it to the attempt's `extra_json` (lines 1053–1055). This lets fast answers be distinguished from guesses under time pressure.
- The timer display element `.ppq-timer` is added hidden unless the module is enabled and prominence isn't "hidden".

So the timer situation is:
- The count-up timer is wired into esat-compare and working (mode:"up", prominence:"subtle"). It counts up from 0 while the question is displayed, and freezes when answered.
- The engine additionally has a full count-down mode with time banking and time-pressure tagging, but esat-compare doesn't use it (it uses count-up). The count-down mode and time-pressure context are available if Smith wants per-question time limits.
- The time data (time_ms, and time_remaining_ms/time_pressure in count-down mode) is captured into the attempt's extra_json.

#### Thinking

Now I have a full picture of the timer:

**Count-up mode (what esat-compare uses):**
- `mode: "up"` — counts up from 0:00 while the question is displayed (`tel.textContent = this._fmtClock(elapsed)`).
- `prominence: "subtle"` — shown with subtle styling (the class `ppq-timer--subtle`).
- On answer (`_commitTimer`), captures `ctx = { time_ms: elapsed }` — the raw elapsed time. This gets appended to the attempt's `extra_json`.
- No time-pressure context in count-up mode (that's count-down only).

**Count-down mode (available in the engine but not used by esat-compare):**
- `mode: "down"` — counts down from a per-question budget (`perQuestionSec`), with `pressureSec` for the "tight" threshold.
- Captures `time_remaining_ms` and `time_pressure` ("forced"/"tight"/"ok").
- Supports time banking (`t.banking`) — saved time carries over.
- Visual state: `--forced` (red, out of time), `--tight` (near the threshold).

**What gets reported:** In count-up mode, `time_ms` (elapsed time) is captured into `_timerCtx` and appended to the attempt's extra_json (lines 1053–1055 only append time_remaining_ms/time_pressure if present, and time_ms is probably appended elsewhere). 3	Universal engine changes are recorded here and notified into each consumer's inbox. Newest at the top.
4	
5	## 2026-07-22 (QoderWork, latest) — analyst handoff: guess semantics repaired, verdict literally first, analysis-v2 consumed (v0.2.7)
6	Integration pass implementing the categorisation analysts' "Handoff to the ppqviewer implementer". This is NOT a rewrite — the functioning viewer, filtering, timer, reporting, modal, plain-question fallback and non-ESAT consumers are all preserved. chem-compare is untouched (every change is opt-in config).
7	
8	### Settled guess-declaration semantics (now implemented)
9	- One declaration offered at BOTH stages: pre-answer ("I'm guessing") and post-answer ("Actually, it was a guess"). A guess is any set from 2 up to every option — not a special "guess between two".
10	- Percentages are OPTIONAL, behind an "Add percentages (optional)" toggle. Equal splitting is only a starting value once that toggle is chosen; a pupil can record just the candidate set.
11	- After answering, the chosen option stays IN the picker and starts PRESELECTED (it is no longer removed).
12	- Both stages fire `qtype:"guess_declaration"` with one payload shape in `extra_json`: `{guess_declared:true, declared_stage:"pre_answer"|"post_answer", candidate_options:[...], attempt_id:"...", candidate_percentages?}`. The post-answer event additionally carries `chosen_option` and `correct`. The legacy `qtype:"unsure"` and its `declared/wavering` payloads are superseded.
13	- Every displayed attempt gets a stable `attempt_id`; the answer event and the stored attempt carry it plus any pre-answer declaration snapshot, so repeated attempts at one question stay distinguishable.
14	- `Done` no longer silently closes on <2 options — the panel stays open with an inline validation message. No event fires for an empty post-answer selection.
15	
16	### Two bugs fixed
17	- `_shouldHandleKey` now ignores `INPUT`/`SELECT`/`TEXTAREA`/content-editable targets, so typing "10", "50" or "80" into a percentage box never commits answer A/E/H.
18	- Percentage redistribution uses a largest-remainder allocation (`allocateLargestRemainder`) — every value is a non-negative integer and the total is exactly 100 (the old proportional pass could drive the final option negative).
19	
20	### Modal order — the verdict is now literally first
21	The pop-up order is: (1) concrete verdict "You chose B — the answer is D", ALWAYS rendered even when the chosen option has an empty `error_path` (the explanation is optional, the verdict is not); (2) the optional post-answer guess correction; (3) the pupil insight; (4) methods + structured eliminations; (5) the primary self-report/knowledge check + matched feedback; (6) the 1-6 rating + Next. The old "What this question is really about" headline no longer precedes the verdict. The outer "Actually, I wasn't sure" control is superseded (hidden, DOM retained) — the correction now sits inside the modal where guess-aware feedback can see it.
22	
23	### Analysis-v2 consumption (with old-data fallback)
24	- The engine detects a v2 record by its `identity` + `pupil_analysis` blocks and renders its fields DIRECTLY: insight (`first_notice`/`why_it_matters`/`next_move`), chosen-option `error_path`, method `title` + `pupil_steps`, red chips from `methods[].eliminates`, green chip from `methods[].lands_on`, the primary `self_report_prompts[]` item, the primary `requirements.post_question_checks[]` item, and structured feedback on `selected_options`/`prompt_id`/`states`/`guess_declared`.
25	- NO regex parsing of v2 steps or eliminations (the `_methodLinesEl`/`_elimChipsEl` stopgaps are legacy-only now). Internal taxonomy is hidden from pupils: `error_tags`, category paths, mechanism codes, diagnostic confidence, difficulty chips, strategy tags.
26	- Feedback matching for v2 is first-match-wins over the array, on the structured constraints; a `guess_declared:true` entry only fires once a guess is on record. The per-method "used it" tickbox stays as supplementary evidence (it does not drive v2 feedback).
27	- `esat-compare.html` loads the generated bundle (`window.ESAT_ANALYSIS_V2`), `analysisOf` prefers `by_id` and falls back to the legacy analysis store for unmigrated questions, and `guessDefaults` is sourced from `interaction_defaults.guess_declaration`. Questions with no analysis of either kind remain the plain viewer.
28	
29	### Content ownership
30	The viewer renders the analysts' v2 pupil prose faithfully (escaped, laid out) and does NOT rewrite it — no JS cleanup layer for praise/jargon/tone. The viewer owns only generic chrome: "I'm guessing", "Actually, it was a guess", validation messages, headings, buttons, and the humanised state-chip labels.

34	## 2026-07-22 (QoderWork) — pre-declare guesses (v0.2.6)
35	Smith's decision: "I think we just go with pre, actually." Pupils can optionally declare which options they're guessing between BEFORE locking in their answer — more honest data than post-declare (which is also still available as "Actually, I wasn't sure").
36	
37	### How it works
38	- A small "Declare guesses?" button sits above the answer row, visible while the question is on screen. Entirely optional — if they just answer, nothing is recorded.
39	- Clicking it opens a panel: one checkbox per option letter. Tick 2+ to engage.
40	- Percentages auto-distribute equally (2 ticks = 50/50, 3 = 34/33/33). Each ticked option gets a number input; typing a bigger number proportionally decreases the others. Total always sums to 100.

### Fixes found in verification (this session)
- ENGINE BUG: the interrogation modal never populated its feedback region on first open — feedback only appeared after a guess was committed or a self-report state was tapped. So entries that match with no guess and no prompt state (v2 `selected_options`-only, legacy `any_wrong`/`any_correct`) were invisible on a plain answer. `_renderInterrogation` now calls `_renderInterrogationFeedback()` once the modal is mounted (it still re-renders on guess/prompt interaction). Caught by the headless test.
- esat-compare SIGN-IN GATE: if `ppq-login.js` failed to load (e.g. a tester opened the file without its folder), the inline script threw at `window.PPQLogin.createLogin` BEFORE the class dropdown was populated — leaving it blank and Start dead, so testers could not get in. The dropdown is now populated FIRST and unconditionally; the estate login is optional with a minimal local fallback gate (name remembered locally, no pulse); and `enterApp` shows a plain "the viewer engine did not load — open from inside the ppqviewer folder" message instead of failing silently if the engine itself is absent.

You want a proper options screen — not one clock but a choice of how it shows: off, a plain number, a single sweeping hand (stopwatch-like, one turn per question), or an ever-increasing pie, with the hand and pie each able to show a number in the middle or not.

At 89 seconds three things are independently switchable: it can go off (a gentle flash, not a siren), it can run into overtime as negative red time, and that overtime can disappear the moment an answer is locked.

While they're categorising — the post-question pop-up with the self-report and methods — the clock pauses, because thinking about the question shouldn't burn their 89 seconds. That paused time is simply ignored (or noted separately if you'd rather).

The time bank shows ahead/behind. Finish in 30s and you're +59s in the bank; take 120s and you owe −31s. You sketched two ways to show it and I've built both: a bar next to the clock whose size is the spare or the hole, or the bank divided by the questions remaining so it reads as "+2.2s per question" — which is calmer than a raw total. The bank is there to be cleared, not to punish.

And any single question can be flagged "don't time this one" with a short reason — a interruption, a mis-read — so its time is left out of the bank and the average while the attempt itself is still recorded.

My top three, badged in the mockup: Off while they're learning which questions matter and whether they can solve them; the filling pie with a centre number as the gentlest paced option once speed becomes the goal; and the plain number as the no-frills pace clock. That matches your "off to start, turn it on occasionally later."

Two things I'd like you to settle when you've had a look: whether the bank should offer both displays as a choice or ship with just one, and whether 89 seconds is the firm number or you want it editable per paper. Everything here sits behind the viewer's existing config — the working viewer and the current count-up timer stay exactly as they are until you pick the faces and switches you like, and then I'll wire precisely those into the engine.
